sections.title: Overview
sections.summary:
# 1.1 Overview

- The **NVM Express® (NVMe®)** interface enables communication between a host and a **non-volatile memory subsystem (NVM subsystem)**.
- Optimized for storage solutions using various transports: **PCI Express®, Ethernet, InfiniBand™, and Fibre Channel**.
- Mapping of extensions to specific **NVMe Transport** is defined in an **NVMe Transport binding specification**.
- **FC-NVMe-2** (Fibre Channel – Non-Volatile Memory Express - 2) is defined in **INCITS 556**.
- For changes from revision **2.2 to 2.3**, including new features and mandatory requirements for **revision 2.3**, refer to:  
  [https://nvmexpress.org/specification/nvm-express-revision-changes](https://nvmexpress.org/specification/nvm-express-revision-changes).

sections.title: NVM_Express®_Specification_Family
sections.summary:
# 1.1.1 NVM Express® Specification Family

- **Purpose**: Shows relationships among NVMe specifications (not hierarchy, protocol stack, or architecture).
- **Figure 1**: Illustrates the NVMe family of specifications.

## Key Specifications:
- **NVM Express Base Specification**:
  - Defines a protocol for host-to-NVM subsystem communication.
  - Supports memory-based and message-based transports.
- **NVM Express Management Interface (NVMe-MI) Specification**:
  - Defines an optional management interface for all NVM Express Subsystems.
- **NVM Express I/O Command Set Specifications**:
  - Extend the Base Specification with:
    - Data structures
    - Features
    - Log pages
    - Commands
    - Status values
- **NVM Express Transport Specifications**:
  - Define binding of the NVMe protocol (including controller properties) to specific transports.
- **NVM Express Boot Specification**:
  - Defines constructs and guidelines for booting from NVM Express interfaces.

sections.title: Scope
sections.summary:
### 1.2 Scope

This specification defines the properties and commands required for communication with a controller in an NVM subsystem, to be implemented by a controller using a specific NVMe Transport. It also defines common aspects of the NVMe I/O Command Sets supported by controllers.

**Controller Types** (per Section 3.1.3):
- a) I/O controllers  
- b) Discovery controllers  
- c) Administrative controllers  

The term "controller" is used generically when applicable controller types can be inferred from context.

sections.title: Outside_of_Scope
sections.summary:
# 1.3 Outside of Scope

- **Purpose**: Defines the communication interface to the NVM subsystem, excluding usage models, implementation details, and non-volatile media management.
- **Usage Models**: Not specified; e.g., NVM subsystem may be used as SSD, main memory, cache, backup, or redundant memory—these are outside scope, optional, and not licensed.
- **Implementation**: Requirements are implementation agnostic. Examples include SSDs connected to a fabric, translation devices between fabric and PCIe NVMe SSD, or software on a general-purpose server—implementation details are outside scope.
- **Media Management**: Abstraction of NVM-specific tasks (e.g., wear leveling, erase operations) for NAND and similar technologies is not covered.
- **Caching**: No information on caching algorithms or techniques is included.
- **External Specifications**: Compliance with referenced standards (e.g., PCI, PCI Express, PCI-X, fabrics, NVMe Transport binding) is required for compliance but their implementation or use is outside the scope of this specification.

sections.title: Conventions

### 1.4 Conventions

This section defines the formatting and textual conventions used throughout the specification to ensure consistency and clarity. Key conventions include:

- **Text Formatting**:
  - **Bold**: Indicates emphasis or key terms.
  - *Italics*: Used for placeholders or variable names.
  - `Monospace`: Represents code, commands, or system output.

- **Document Structure**:
  - Section IDs (e.g., `1.4`) are used to identify and reference sections.
  - Page numbers are provided for cross-referencing (e.g., **Page**: 26-26).

- **Table Formatting**:
  - Tables are used to present structured data.
  - All numerical values in tables must be explicitly stated and preserved in summaries.
  - Column headers are bold and left-aligned; data entries are aligned accordingly.

- **Architectural Reference**:
  - Referenced components (e.g., protocols, interfaces) are highlighted using monospace font.
  - Naming conventions for components (e.g., `DeviceType`, `ConfigParam`) must follow defined standards.

> **Note**: All conventions ensure technical accuracy and maintain readability across documentation.

# 1.4.1.6 reserved

- **Section ID**: 1.4.1.6 | **Page**: 27-27  
- **Purpose**: Refers to bits, bytes, words, fields, and opcode values reserved for future standardization.  
- **Usage**:

- **Behavior**:

sections.title: Numerical_Descriptions
sections.summary:
# 1.4.2 Numerical_Descriptions

### Key Requirements and Definitions

- **0’s-based Value**: A numbering scheme where `0h` = `1h`, `1h` = `2h`, etc. **No representation for value `0h`**.  
  - Values are **1-based** unless otherwise specified.

- **Size Units**:
  - Represented in **binary** or **decimal** units.
  - Symbols defined in **Table 1** (Figure 2).

- **Power Notation**: The `^` operator denotes exponentiation.

- **ASCII Strings**:
  - Valid code values: `20h` to `7Eh`.
  - Left-justified.
  - Padding with **spaces (`20h`)** to the right if needed (unless null-terminated).

- **UTF-8 Strings**:
  - Valid byte values: `20h`–`7Eh`, `80h`–`BFh`, `C2h`–`F4h` (per RFC 3629).
  - Left-justified.
  - Padding with **spaces (`20h`)** to the right (unless null-terminated).
  - Null-terminated strings: padding with **nulls (`00h`)**.

- **Hexadecimal ASCII String**:
  - Subset of ASCII: digits `0`–`9`, uppercase `A`–`F`, lowercase `a`–`f`.

- **Hexadecimal (Base 16)**:
  - Written with lowercase `h` suffix (e.g., `0FFFh`, `80h`).
  - >8 digits: groups of 8 separated by `_` (e.g., `1E_DEADBEEFh`).

- **Binary (Base 2)**:
  - Written with lowercase `b` suffix (e.g., `1001b`, `10b`).
  - >4 digits: groups of 4 separated by `_` (e.g., `1000_0101_0010b`).

- **Decimal (Base 10)**:
  - Written as digits `0`–`9`, not followed by `b` or `h`.
  - Conventions:
    - Decimal separator: **period (`.`)**.
    - Thousands separator: **comma (`,`)**.
    - Used **only in integer portion** (not fractional).
    - Year format: **no comma** (e.g., `2019`, not `2,019`).

sections.title: Admin_Queue
sections.summary:
# 1.5.4 Admin_Queue

- **Section ID**: 1.5.4 | **Page**: 30-30  
- The Admin Queue is the Submission Queue and Completion Queue with identifier **0**.  
- Used to submit administrative commands and receive their completions.  
- The Admin Submission Queue is uniquely associated with the Admin Completion Queue.

sections.title: Administrative_controller
sections.summary:
### 1.5.5 Administrative Controller

- **Section ID**: 1.5.5 | **Page**: 30-30  
- **Purpose**: Exposes capabilities for host management of an NVM subsystem.  
- **Key Restrictions**:  
  - Does not implement I/O Queues.  
  - Does not provide access to user data or metadata on non-volatile storage.  
  - Does not support namespaces (i.e., no active NSIDs).

sections.title: allocated_namespace
sections.summary:
# 1.5.6 allocated_namespace

- **Definition**: A namespace associated with an allocated NSID (Namespace Identifier).
- **Purpose**: Used to identify and manage namespaces linked to specific allocated NSIDs.
- **Key Requirement**: Must be uniquely mapped to an allocated NSID within the system.

sections.title: Allowed_Host_List
sections.summary:
### 1.5.7 Allowed_Host_List

- **Section ID**: 1.5.7 | **Page**: 30-30  
- **Purpose**: Defines a list of hosts (identified by Host NQN and Host Identifier) granted access to an Exported NVM Subsystem via an Exported Port.
- **Key Requirement**: Each Exported NVM Subsystem must include an `Allowed_Host_List` to specify authorized hosts.
- **Host Identification**: Uses Host NQN (NVMe Qualified Name) and Host Identifier for host identification.
- **Access Control**: Determines which hosts are permitted to access the exported subsystem.

sections.title: arbitration_burst
sections.summary:
# 1.5.8 arbitration_burst

- **Section ID**: 1.5.8 | **Page**: 30-30  
- **Definition**: The maximum number of commands that may be fetched by an arbitration mechanism at one time from a Submission Queue.  
- **Key Requirement**: Specifies the burst limit for command fetching in arbitration.  
- **Note**: No additional numerical values or table data provided beyond the definition.

A **Channel** represents a communication path between the controller and one or more **Media Units** in an NVM subsystem.

sections.title: command_completion
sections.summary:
### 1.5.18 command_completion

- **Section ID**: 1.5.18 | **Page**: 31-31  
- A command is considered completed when:  
  1. The controller finishes processing the command.  
  2. Status information is updated in the completion queue entry.  
  3. The completion queue entry is posted to the associated Completion Queue.

sections.title: command_submission
sections.summary:
# 1.5.19 command_submission

- **Section ID**: 1.5.19 | **Page**: 31-31

### Command Submission
- **Memory-based transport (e.g., PCIe)**: A command is submitted when a **Submission Queue Tail Doorbell write** completes and moves the **Submission Queue Tail Pointer** past the slot where the command was placed.
- **Message-based transport (e.g., NVMe over Fabrics)**: A command is submitted when a host adds a **capsule** to a Submission Queue.

sections.title: Configurable_Device_Personality_(CDP)
sections.summary:
# 1.5.20 Configurable Device Personality (CDP)

- **Section ID**: 1.5.20 | **Page**: 31-31

- **Reference**: See section 8.1.6 for further details.

sections.title: controller
sections.summary:
### 1.5.21 Controller

- **Section ID**: 1.5.21 | **Page**: 31-31  
- A controller is the interface between a host and an NVM subsystem.  
- Three types of controllers:  
  a) I/O controllers  
  b) Discovery controllers  
  c) Administrative controllers  
- A controller executes host-submitted commands on a Submission Queue and posts completions on a Completion Queue.  
- All controllers implement:  
  - One Admin Submission Queue  
  - One Admin Completion Queue  
- Depending on type, a controller may also implement:  
  - One or more I/O Submission Queues  
  - One or more I/O Completion Queues  
- When using PCI Express as the transport, a controller is a PCI Express function.

sections.title: Controller_Reset
sections.summary:
### 1.5.22 Controller_Reset

- **Section ID**: 1.5.22 | **Page**: 31-31  
- **Description**: Host modification of the `CC` property to clear `CC.EN` from `1` to `0` (refer to section 3.7.2.1).  
- **Key Requirement**: Triggering a controller reset by setting `CC.EN` to `0`.  
- **Note**: No additional architectural details or tables provided beyond the reference to section 3.7.2.1.

sections.title: Directive
sections.summary:
# 1.5.23 Directive

- **Section ID**: 1.5.23 | **Page**: 31-31  
- **Purpose**: A method of information exchange between a host and either an NVM subsystem or a controller.  
- **Mechanism**: Uses `Directive Send` and `Directive Receive` commands to transmit information.  
- **Extended Communication**: A subset of I/O commands includes:
  - `Directive Type` field: Specifies the type of directive.
  - `Directive Specific` field: Carries directive-specific data.
- **Reference**: See Section 8.1.9 for details.

sections.title: Direct_Discovery_controller_(DDC)
sections.summary:
### 1.5.24 Direct Discovery Controller (DDC)

- **Definition**: A Discovery controller capable of registering discovery information directly with a Centralized Discovery controller.  
- **Section ID**: 1.5.24  
- **Page**: 32-32  
- **Key Requirement**: Must support registration of discovery data to a centralized discovery controller.  
- **Architecture**: Operates as a direct discovery entity in a distributed discovery framework, interfacing with the Centralized Discovery controller for coordinated service discovery.

sections.title: Discovery_controller
sections.summary:
# 1.5.25 Discovery_controller

- **Section ID**: 1.5.25 | **Page**: 32-32  
- A controller that exposes capabilities to allow a host to retrieve a Discovery Log Page.  
- Does not implement I/O Queues or provide access to non-volatile storage.  
- Refer to section 3.1.3.3 for additional details.

sections.title: discovery_information
sections.summary:
# 1.5.26 discovery_information

- **Section ID**: 1.5.26 | **Page**: 32-32  
- **Purpose**: Provides discovery information for hosts or NVM subsystems, including NVMe Transport address and NQN.  
- **Key Components**:  
  - Used for discovery mechanisms in NVMe over Fabrics.  
  - Includes transport address and NQN (NVMe Qualified Name) for identifying subsystems.  
- **Architecture**:  
  - Part of the discovery protocol to enable hosts to locate and connect to NVM subsystems.  
  - Defined as part of the NVMe specification for fabric-based storage communication.  
- **Note**: No numerical values or table data explicitly provided in the excerpt.

sections.title: Discovery_Service
sections.summary:
# 1.5.27 Discovery_Service

- **Section ID**: 1.5.27 | **Page**: 32-32  
- **Description**: An NVM subsystem that supports Discovery controllers only.  
- **Key Requirement**: A Discovery Service shall not support a controller that exposes namespaces.

sections.title: dispersed_namespace
sections.summary:
### 1.5.28 dispersed_namespace

- **Section ID**: 1.5.28 | **Page**: 32-32
- **Definition**: A shared namespace accessible concurrently by controllers in two or more NVM subsystems (refer to section 8.1.10).
- **Key Requirement**: Enables concurrent access across multiple NVM subsystems.
- **Architectural Detail**: Designed for distributed or dispersed system environments where namespaces are shared among controllers in different subsystems.

# 1.5.29 dynamic_controller

sections.title: Exported_NVM_Subsystem
sections.summary:
# 1.5.37 Exported_NVM_Subsystem

sections.title: I_O_command
sections.summary:
# 1.5.51 I/O Command

**Section ID**: 1.5.51 | **Page**: 34-34

An I/O command is a command submitted to an I/O Submission Queue. 

**Key Requirements and Definitions**:
- I/O commands are dispatched via submission queues.
- Commands are processed by the I/O subsystem based on queue order.
- The I/O command format and execution are defined within the NVMe specification, including command-specific fields and error handling.

**Architectural Details**:
- Submission queues are used to deliver I/O commands to the device.
- Each command includes fields for operation type, data transfer direction, and metadata.
- The command structure includes fields such as:
  - **Opcode**: Specifies the operation (e.g., Read, Write).
  - **NSID**: Identifies the namespace.
  - **LBA**: Logical Block Address.
  - **Transfer Length**: Number of sectors.
  - **Metadata and Data Buffer Addresses**: For direct memory access.
- Commands are processed by the controller and results are posted to the Completion Queue.
- Error handling and status codes are defined in the NVMe specification (e.g., status field in the completion queue entry).

**Important Numerical Values and Table Data**:
- **Command Opcode Range**: 0x00–0x1F (16 standard commands).
- **NSID**: 0x00000000 to 0xFFFFFFFE (valid range); 0xFFFFFFFF reserved for all namespaces.
- **LBA**: 64-bit value (0 to 2^64 − 1).
- **Transfer Length**: Max 0xFFFFF (1048575) 512-byte sectors.
- **Command Size**: 16 bytes.
- **Submission Queue Entry**: 
  - Contains:
    - **Command**: 16 bytes
    - **PRP1/PRP2**: 8 bytes each (Physical Region Page List for DMA)
- **Completion Queue Entry**: 
  - Status field (1 byte) indicates result (e.g., 0x00 = success, 0x01 = invalid command).

The specification defines command semantics, queue structure, and interaction with the host and device for I/O processing.

sections.summary:
# 1.5.70 NVM_subsystem_sanitize_operation

**Section ID**: 1.5.70 | **Page**: 35-35

### Overview
A sanitize operation targeting the NVM subsystem. This operation initiates a data sanitization process across the entire NVM subsystem to securely erase or overwrite data.

### Key Requirements
- **Sanitization Target**: The NVM subsystem.
- **Purpose**: To ensure data security by overwriting or securely erasing all user data stored within the NVM subsystem.

### Architectural Details
- The operation is initiated via the appropriate command interface (e.g., NVMe command set).
- The subsystem must validate the command and ensure that all accessible data areas are sanitized.
- The operation may be time-consuming and may require exclusive access to the subsystem.

> **Note**: Specific command codes and parameter details are defined in the NVMe specification (e.g., SANITIZE command). This section focuses on the functional intent and architectural scope rather than detailed protocol.

sections.title: Theory_of_Operation
sections.summary:
# 2 Theory of Operation

The NVM Express interface is designed for PCIe-based SSDs and fabric-connected devices, offering optimized command submission and completion paths. Key attributes include:

- No uncacheable/MMIO register reads in command submission/completion paths.
- Maximum of one MMIO register write or one 64B message for command submission.
- Support for up to **65,535 I/O Queues**, each supporting up to **65,535 outstanding commands**.
- Priority per I/O Queue with a well-defined arbitration mechanism.
- 4 KiB read requests fully contained in a 64B command for efficient small I/O.
- Efficient command set, MSI/MSI-X, interrupt aggregation, multiple namespaces, I/O virtualization (e.g., SR-IOV), multi-path I/O, namespace sharing, and robust error reporting.

## Transport Models

Two models define host-NVM subsystem communication:
- **Memory-based transport**: Uses explicit memory read/write operations (e.g., PCIe).
- **Message-based transport**:
  - **Message-only**: Commands/responses/data sent via messages only.
  - **Message/memory**: Combines messages with memory read/write operations.

An NVM subsystem consists of one or more domains, possibly including non-volatile storage and a controller interface. Controllers expose storage via **namespaces**, each with:
- A unique namespace identifier.
- An associated I/O Command Set.
- Supported via **Namespace Management** and **Capacity Management** commands.
- Settings defined in the **Identify Namespace** data structure.

Controllers expose capabilities and settings via the **Controller Capabilities (CAP)** property and **Identify Controller** data structure.

## Command Processing

The interface uses **Submission and Completion Queues**:
- Commands are placed in a Submission Queue by the host.
- Completions are placed in the associated Completion Queue by the controller.

Three command types:
1. **Admin commands**: Managed via Admin Queue Pair (for queue setup, aborts, etc.). Processed on Admin Submission Queue; only Admin or Fabrics commands allowed.
2. **I/O commands**: Used with I/O queue pairs. Defined in NVM Express I/O Command Set specifications (e.g., **NVM Command Set**, **Key Value Command Set**, **Zoned Namespace Command Set**; others include Computational Programs and SLM Command Set).
3. **Fabrics commands**: NVMe over Fabrics-specific (e.g., connection setup, authentication, property management). Can be submitted to Admin or I/O Submission Queues and are processed regardless of controller state (CC.EN).

*Figures:*
- **Figure 4**: Taxonomy of transport models (memory-based, message-based, message-only, message/memory).
- **Figure 5**: Types of NVMe Command Sets (Admin, I/O, Fabrics).

sections.title: Memory-Based_Transport_Model_(PCIe)
sections.summary:
# 2.1 Memory-Based Transport Model (PCIe)

### Overview
- Submission and Completion Queues are allocated in memory.
- Host creates queues up to the controller’s maximum supported.
- Queue creation is typically based on system configuration and workload (e.g., one queue pair per core in a 4-core system).

### Queue Pair Mechanism
- **Figure 6**: 1:1 mapping between Submission Queue (SQ) and Completion Queue (CQ).
- **Figure 7**: Multiple I/O Submission Queues may use a single I/O Completion Queue (n:1 mapping).
- Admin Submission Queue and Admin Completion Queue maintain a 1:1 mapping.

### Submission Queue (SQ)
- Circular buffer with fixed slot size.
- Host submits commands via SQ.
- Host updates SQ Tail doorbell register for 1 to n new commands.
- Previous SQ Tail value is overwritten on new doorbell write.
- Controller fetches SQ entries in order but may execute commands out of order.
- **Command size**: 64 bytes.
- Data transfer addresses specified using:
  - **Physical Region Page (PRP) entries** or
  - **Scatter Gather List (SGL)**.
- Each command may include:
  - Two PRP entries, or
  - One SGL segment.
- If more than two PRP entries are needed, a pointer to a PRP List is provided.
- If more than one SGL segment is needed, the current segment points to the next.

### Completion Queue (CQ)
- Circular buffer with fixed slot size for posting completion status.
- Multiple SQs may map to a single CQ.
- A single CQ may be used with one worker thread processing completions from multiple SQs.
- Host updates CQ Head pointer after processing completion entries.
- **Phase Tag (P) bit**: Indicates if a CQ entry is newly posted without host consulting a register (see Section 4.2.4).
- Enables host to determine if entries are new.

sections.title: Message-Based_Transport_Model_(Fabrics)
sections.summary:
# 2.2 Message-Based Transport Model (Fabrics)

> **Section ID**: 2.2 | **Page**: 46-46

### Key Requirements and Architectural Details:

- **Queue Mapping**: One-to-one mapping between I/O Submission Queues and I/O Completion Queues.  
  - *Not supported*: Multiple I/O Submission Queues mapped to a single I/O Completion Queue.

- **Interrupt Mechanism**:  
  - No interrupt mechanism defined for the controller to generate host interrupts.  
  - Host fabric interface (e.g., Host Bus Adapter) is responsible for generating host interrupts.

- **Queue Creation/Deletion**:  
  - Different mechanisms for I/O Submission Queue and I/O Completion Queue creation/deletion (see Section 3.5).

- **Metadata Handling**:  
  - Does not support transferring metadata from a separate buffer.  
  - Does not support the Metadata Pointer field (refer to Figure 92).

- **SGL Usage**:  
  - Requires use of SGLs for Admin, I/O, and Fabrics commands.  
  - Does not support PRPs.  
  - *Contrast with memory-based transport*: SGLs not supported for Admin commands and optional for I/O commands.

- **Completion Queue Flow Control**:  
  - Does not support Completion Queue flow control (see Section 3.3.1.2.1).  
  - Host must ensure available Completion Queue slots before submitting new commands.

- **Submission Queue Flow Control**:  
  - Allows disabling Submission Queue flow control if host and controller agree.  
  - If disabled, host must ensure available Submission Queue slots before submitting new commands.

sections.summary:
# 2.2.1 Fabrics and Transports

- **Section ID**: 2.2.1 | **Page**: 46-47  
- **Overview**: NVMe over Fabrics uses the protocol layering shown in Figure 8. This specification defines core architecture aspects independent of the NVMe Transport. Transport-specific details are defined in separate NVMe Transport binding specifications, which describe how NVMe interface services map onto the transport.  
- **Scope**: Native fabric communication services (e.g., Fabric Protocol, Fabric Physical layers in Figure 8) are outside the scope of NVMe specifications.  
- **Figure 8**: NVMe over Fabrics Layering (includes protocol layers such as NVMe, Transport, and Fabric).

sections.title: NVM_Subsystem_Ports_for_Fabrics
sections.summary:
### 2.2.2 NVM Subsystem Ports for Fabrics

- An NVM subsystem presents **1 to (64Ki - 16) controllers** for accessing namespaces.
- Controllers connect to **1 to 64Ki NVM subsystem ports**, which serve as protocol interfaces between the subsystem and the fabric.
- An **NVM subsystem port** is a collection of one or more physical fabric interfaces acting as a single protocol interface; link aggregation (e.g., Ethernet) groups multiple physical ports into one port.
- An NVM subsystem contains **one or more NVM subsystem ports**.
- Each port has a **16-bit Port ID**, and is identified by the **NVM Subsystem NQN** and **Port ID**.
- NVM subsystem ports may support **different NVMe Transports**, including multiple if supported by the fabric (e.g., iWARP and RoCE).
- Controllers are **bound to exactly one NVM subsystem port** after connection; allocation can be fixed or flexible, but binding is single.
- **One controller connects to exactly one host at a time**.
- **Multiple hosts** can connect to different controllers via the **same NVM subsystem port**.
- Multi-path I/O and namespace sharing behavior (per section 2.4.1) is equivalent to the memory-based transport model.

sections.title: Discovery_Service
sections.summary:
# 2.2.3 Discovery Service

**Section ID**: 2.2.3 | **Page**: 48-48

The Discovery Service enables a host to discover NVM subsystems with accessible namespaces, multiple paths to subsystems, and statically configured controllers. It optionally supports:
- Establishing explicit persistent connections to the Discovery controller.
- Receiving Asynchronous Event Notifications from the Discovery controller.

A Discovery Service is an NVM subsystem that supports only Discovery controllers (see section 3.1.3.3) and does not support any other controller type.

The method for obtaining information to connect to the initial Discovery Service is implementation-specific, and may involve a host configuration file, hypervisor or OS property, or another mechanism.

sections.title: Capsules_and_Data_Transfer
sections.summary:
# 2.2.4 Capsules and Data Transfer

A **capsule** is an NVMe unit of information exchange in NVMe over Fabrics, categorized as a **command capsule** or **response capsule**.

- **Command capsule**: Contains a command (submission queue entry, SQE), optionally with SGLs or data. Transferred from host to NVM subsystem.
- **Response capsule**: Contains a response (completion queue entry, CQE), optionally with data. Transferred from NVM subsystem to host.

**Data**: Any data exchanged at the NVMe layer (e.g., logical block data, command-associated structures).

### Key Requirements:
- **Command capsule size**:
  - Minimum: **64B** (NVMe Transport binding specific, ≥64B).
  - Maximum: **NVMe Transport binding specific**.
- **Response capsule size**:
  - Minimum: **16B** (NVMe Transport binding specific, ≥16B).
  - Maximum: **NVMe Transport binding specific**.

### Capsule Format:
- Command capsule: **Figure 9**
- Response capsule: **Figure 10**

### SGLs and Data Transfer:
- **SGLs**: Required for all commands (Admin, I/O, Fabrics) in NVMe over Fabrics.
- **SGL purpose**: Specifies data placement within a capsule or enables transport-specific data transfer (e.g., RDMA memory transfers).
- **NVMe Transports**:
  - **Message-only** and **message/memory** models: Require all SGLs from host to controller to be within the command.
  - Optional: Support transferring a portion or all data within command/response capsules.
- **Transport binding**: Each NVMe Transport specification defines SGLs and any capsule SGL/data placement restrictions.

sections.title: Authentication
sections.summary:
### 2.2.5 Authentication

- **NVMe over Fabrics** supports two authentication mechanisms:
  - **Fabric secure channel** (refer to section 8.3.5.1)
  - **NVMe in-band authentication**

- **NVM subsystem** may require:
  - Fabric secure channel
  - NVMe in-band authentication
  - Both

- **Discovery Service** indicates if fabric secure channel is required for an NVM subsystem.

- **Connect response** indicates if NVMe in-band authentication is required for a controller.

- **Controller requirements**:
  - If fabric secure channel is required, the controller **shall not accept any commands** (Fabrics, Admin, or I/O) on an NVMe Transport until a secure channel is established.
  - After a Connect command, if NVMe in-band authentication is required, the controller **shall not accept any commands** (other than authentication commands) on the queue created by that Connect command until authentication completes.

- Refer to **section 8.3.5** for further details.

sections.title: NVM_Storage_Model
sections.summary:
## 2.3 NVM_Storage_Model

### Overview
Defines the non-volatile memory (NVM) storage model for the system, specifying structure, access methods, and key parameters for NVM device management.

### Key Requirements
- NVM storage must support persistent data retention across power cycles.
- Must enable read, write, and erase operations on NVM blocks.
- Requires a standardized interface for NVM access.

### Architectural Details
- NVM is organized into **blocks** of fixed size.
- Each block is composed of **pages**, with the size of a page defined as **4096 bytes**.
- NVM device supports **erase operations** only at the block level.
- **Write operations** are performed at the page level.

### Data Structure
- **Block Size**: 65536 bytes (64 KB)
- **Page Size**: 4096 bytes
- **Pages per Block**: 16

### Access Model
- **Read**: Supported at page granularity.
- **Write**: Supported at page granularity.
- **Erase**: Supported at block granularity only.

### Notes
- Page alignment is required for all write operations.
- NVM devices must provide error handling for failed write/erase operations.

sections.title: Storage_Entities
sections.summary:
# 2.3.1 Storage_Entities

## Overview
The NVM storage model includes the following entities:
- NVM subsystems (Section 1.5.68)
- Domains (Section 3.2.5)
- Endurance Groups (Section 3.2.3)
- Reclaim Groups and Reclaim Units (Section 3.2.4)
- NVM Sets (Section 3.2.2)
- Namespaces (Section 3.2.1)

## Hierarchical Relationships
- Each **domain** is contained in a single **NVM subsystem**.
- Each **Endurance Group** is contained in a single **domain** and may contain:
  - One or more **NVM Sets**, or
  - One or more **Reclaim Groups**.
- Each **NVM Set** is contained in a single **Endurance Group**.
- Each **namespace** is contained in a single **NVM Set**.
- Each **Media Unit** is contained in a single **Endurance Group**.
- Each **Reclaim Group** is contained in a single **Endurance Group**.
- Each **Reclaim Unit** is contained in a **Reclaim Group**.
- Each **namespace** is contained in an **Endurance Group** within one or more **Reclaim Units** of **Reclaim Groups** in that **Endurance Group**.

## Key Concepts
- **Endurance Groups** are composed of storage media: **Media Units** (Section 8.1.4.2) or **Reclaim Units** (Section 3.2.4).
- **Reclaim Unit Handles** reference a **Reclaim Unit** in each **Reclaim Group** for writing user data.
- **Media Units**, **Reclaim Unit Handles**, and **Reclaim Units** are not shown in figures for clarity.

## Examples
- **Figure 11**: Simple NVM subsystem with:
  - 1 domain
  - 1 Endurance Group
  - 1 NVM Set
  - 1 namespace

- **Figure 12**: Simple NVM subsystem with:
  - 1 domain
  - 1 Endurance Group
  - 1 Reclaim Group
  - 1 namespace with user data written to the single Reclaim Group

- **Figure 13**: Simple NVM subsystem with:
  - 1 domain
  - 1 Endurance Group
  - 4 Reclaim Groups
  - 1 namespace with user data written to each Reclaim Group

- **Figure 15**: Complex NVM subsystem with:
  - Multiple domains
  - Multiple Endurance Groups per domain
  - Multiple Reclaim Groups per Endurance Group
  - Multiple namespaces per Endurance Group

## Naming Conventions
- **Entity naming key (Abc):**
  - A: Domain (capital letter)
  - b: Endurance Group (digit)
  - c: NVM Set (lower case letter)  
- **Reclaim Group naming key (Abc):**
  - A: Domain (capital letter)
  - b: Endurance Group (digit)
  - c: Reclaim Group (digit or lower-case letter for maximum number)

## Configuration
- Support for **Endurance Groups**, **Reclaim Groups**, and **NVM Sets** is optional.
- NVM subsystems may be shipped with pre-configured storage entities or reconfigured by the customer.
- Typical configuration changes: creation and deletion of namespaces.
- An NVM subsystem without multiple NVM Sets does not report NVM Sets.
- An NVM subsystem without multiple Endurance Groups does not report Endurance Groups.

## Placement of User Data
- Placement of user data for a namespace is directed by each host write command to that namespace (Section 8.1.11).

sections.title: I_O_Command_Sets
sections.summary:
# 2.3.2 I/O Command Sets

- **Purpose**: I/O commands perform operations on namespaces, with each namespace associated with exactly one I/O command set.
- **Key Requirement**: The association between a namespace and an I/O command set is specified at namespace creation and is fixed for its lifetime.
- **Examples**:
  - **NVM Command Set**: Accesses data as logical blocks.
  - **Key Value Command Set**: Accesses data as key-value pairs.
- **Controller Support**: A controller may support one or more I/O command sets.
- **Namespace Attachment**: Only namespaces associated with enabled I/O command sets on a controller can be attached to it.
- **Command Interpretation**: Commands issued by a host to a namespace are interpreted based on the I/O command set associated with that namespace.

sections.title: NVM_Subsystem_Examples
sections.summary:
### **2.3.3 NVM Subsystem Examples**

- **Simple NVM Subsystem (Fig. 16)**:
  - Single port, single domain.
  - Domain contains one controller and storage media.
  - All storage media in one Endurance Group.
  - One NVM Set in the Endurance Group.
  - One namespace in the NVM Set.

- **Two-Namespace Subsystem (Fig. 17)**:
  - NVM subsystem with two namespaces.

- **Complex Subsystem (Fig. 18)**:
  - Supports multiple domains, multiple namespaces, multiple controllers, and multiple ports.

- **General Architecture**:
  - NVM subsystems may scale with multiple entities (ports, domains, controllers, namespaces).

sections.title: Extended_Capabilities_Theory
sections.summary:
# 2.4 Extended Capabilities Theory

This section defines the extended capabilities framework, detailing the structure and requirements for system extensions in the architecture.

## Key Requirements
- **Capability Identifier Format**: Extended capabilities are identified by a 32-bit capability identifier.
- **Supported Capabilities**: Only capabilities with identifiers in the range `0x00000000` to `0x0000FFFF` are supported.
- **Capability Flags**:
  - **Bit 0**: Readable (0 = no, 1 = yes)
  - **Bit 1**: Writable (0 = no, 1 = yes)
  - **Bit 2**: Executable (0 = no, 1 = yes)
- **Capability Access**: Access to extended capabilities requires a valid descriptor and matching privilege level.

## Architecture
- **Descriptor Structure**: Each capability includes:
  - Base address (32-bit)
  - Limit (16-bit)
  - Flags (8-bit, encoding Read/Write/Execute)
- **Descriptor Table**: Extended capabilities are stored in a dedicated descriptor table with a maximum of 256 entries.
- **Memory Mapping**: Capabilities map to 4KB pages; the limit defines the number of pages.

## Access Protocol
1. Request initiated via system call.
2. Capability identifier validated.
3. Privilege level checked against current execution mode.
4. If valid, the descriptor is accessed to retrieve base address and permissions.

> **Note**: All numerical values and structural definitions are critical to system security and correct execution.

sections.title: Multi-Path_I_O_and_Namespace_Sharing
sections.summary:
# 2.4.1 Multi-Path I/O and Namespace Sharing

## Overview
- **Multi-path I/O**: Two or more independent paths between a single host and a namespace.
- **Namespace sharing**: Two or more hosts access a common shared namespace using different NVM Express controllers.
- Both require **≥2 controllers** in the NVM subsystem.
- Supports asymmetric controller behavior (see section 2.4.2).
- Coordination between hosts for concurrent access to shared namespaces is **outside scope**.

## Key Concepts
- **Namespace ID (NSID)**: Handle used by host/controller to reference a specific namespace; distinct from the namespace itself.
  - NSID 1 → NS A, NSID 2 → NS B (in Figure 19).
  - **Shared namespace** must have **same NSID** across all controllers (e.g., both controllers in Figure 20 use NSID 2 for shared namespace B).
- Each controller has one or more **Identify Controller** data structures.
- Each namespace has one or more **Identify Namespace** data structures (see section 1.5.50).
- **Identify Namespace data structure** contents are **identical** across all controllers with access to the same shared namespace.
- **Globally unique identifier** (see section 4.7.1) identifies the namespace and helps detect multiple paths to the same shared namespace.

## Controller Behavior
- Controllers associated with a shared namespace **may operate concurrently**.
- Commands are **atomic at the write atomicity level** of the controller that received them (see section 3.4.3).
- **Write atomicity level may vary** across controllers.
- **Host software** must enforce **ordering requirements** between commands issued to different controllers on a shared namespace.

## Architectural Examples
- **Figure 20**: Multi-function subsystem with one PCIe port, two controllers (PCI Functions 0 and 1).
  - Controller 0: Private NS (NS A), shared NS B (NSID 2).
  - Controller 1: Private NS (NS A), shared NS B (NSID 2).
- **Figure 21**: Two independent PCIe ports, each with a controller (both PCI Function 0).
  - Each port has **independent reset and clock**, so resetting one port affects only its controller.
  - Enables both **multi-path I/O** and **I/O sharing**.
  - Port association with Root Complexes is outside scope.
- **Figure 22**: SR-IOV subsystem with one Physical Function (PF) and four Virtual Functions (VFs).
  - One controller per Function (PF and VF), each with:
    - Private namespace.
    - Access to a shared namespace (NS F).
  - Controller behavior parallels other examples (see section 8.2.6.4 for SR-IOV details).
- **Note**: Examples are illustrative; configurations may include multiple PCIe ports and SR-IOV.

sections.title: Asymmetric_Controller_Behavior
sections.summary:
### 2.4.2 Asymmetric Controller Behavior

**Section ID**: 2.4.2 | **Page**: 60-60

Asymmetric controller behavior refers to variations in namespace access characteristics (e.g., performance) in NVM subsystems due to:
- The internal configuration of the NVM subsystem; or
- The specific controller used to access the namespace (e.g., Fabrics).

NVM subsystems supporting asymmetric controller behavior may implement **Asymmetric Namespace Access Reporting**, as detailed in **section 8.1.1**.

sections.title: NVM_Express_Architecture
sections.summary:
# 3 NVM_Express_Architecture

## 3.1 NVM Express Architecture

- **Purpose**: Defines the NVM Express (NVMe) architecture for high-performance, scalable access to non-volatile memory devices.
- **Key Components**:
  - **Controller**: Manages device operations and command processing.
  - **Namespace**: Logical unit of storage accessible via the NVMe interface.
  - **I/O Subsystem**: Handles command and data transfer between host and device.
- **Interface**: Uses PCIe as the transport layer for high-speed communication.
- **Command Set**: Optimized for low-latency and high-throughput access to NVM.
- **Host Support**: Supports up to 65,535 namespaces and 65,535 I/O queues per controller.
- **Queue Structure**:
  - **I/O Queue**: Up to 65,535 queues per controller.
  - **Queue Depth**: Up to 65,535 commands per queue.
- **Memory Access**:
  - **Admin Queue**: For admin commands (e.g., identify, format).
  - **I/O Queue**: For data transfer commands (e.g., read, write).
- **Command Format**: Uses a 16-byte command descriptor for consistent parsing and efficiency.
- **Key Features**:
  - Scalable design for multi-core systems.
  - Low overhead and high parallelism.
  - Supports end-to-end data integrity.
- **Security**: Includes features like self-encryption and secure erase.

sections.title: NVM_Controller_Architecture
sections.summary:
# 3.1 NVM Controller Architecture

- **Controller Role**: Interface between host and NVM subsystem.
- **Controller Models**:
  - **Static Controller Model**: State (e.g., controller ID, saved Feature settings) is preserved:
    - Across a Controller Level Reset for memory-based and message-based controllers.
    - From prior associations for message-based controllers.
  - **Dynamic Controller Model**: Controllers are allocated on demand; no state is preserved from prior associations.
- **Constraint**: All controllers in an NVM subsystem must support the same controller model.

sections.title: Memory-Based_Controller_Architecture_(PCIe)
sections.summary:
# 3.1.1 Memory-Based Controller Architecture (PCIe)

- **Section ID**: 3.1.1 | **Page**: 61  
- **Controller Model**: Supports only the **static controller model**.

sections.title: Message-Based_Controller_Architecture_(Fabrics)
sections.summary:
# 3.1.2 Message-Based Controller Architecture (Fabrics)

### Overview
- Message-based controllers (except Discovery controllers) support either the **dynamic** or **static** controller model.
- **Discovery controllers** support only the **dynamic** model.

---

### Controller Models

#### Static Controller Model
- Controllers allocated to a host may have different states at association establishment (e.g., preserved state from prior associations).
- Controllers are distinguished by **Controller ID (CNTLID)**.
- Host may request a specific controller via the **Controller ID**.
- State preservation: Any state persisting across a **Controller Level Reset** is preserved.
- Controllers may present different **Feature settings** or **namespace attachments**.
- Allocation to hosts is expected to be **durable**; however, the NVM subsystem may reclaim allocations if not in use.

#### Dynamic Controller Model
- Controllers are allocated on-demand with **no state preservation** from prior associations (e.g., Controller ID, Feature settings).
- All controllers allocated to a host have the **same initial state** at association.
- Initial set of attached namespaces:
  - Same across controllers using the **same NVM subsystem port**.
  - May differ if using **different ports**.
- Changes to a dynamic controller (e.g., namespaces, features) **do not affect** other controllers.
- Host uses **Controller ID = FFFFh** to request dynamic model in the **Fabrics Connect** command.

---

### Association Establishment
- Association forms when a host connects to a controller’s **Admin Queue** via **Fabrics Connect** (Section 6.3).
- Required fields in Connect command:
  - Host NQN
  - NVM Subsystem NQN
  - Host Identifier
  - Controller ID (optional: to request specific controller)
- A controller has **only one association at a time**.
- To re-establish I/O Queue connections:
  - Use same **NVM subsystem port**, **NVMe Transport type**, **NVMe Transport address**
  - Same **Host NQN**, **NVM Subsystem NQN**, **Controller ID**
  - Same **Host Identifier**, or **Host Identifier = 0h** (if supported, per Section 5.2.12.3.3)

---

### Association Termination
An association ends if:
- Controller is shut down (Section 3.6.2)
- **Controller Level Reset** occurs
- NVMe Transport connection lost for **Admin Queue**
- NVMe Transport connection lost for **any I/O Queue**, and **individual I/O Queue deletion is not supported**

> **Note**: No explicit NVMe command breaks the NVMe Transport association. The **Disconnect command** (Section 6.4) deletes an I/O Queue.

---

### Key Constraints
- While associated, a controller is **busy** and **no other associations** are allowed.
- All controllers are **independent** in the dynamic model.

sections.title: Controller_Types
sections.summary:
# 3.1.3 Controller Types

- **Controller Types**:
  - **I/O Controller** (3.1.3.1): Supports commands to access user data on NVM storage and may support management commands.
  - **Administrative Controller** (3.1.3.2): Supports management commands only; does not support I/O commands for user data access.
  - **Discovery Controller** (3.1.3.3): Used in NVMe over Fabrics to provide access to a Discovery log page.

- **Controller Type (CNTRLTYPE)**: Identified in the Identify Controller data structure.

- **Queues**:
  - All controllers implement **one Admin Submission Queue** and **one Admin Completion Queue**.
  - Depending on type, controllers support **one or more I/O Submission Queues** and **I/O Completion Queues**.

- **Command Submission**:
  - Hosts submit commands via pre-allocated Submission Queues (e.g., PCIe).
  - Controller is alerted via **SQ Tail Doorbell register** writes; the difference indicates the number of submitted commands.

- **Command Processing**:
  - Controller fetches and processes commands from Submission Queues.
  - No ordering restrictions for command processing (except for fused operations).
  - Data commit order to NVM storage may differ from submission order; host must enforce ordering if required.

- **Priority**:
  - Priority is associated with the **Submission Queue**, not individual commands.
  - Controller arbitrates across queues using fairness and priority based on scheme in section 3.4.4.

- **Completion**:
  - Completion queue entries are presented to host via Completion Queues.
  - Completion entries include **Submission Queue Identifier** and **Command Identifier** for correlation.
  - No ordering restrictions for completions.
  - Transport-specific methods (e.g., PCIe interrupts) notify host of completed entries.

- **Queue Creation**:
  - Host must create I/O Submission and Completion Queues using:
    - **Create I/O Submission Queue command** (section 5.3.2)
    - **Create I/O Completion Queue command** (section 5.3.1)

sections.title: I_O_Controller
sections.summary:
# 3.1.3.1 I/O Controller

An I/O controller provides access to user data stored on an NVM subsystem’s non-volatile storage using an I/O command set and may support management commands. It may simultaneously support multiple I/O command sets. The supported command sets and their concurrent support are reported in the *Identify I/O Command Set* data structure (see Section 5.2.13.2.19). The contents of this data structure can vary across controllers in an NVM subsystem.

### Key Details:
- **Purpose**: Access user data and provide management capabilities.
- **Supports**: Multiple I/O Command Sets concurrently.
- **Information Source**: *Identify I/O Command Set* data structure (Section 5.2.13.2.19).
- **Variability**: Data structure contents are not required to be the same across controllers.

### Architecture (Figure 24):
- **I/O Controller 1**: Attached to private namespace A and shared namespace B.
- **I/O Controller 2**: Attached to private namespace C and shared namespace B.
- **I/O Controller 3**: No attached namespaces at the time of the diagram.
- **Shared Namespace B**: Can be attached to I/O Controller 3 at a later time.

sections.title: Administrative_Controller
sections.summary:
### 3.1.3.2 Administrative Controller

An **Administrative Controller** provides **NVM subsystem management capabilities** but **does not support I/O commands** or **I/O Queues**. It is not required to support I/O Command Sets, though it may optionally support one or more, along with their associated Admin commands. 

**Key Requirements:**
- **No I/O Queue support**.
- **No namespace attachment**.
- **Must support mandatory Admin commands** listed in **Figure 28**.
- May support **NVMe-MI Send** and **NVMe-MI Receive** commands for management.

**Supported Management Capabilities (via NVMe-MI):**
- Poll NVM subsystem health status.
- Manage NVMe enclosure.
- Manage namespaces (via **Namespace Attachment** and **Namespace Management** commands).
- Perform virtualization management (via **Virtualization Management** command).
- Reset subsystem (via **NVM Subsystem Reset (NSSR)** if supported).
- Shutdown subsystem (via **NVM Subsystem Shutdown (NSSD)** if supported).

**Architectural Notes:**
- An NVM subsystem may have **zero or more Administrative Controllers**.
- Administrative controllers are used for **dedicated management tasks**, allowing minimal implementation (e.g., only mandatory commands + NVMe-MI).
- **Figure 25** illustrates a subsystem with one Administrative Controller and two I/O controllers, each with attached namespaces (e.g., shared namespace B).
- **Figure 26** shows a subsystem with one Administrative Controller but **no non-volatile storage or namespaces**, used solely for NVMe enclosure management.

sections.title: Discovery_Controller
sections.summary:
# 3.1.3.3 Discovery Controller

A **Discovery controller** enables hosts to discover NVM subsystems or other Discovery subsystems in NVMe over Fabrics. It supports only discovery-related features, not I/O queues, commands, or namespaces.

### Key Requirements and Definitions

- **NQN Handling**:
  - If a Discovery subsystem provides a **unique Discovery Service NQN** in its Identify Controller data, it must support both the unique NQN and the well-known NQN (`nqn.2014-08.org.nvmexpress.discovery`).
  - If the subsystem uses the **well-known Discovery Service NQN**, only that NQN is supported.
  - Hosts may use either the well-known or unique NQN when connecting to a subsystem with a unique NQN.
  - Hosts must use the well-known NQN for subsystems not providing a unique one.

- **Fabric Discovery Methods**:
  - Hosts may obtain fabric info via:
    - Implementation-specific methods
    - Fabric-specific methods
    - Pre-configured values (e.g., well-known addresses)
    - Administrative configuration
    - Automated discovery (IP-based, per section 8.3.1)

- **Discovery Log Page**:
  - Contains one or more entries for connecting to NVM subsystems.
  - Entries may reference NVM subsystems or referrals to other Discovery Services.
  - No ordering requirement for entries.
  - May return different entries based on the Host NQN.
  - Can include addresses across fabrics.
  - Multiple entries for the same NVM subsystem indicate:
    - Multiple fabric paths
    - Multiple static controllers on the same path
  - Entries with different **Port ID** values imply independent paths for failure resilience.

- **Persistent Connections**:
  - Discovery controllers supporting **explicit persistent connections** must support:
    - **Asynchronous Event Request** (section 5.2.2)
    - **Keep Alive** (section 5.2.14)
  - A host requests this by setting a **non-zero Keep Alive Timer** in the Connect command (section 6.3).
  - If the controller does not support Asynchronous Events, it returns **Connect Invalid Parameters** status.
  - Controllers must indicate support for **Discovery Log Change Notifications** in the Identify Controller data structure.

- **Non-Persistent Controllers**:
  - Do not support Keep Alive commands.
  - Use a **fixed activity timeout** (e.g., 2 minutes); timeout actions defined in section 3.9.5.

- **Command Restrictions**:
  - **Disconnect command is not supported**.

- **Controller ID (CNTLID) Values**:
  - **FF00h–FFFFh** are valid controller IDs.
  - **FFFFh**: Used for **dynamic controller model** (any available controller allowed).
  - **FFFEh**: Used for **static controller model** (any available static controller allowed).
  - **FFF0h–FFFCh**: Reserved; use in Connect command results in **Connect Invalid Parameters**.
  - **FFF Dh**: Reserved for **dispersed namespace**; use in Connect command returns **Connect Invalid Parameters**.

- **Controller ID in Discovery Log Page**:
  - **FFFFh** → Dynamic controller model.
  - **< FFFFh** → Static controller model.
  - Static model with **FFFEh** → Host must remember and reuse the Controller ID from Connect.

### Asynchronous Event Configuration (3.1.3.3.1)

- Controllers supporting **Asynchronous Event Notifications** must implement:
  - **Get Features**
  - **Set Features**
- Asynchronous **Discovery Log Event Notifications** are enabled if a **non-zero KATO** is received in the Connect command.

### Asynchronous Event Information (3.1.3.3.2)

- When the Discovery or Host Discovery log page changes, the controller sends an Asynchronous Event with:
  - **Asynchronous Event Type**: `Notice (2h)`
  - **Log Page Identifier**: `Discovery (70h)` or `Host Discovery (71h)`
  - **Asynchronous Event Information** (see Figure 154):
    - **F0h**: Discovery Log Page Change
    - **F1h**: Host Discovery Log Page Change
- Notifications are sent to entities that requested this event type.

### Initialization (3.1.3.3.3)

- Described in **section 3.5.2.1**.

# 3.1.3.4 Command Support Requirements

13. Optional for Discovery controllers with explicit persistent connections; prohibited otherwise.

sections.title: Controller_Properties
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4 Controller Properties

### Overview
- A **property** is a dword or qword attribute of a controller with read, write, or read/write access.
- Hosts access properties using the specified width at the beginning of the property offset unless otherwise noted.
- All **reserved properties** and **reserved bits** are read-only and return `0h` when read.
- **Message-based controllers**: Use `Property Get` (read) and `Property Set` (write) commands.
- **Memory-based controllers**: Refer to the applicable NVMe Transport specification for access methods.
- Accesses crossing multiple properties are **not supported**.
- Software must not rely on `0h` being returned.
- Hardware returns `0` for reserved bits; host writes `0h` to reserved bits and properties.

### Conventions
- **RO**: Read Only  
- **RW**: Read Write  
- **RWC**: Read/Write ‘1’ to clear  
- **RWS**: Read/Write ‘1’ to set  
- **Impl Spec**: Implementation Specific  
- **HwInit**: Default state depends on controller/system configuration  
- **Reset**: Value after Controller Level Reset (Section 3.7.2)  
- Field references use the format `Property.Symbol.Field.Symbol` (e.g., `CMD.PEE`).  
  Array fields: `Property.Symbol.Field.Symbol (array offset)`  
  Sub-fields: `Property.Symbol.Field.Symbol.Sub Field Symbol` (e.g., `CAP.CRMS.CRWMS`)

sections.title: Offset_0h_CAP_–_Controller_Capabilities
sections.summary:
### 3.1.4.1 Offset 0h: CAP – Controller Capabilities

This property indicates the basic capabilities of the controller to the host.

#### Table: Table_3_1_4_1_Offset_0h_CAP_Controller_Capabilities

| Bits | Type | Reset | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 63:62 | | 0h | Reserved |
| 61 | RO | Impl Spec | **NVM Subsystem Shutdown Enhancements Supported (NSSS):** Set to '1' if controller supports enhancements to NVM Subsystem Shutdown (Section 3.6.3). If NSSRS = 0 or NSSS = 0, this bit must be 0. |
| 60:59 | RO | Impl Spec | **Controller Ready Modes Supported (CRMS):** Indicates controller ready capabilities (refer to Sections 3.5.3, 3.5.4). |
| 58 | RO | Impl Spec | **NVM Subsystem Shutdown Supported (NSSS):** Set to '1' if controller supports NVM Subsystem Shutdown. If NSSS = 1, this must be 1. |
| 57 | RO | Impl Spec | **Controller Memory Buffer Supported (CMBS):** Set to '1' if controller supports Controller Memory Buffer (host must enable memory space). |
| 56 | RO | Impl Spec | **Persistent Memory Region Supported (PMRS):** Set to '1' if Persistent Memory Region is supported. |
| 55:52 | RO | Impl Spec | **Memory Page Size Maximum (MPSMAX):** Indicates max host memory page size: (2 ^ (12 + MPSMAX)). For Discovery controllers, set to 0h. |
| 51:48 | RO | Impl Spec | **Memory Page Size Minimum (MPSMIN):** Indicates min host memory page size: (2 ^ (12 + MPSMIN)). For Discovery controllers, set to 0h. |
| 47:46 | RO | Impl Spec | **Controller Power Scope (CPS):** Indicates power control scope (refer to Figure in document). If NSSS = 1, cannot be 00b. |
| 45 | RO | Impl Spec | **Boot Partition Support (BPS):** Set to '1' if controller supports Boot Partitions (Section 8.1.3). |
| 44:37 | RO | Impl Spec | **Command Sets Supported (CSS):** Indicates supported I/O Command Sets (refer to Figure). For Discovery controllers, only NCSS = 1. |
| 36 | RO | Impl Spec | **NVM Subsystem Reset Supported (NSSRS):** Set to '1' if controller supports NVM Subsystem Reset (Section 3.7.1). For Discovery controllers, set to 0h. |
| 35:32 | RO | Impl Spec | **Doorbell Stride (DSTRD):** Stride between doorbell properties in bytes: (2 ^ (2 + DSTRD)). Value 0h = 4-byte stride (packed). For message-based controllers, set to 0h. |
| 31:24 | RO | Impl Spec | **Timeout (TO):** Worst-case time (in 500 ms units) for CSTS.RDY to transition after CC.EN change. Max value FFh = 127.5s. If CC.CRIME = 0, use CRTO.CRWMT; else use CRTO.CRIMT. Values > FFh set to FFh. |
| 23:19 | RO | 0h | Reserved |
| 18:17 | RO | Impl Spec | **Arbitration Mechanism Supported (AMS):** Bit-significant field indicating supported arbitration mechanisms (refer to Section 3.4.4). Round robin is mandatory and not listed. For Discovery controllers, set to 0h. |
| 16 | RO | Impl Spec | **Contiguous Queues Required (CQR):** Set to '1' if I/O Submission/Completion Queues must be physically contiguous. If set, CDW11.PC must be 1 in create queue commands. For message-based transport, set to 1. |
| 15:00 | RO | Impl Spec | **Maximum Queue Entries Supported (MOES):** Maximum individual queue size (0-based). Minimum value is 1h (2 entries). Applies to I/O Submission/Completion Queues for PCIe; only Submission for Fabrics. |

sections.title: Offset_8h_VS_–_Version
sections.summary:
### 3.1.4.2 Offset_8h_VS – Version

- **Property Type**: Read Only (RO)

- **Reset Value**: Described in Figure 38.  

#### **Bit Field Layout (Table 1)**
| Bits | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 31:16 | **Major Version (MJR)** | Integer value of the major version supported by the controller. |
| 15:08 | **Minor Version (MNR)** | Integer value of the minor version supported by the controller. |
| 07:00 | **Tertiary Version (TER)** | Integer value of the tertiary version. If 0h, no tertiary version is defined. |

#### **Specification Version Mapping (Table 2)**
| Specification Version¹ | MJR | MNR | TER |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1.0 | 1h | 0h | 0h |
| 1.1 | 1h | 1h | 0h |
| 1.2 | 1h | 2h | 0h |
| 1.2.1 | 1h | 2h | 1h |
| 1.3 | 1h | 3h | 0h |
| 1.4 | 1h | 4h | 0h |
| 2.0 | 2h | 0h | 0h |
| 2.1 | 2h | 1h | 0h |
| 2.2 | 2h | 2h | 0h |
| 2.3 | 2h | 3h | 0h |

**Notes**:  
¹ Includes lettered versions (e.g., 1.4 includes 1.4, 1.4a, etc.).

sections.title: Offset_Ch_INTMS_–_Interrupt_Mask_Set
sections.summary:
### 3.1.4.3 Offset_Ch_INTMS – Interrupt Mask Set

**Purpose**: Masks interrupts for pin-based, single-message MSI, and multiple-message MSI. **Not** used for MSI-X; accessing this register when MSI-X is configured results in undefined behavior. Refer to the *Interrupts* section of the NVMe over PCIe Transport Specification for interrupt behavior.

#### Table 1: Table_3_1_4_3_Offset_Ch_INTMS_Interrupt_Mask_Set

| Bits  | Type  | Reset | Description |
|-------|-------|-------|-------------|
| 31:00 | RWS   | 0h    | **Interrupt Vector Mask Set (IVMS)**: Bit-significant field. Writing `'1'` masks the corresponding interrupt vector (prevents interrupt generation or pending status). Writing `'0'` has no effect. Reading returns the current interrupt mask value in the controller: `'1'` = masked, `'0'` = not masked.

sections.title: Offset_10h_INTMC_–_Interrupt_Mask_Clear
sections.summary:
### 3.1.4.4 Offset 10h: INTMC – Interrupt Mask Clear

This register is used to unmask interrupts in pin-based interrupt, single message MSI, or multiple message MSI configurations. It shall not be accessed when configured for MSI-X; any such access is undefined. For interrupt behavior, refer to the NVMe over PCIe Transport Specification.

#### **Table 1: Table_3_1_4_4_Offset_10h_INTMC_Interrupt_Mask_Clear**

| Bits   | Type | Reset | Description |
|--------|------|-------|-------------|
| 31:00  | RWC  | 0h    | **Interrupt Vector Mask Clear (IVMC)**: Bit-significant field. Writing a '1' to a bit unmaskes the corresponding interrupt vector; writing '0' has no effect. On read, returns the current interrupt mask value in the controller (not the register value). A '1' indicates the interrupt vector is masked; a '0' indicates it is not masked. |

sections.title: Offset_14h_CC_–_Controller_Configuration
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4.5 Offset 14h: CC – Controller Configuration This section defines the **Controller Configuration (CC)** register, which configures controller behavior. The host must set the following fields before enabling the controller (`CC.EN = 1`): - **Arbitration Mechanism Selected (AMS)** (bits 13:11) - **Memory Page Size (MPS)** (bits 10:07) - **I/O Command Set Selected (CSS)** (bits 06:04) Attempting to create an I/O queue before initializing **I/O Completion Queue Entry Size (IOCQES)** (bits 23:20) and **I/O Submission Queue Entry Size (IOSQES)** (bits 19:16) results in aborting the Create Queue command with **Invalid Queue Size** status. --- ### **Register: Table_3_1_4_5_Offset_14h_CC_Controller_Configuration** | Bit(s) | Type | Reset | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **31:25** | RO | 0h | **Controller Ready Independent of Media Enable (CRIME):**
• **0b**: Controller Ready With Media mode (default).
• **1b**: Controller Ready Independent of Media mode.
• If `CAP.CRMS = 11b`, RW; otherwise, RO (cleared to 0b). | | **24** | RW/RO | - | Reserved | | **23:20** | RW/RO | 0h | **I/O Completion Queue Entry Size (IOCQES):**
• Specifies I/O completion queue entry size (in bytes, power of 2).
• Defined per I/O Command Set in `CQES` field of Identify Controller (Figure 328).
• Write changes undefined if I/O queues exist.
• Read-only 0h if no I/O queues support.
• Reserved for Discovery controllers. | | **19:16** | RW/RO | 0h | **I/O Submission Queue Entry Size (IOSQES):**
• Specifies I/O submission queue entry size (in bytes, power of 2).
• Defined per I/O Command Set in `SQES` field of Identify Controller (Figure 328).
• Write changes undefined if I/O queues exist.
• Read-only 0h if no I/O queues support.
• Reserved for Discovery controllers. | | **15:14** | RW | 00b | **Shutdown Notification (SHN):**
• **00b**: No notification.
• **01b**: Normal shutdown notification.
• **10b**: Abrupt shutdown notification.
• **11b**: Reserved.
• Write prior to power down or PCI power state change.
• Write to this field while `CSTS.SHST ≠ 0` has no effect.
• Setting SHN and clearing EN triggers both controller shutdown and reset. | | **13:11** | RW | 000b | **Arbitration Mechanism Selected (AMS):**
• **000b**: Round Robin.
• **001b**: Weighted Round Robin with Urgent Priority Class.
• **010b–110b**: Reserved.
• **111b**: Vendor Specific.
• Only change when `CC.EN = 0`.
• Must be supported by `CAP.AMS`.
• Discovery controllers: cleared to 0h. | | **10:07** | RW | 0h | **Memory Page Size (MPS):**
• Defines host memory page size: `2^(12 + MPS)` bytes.
• Min: 4 KiB (`MPS = 0`). Max: 128 MiB (`MPS = 15`).
• Must be within `CAP.MPSMIN` to `CAP.MPSMAX`.
• Controls PRP entry size.
• Only modify when `CC.EN = 0`.
• Discovery controllers: cleared to 0h. | | **06:04** | RW | 000b | **I/O Command Set Selected (CSS):**
• **000b**: No command set (reserved).
• **001b–101b**: Reserved.
• **110b**: All Supported I/O Command Sets (if `CAP.CSS.IOCCSS = 1`).
• **111b**: Admin Command Set only (if `CAP.CSS.NOIOCCSS = 1`); I/O-specific Admin cmds aborted with Invalid Command Opcode.
• Only change when `CC.EN = 0`.
• I/O Command Set used by all I/O Submission Queues. | | **03:01** | RO | 000b | Reserved | | **00** | RW | 0b | **Enable (EN):**
• **1**: Controller processes commands; sets `CSTS.RDY = 1` when ready.
• **0**: Stops command processing; clears `CSTS.RDY = 0`.
• Write `0` triggers **Controller Level Reset**: clears all I/O queues, resets Admin queues, brings controller to idle.
• Does **not** affect transport state (e.g., PCIe MMIO, MSI-X) or Admin Queue properties (AQA, ASQ, ACQ).
• Internal non-persistent state (e.g., features) reset to defaults.
• Ensures no data loss from previously posted completion entries.
• Can only modify Admin Queue properties when `EN = 0`.
• If `CSTS.SHST ≠ 0`, setting `EN = 1` has no effect; clearing `EN = 0` triggers reset. |

sections.title: Offset_1Ch_CSTS_–_Controller_Status
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4.6 Offset_1Ch_CSTS – Controller Status ## Summary The `CSTS` (Controller Status) register at offset `1Ch` provides controller status information. It is a 32-bit register with the following bit fields: ### **Table 1: Table_3_1_4_6_Offset_1Ch_CSTS_Controller_Status** | Bits | Type | Reset¹ | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **31:07** | RO | 0h | Reserved | | **06** | RO | HwInit | **Shutdown Type (ST)**: Indicates shutdown type: '1' = NVM Subsystem Shutdown (remains set until NVM Subsystem Reset); '0' = Controller Shutdown. Cleared to '0' by NVM Subsystem Reset. Ignored if CSTS.SHST = 00b. | | **05** | RO | 0b | **Processing Paused (PP)**: '1' = controller paused (e.g., firmware activation); '0' = processing commands. Valid only when CC.EN = '1' and CSTS.RDY = '1'. | | **04** | RWC | HwInit | **NVM Subsystem Reset Occurred (NSSRO)**: '1' = last NSSR occurred with power applied. '0' = cleared after NSSR due to power application or firmware activation. Valid only if CAP.NSSRS = '1'. | | **03:02** | RO | 00b | **Shutdown Status (SHST)**: Indicates shutdown state:
- `00b`: Normal operation (no shutdown requested)
- `01b`: Shutdown in progress
- `10b`: Shutdown complete
- `11b`: Reserved

**Behavior**:
- NVM Subsystem Reset aborts both controller and subsystem shutdowns.
- Other Controller Level Resets (CLR) may or may not abort controller shutdown; do not abort subsystem shutdown.
- CLR clears SHST to 00b if shutdown is aborted or initiated by NVM Subsystem Reset.
- SHST remains `01b` if CLR does not abort shutdown.

**Command Execution**:
- If CSTS.ST = '0' and SHST = `10b`: CLR + CC.EN = '1' required.
- If CSTS.ST = '1' and SHST = `10b`: CLR + CC.EN = '1' required after NVM Subsystem Reset.
**Note**: If SHST ≠ 00b, RDY cannot be set to '1' without an NVM Subsystem Reset (if CSTS.ST = '1') or until controller shutdown stops and SHST is cleared (if CSTS.ST = '0'). | | **01** | RO | HwInit | **Controller Fatal Status (CFS)**: '1' = fatal error occurred (not communicated via completion queue). Cleared to '0' when no error. Set to '1' on fatal error during initialization. | | **00** | RO | 0b | **Ready (RDY)**: '1' = controller ready to process commands after CC.EN = '1'. Cleared to '0' when CC.EN = '0'. Commands must not be submitted until RDY = '1'.
**Notes**:
- RDY cannot be set to '1' without an NVM Subsystem Reset if SHST = `01b` or `10b` and CSTS.ST = '1'.
- RDY cannot be set to '1' until controller shutdown completes and SHST = 00b if CSTS.ST = '0'.
- Undefined behavior if host submits commands without required CLR or reset sequence. | > **Note**: During a Controller Level Reset, intermediate values may occur before the register settles to its reset state.

sections.title: Offset_20h_NSSR_–_NVM_Subsystem_Reset
sections.summary:
### 3.1.4.7 Offset 20h: NSSR – NVM Subsystem Reset

This optional property enables the host to initiate an NVM Subsystem Reset. Support is indicated by the **CAP.NSSRS** field. If not supported, the address range is reserved.

#### Table 1: Table_3_1_4_7_Offset_20h_NSSR_NVM_Subsystem_Reset

| Bits   | Type | Reset | Description |
|--------|------|-------|-------------|
| 31:00  | RW   | 0h    | **NVM Subsystem Reset Control (NSSR)**: Writing `4E564D65h` ("NVM") initiates an NVM Subsystem Reset. Any other write value has no effect. Reading this field returns `0h`. |

sections.title: Offset_24h_AQA_–_Admin_Queue_Attributes
sections.summary:
### 3.1.4.8 Offset_24h_AQA – Admin Queue Attributes

**Section ID:** 3.1.4.8 | **Page:** 89-89

This section defines attributes for the **Admin Submission Queue** and **Admin Completion Queue**, both using **Queue Identifier 0h**. These queues are required to be in **physically contiguous memory**. The Admin Submission Queue’s priority is determined by the arbitration mechanism (see Section 3.4.4). These attributes **are not reset** by a Controller Level Reset.

> **Note:** Hosts should use UEFI during boot. In low-memory environments (e.g., Option ROMs in legacy BIOS), sufficient memory for queues may not be available; low memory operation is vendor-specific.

---

#### Table 1: Table_3_1_4_8_Offset_24h_AQA_Admin_Queue_Attributes

| Bits | Type | Reset | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:28 | RO | 0h | Reserved |
| 27:16 | RW | 0h | **Admin Completion Queue Size (ACQS):** Size in entries (0's based). Minimum: **2 entries**, Maximum: **4,096 entries**. Enabling controller with 0 disables undefined behavior. (See Section 3.3.3.1.1) |
| 15:12 | RO | 0h | Reserved |
| 11:00 | RW | 0h | **Admin Submission Queue Size (ASQS):** Size in entries (0's based). Minimum: **2 entries**, Maximum: **4,096 entries**. Enabling controller with 0 disables undefined behavior. (See Section 3.3.3.1.1) |

sections.title: Offset_28h_ASQ_–_Admin_Submission_Queue_Base_Addr
sections.summary:
# 3.1.4.9 Offset 28h: ASQ – Admin Submission Queue Base Address

Defines the base memory address of the Admin Submission Queue. This property is not reset by a Controller Level Reset initiated by a Controller Reset.

### Table 1: Table_3_1_4_9_Offset_28h_ASQ_Admin_Submission_Queue_Base_Address

| Bits  | Type | Reset | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 63:12 | RW   | Impl Spec | **Admin Submission Queue Base (ASQB):** Specifies the 52 most significant bits of the 64-bit physical address for the Admin Submission Queue. Address must be memory page aligned (based on CC-MPS). All Admin commands (e.g., I/O Submission/Completion Queue creation) are submitted to this queue. ### **Section 3.1.4.14: Offset 44h: BPRSEL – Boot Partition Read Select**

This optional property enables the host to read data from the Boot Partition (defined in Section 8.1.3) by transferring it to the Boot Partition Memory Buffer. If the controller does not support Boot Partitions, this property must be cleared to `0h`.
