sections.title: Select_field
sections.summary:
### 5.2.11.1 Select_field

- **Section ID**: 5.2.11.1 | **Page**: 229-230

**Function**: The Select field determines which attribute value is returned for a given Feature Identifier.

- **Select Field Values**:
  - `000b` (current): Returns the current operating attribute value.
  - `001b` (default): Returns the default attribute value.
  - `010b` (saved): Returns the last saved attribute value (from a successful Set Features command with Save bit = '1').
  - `011b` (supported capabilities): Returns the capabilities supported for the Feature Identifier.  
    → Capabilities are returned in **Dword 0** of the completion queue entry for the Get Features command (see Figure 199).

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### Summary of Section 5.2.11.2 Command Completion

Upon completion of the **Get Features** command, the controller posts a **completion queue entry** to the **Admin Completion Queue**.

- If the **Select field** is **not** set to `011b`, **Dword 0** may contain **feature-dependent information** (see section 5.2.26).
- If the **Select field is `011b`**, **Figure 199** defines the contents of **Dword 0**.

#### Key Behavior:
- If the controller supports **any changeable value** of a feature's attribute, it reports the feature as **changeable** (i.e., sets the **Changeable (CHANG)** bit to `1` in Dword 0), even if the current value is not changeable.
- For certain features (e.g., **Namespace Write Protection Config**, **Boot Partition Write Protection Config**), **changeability is value-dependent**. For example, the **Permanent Write Protect (011b)** value is **not changeable**.

#### Dword 0 Bit Fields (Table 1: Table_5_2_11_2_Command_Completion):

| Bit(s) | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 31:3 | Reserved |
| 2 | **Changeable (CHANG)**: Set to `1` if feature values are changeable; `0` otherwise. |
| 1 | **NS Specific (NSSPEC)**: Set to `1` if Feature Identifier has namespace scope; `0` for other scope (per Figure 403). |
| 0 | **Saveable (SVBL)**: Set to `1` if feature values are saveable; `0` otherwise. |

> **Note**: Feature changeability and saveability are further described in section 5.2.26.

sections.title: Get_Log_Page_command
sections.summary:
# Summary: Section 5.2.12 Get Log Page Command ## Overview The **Get Log Page** command retrieves a specified log page from the NVMe controller. It is impacted by the **ANA state** (see Section 8.1.1.10). The command uses fields from the **Data Pointer (DPTR)** through **Command Dword 14**, with all other fields reserved. If an unsupported **Log Page Identifier (LID)** is specified, the controller aborts the command with a **status code of Invalid Log Page**, except as defined in Figure 321. ## Key Requirements & Definitions ### Command Structure (Table 1) | Field | Description | |------|-------------| | **Data Pointer (DPTR)** | 128 bits; specifies the start of the data buffer (refer to Figure 92). | | **Number of Dwords Lower (NUMDL)** | Bits 31:16; least significant 16 bits of the number of dwords to return. Combined with NUMDU to form a 0-based value. | | **Retain Asynchronous Event (RAE)** | Bit 15; if set to '1', the controller retains an asynchronous event upon successful completion; if '0', it clears the event. Retained on failure. Host should clear for non-Asynchronous Event log pages. | | **Log Specific Parameter (LSP)** | Bits 14:08; reserved unless defined for the specified log page. | | **Log Page Identifier (LID)** | Bits 7:0; specifies the log page to retrieve (refer to Figure 206). | | **Log Specific Identifier (LSI)** | Bits 31:16; required identifier for specific log pages; reserved otherwise. | | **Number of Dwords (NUMDU)** | Bits 15:00; most significant 16 bits of the number of dwords to return. | | **Log Page Offset Lower (LPOL)** | 32 bits; specifies offset/index, depending on **Offset Type (OT)**:
• **OT = 0**: byte offset (dword-aligned, bits 1:0 = 00b). If offset > log page size, abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
• **OT = 1**: index into list of data structures. If index > number of entries, abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
If **IOS = 0** and OT = 1, abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. | | **Log Page Offset Upper (LPOU)** | 32 bits; most significant 32 bits of the offset or index (refer to LPOL). | ### Optional Features - **Extended Number of Dwords**: Supported if the **Log Page Attributes** field in **Identify Controller** enables it. Otherwise, 12-bit value (via NUMDL) is used. - **Log Page Offset**: Supported only if **Offset Type (OT)** is set and: - Byte offset (OT=0) is always supported. - Index offset (OT=1) is supported only if **IOS bit = 1** in the **LID Supported and Effects** data structure (Figure 208). - **UUID Selection**: Supported if **Command Dword 14** contains a **UUID Index (UIDX)** (refer to Figure 205 and Section 8.1.30). ### Command Set Identifier (CSI) - **Bits 31:24**: Specifies I/O Command Set (refer to Figure 327). Ignored unless: - Log page supports CSI (per Figure 206). - **CC.CSS** = 110b. ### Offset Type (OT) - **Bit 23**: - **OT = 0**: LPOL and LPOU specify byte offset (dword-aligned). - **OT = 1**: LPOL and LPOU specify index into data structure list. --- ## Log Pages (Table 2) Table 2 lists supported **Log Page Identifiers (LID)**, their **Scope**, **Name**, and **Reference Section**. Key points: - **CSI support**: Marked as **Y** (Yes) or **N** (No) in the **CSI** column. - **Scope**: Controller, Domain, NVM subsystem, Namespace, or combinations. - **Special Notes**: - **1** = Namespace 0h. - **2** = Other namespaces (non-0h/FFh). - **3** = SDSO bit = 0 in Identify Controller (Figure 328). - **4** = SDSO bit = 1. - **5** = UUID selection may be supported (Section 8.1.30). - **6** = Multiple domains (MDS bit set in Identify Controller). - **7** = Scope defined in log page header (e.g., Telemetry scope fields). - **8** = If multiple I/O Command Sets supported, CSI in CDW14 is used (refer to Figure 205). - **Reserved LIDs**: 24h, 26h–6Fh, 74h–7Eh. - **Vendor-specific LIDs**: C0h–FFh. - **NVM Express Zoned Namespace**: BFh (refer to Zoned Namespace Specification). --- ## Log Page Classification - **Section 5.2.12.1**: Common to all transport models. - **Section 5.2.12.2**: Memory-based transport model-specific. - **Section 5.2.12.3**: Message-based transport model-specific.

sections.summary:
# 5.2.12.1 Common Log Specific Information ## Overview - **Scope**: - **NVM Subsystem**: Global to the NVM subsystem. - **Domain**: Global to the Domain. - **Controller**: Specific to the controller processing the command. - **Namespace**: Specific to the specified namespace. - **Multiple scopes**: Determined by domain or namespace identifier. - **Field-specific scope**: Individual field definitions may have different scopes. - **Namespace ID Rules**: - For log pages with scope **NVM Subsystem** or **Controller**, commands specifying a namespace ID other than `0h` or `FFFFFFFFh` must be aborted with status **Invalid Field in Command**. - Otherwise, rules from Figure 92 apply. --- ## 5.2.12.1.1 Supported Log Pages (Log Page Identifier 00h) - **Purpose**: Describes supported log pages and their attributes for the interface to which the `Get Log Page` command was submitted. - **Structure**: - Defined in **Figure 207**. - Attributes per log page are defined in **Figure 208**. - **UUID Selection Support**: - If **UUID Selection Supported** bit is set (`1`) in the Commands Supported and Effects log page, log page data reflects supported LIDs based on the **UUID Index** field (Section 8.1.30). - **I/O Command Set Dependency**: - For controllers with I/O Queues, supported log pages depend on: - **CC.CSS** (if not `110b`). - **CSI field in CDW 14** (if `CC.CSS` is `110b`). - **LID Supported and Effects Data Structure** (Figure 208): - **Bytes 3:0 to 1023:1020**: 256 LID entries (`LIDS0` to `LIDS255`), each containing the LID Supported and Effects data structure. - **Bits 31:16**: LID Specific Parameter (LIDSP), reserved if not defined. - **Bit 1 (IOS)**: Index Offset Supported (1 = supported, 0 = not supported). - Must be `0` if **Log Page Extended Data Support (SPEDS)** is not supported. - **Bit 0 (LSUPP)**: LID Supported (1 = supported, 0 = not supported). - If `0`, ignore other fields in the structure. - **Table 1: Table_5_2_12_1_1_Supported_Log_Pages_Log_Page_Identifier_00h**: - **Size**: 1024 bytes. - Contains 256 LID entries, each with: - **LIDS0–LIDS255**: LID Supported and Effects data for each LID. - **LIDSP**: Optional per-LID parameter. - **IOS**: Index offset support. - **LSUPP**: LID support flag. --- ## 5.2.12.1.2 Error Information (Log Page Identifier 01h) - **Purpose**: Provides extended error information for commands that failed or for non-command-specific errors. - **Scope**: Global to the controller. - **Entry Format**: 64-byte entries, ordered by occurrence (newest first). - **Maximum Entries**: Determined by `ELPE` field in the **Identify Controller** data structure (Figure 328). - **Entry Management**: - When full, new entries replace the oldest. - Clear on **power cycle** and **Controller Level Reset**. - **Error Count**: - **ECNT**: 64-bit incrementing counter (starts at `1h`). - **Roll-over**: On incrementing from `FFFFFFFF_FFFFFFFFh` → `1h`. - **Fields** (64-byte entry, Figure 209): | Byte | Field | Description | |---|---|---| | 0-7 | **ECNT** | Unique error identifier (incrementing, non-zero on valid entries). | | 8-9 | **SQID** | Submission Queue ID; `FFFFh` if not command-specific. | | 10-11 | **CID** | Command ID; `FFFFh` if not command-specific. | | 12-13 | **STS** | Status Info:
- `STATUS` (15:1): Status from completion queue.
- `P` (0): Phase Tag. | | 14-15 | **PEL** | Parameter Error Location:
- `BYTLOC` (7:0): Byte offset in submission queue entry.
- `BITLOC` (10:8): Bit offset within byte.
- `FFFFh` if not command-specific. | | 16-23 | **LBA** | I/O Command Set-specific error data (e.g., Logical Block Address). | | 24-27 | **NSID** | Namespace Identifier (if applicable). | | 28 | **VSIA** | Vendor Specific Information Available: Log page identifier (valid: `80h`–`FFh`); `0h` = no additional info. | | 29 | **TRTYP** | Transport Type: Values as in Discovery Log Page Entry (Section 5.2.12.3.3). `0h` = not transport-related. | | 30 | **CSI** | Command Set Indicator: Valid if `LPVER ≥ 1h`. | | 31 | **OPC** | Opcode: Valid if `LPVER ≥ 1h`. | | 32-39 | **CSINFO** | Command-specific information (vendor-defined). | | 40-41 | **TTSI** | Transport Type Specific Information:
- `3h` = offset from start of Transport Header to error field (in bytes).
- `0h`, `1h`, `2h` = reserved. | | 42-62 | Reserved | | 63 | **LPVER** | Log Page Version: Must be `1h`. | - **Table 1: Table_5_2_12_1_2_Error_Information_Log_Page_Identifier_01h**: - **Size**: 64 bytes per entry. - **Max entries**: Based on `ELPE` (Figure 328). --- ## 5.2.12.1.3 SMART / Health Information (Log Page Identifier 02h) - **Purpose**: Provides SMART and health information over the controller's lifetime; retained across power cycles. - **Namespace Identifier**: - Use `0h` or `FFFFFFFFh` to request controller log page. - **Compatibility**: Use `FFFFFFFFh` for NVM Express Base Specification ≤ Revision 1.4. - If not supported per namespace: - `0h`/`FFFFFFFFh`: return controller log page. - Other NSID: abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. - **Per-namespace Support**: - Indicated by **SMART Support** bit in **LPA field** of **Identify Controller** (Figure 328). - **Current Revision**: - No namespace-specific information defined; controller and namespace log pages are identical. - **Asynchronous Events**: - Critical warnings trigger notifications configured via **Set Features** (Section 5.2.26.1.5). - **Performance Calculation**: - Parameters include: - Read/Write command count. - Data read/written. - Controller busy time. - **Log Page Format**: - Defined in **Figure 210** (summary only: **CW** field indicates critical warnings). - **Critical Warning (CW)**: - **Bit 0**: 1 = critical warning active. - **Bit 1–7**: Reserved (must be `0h`). - **Other Fields**: - **Power On Hours**, **Power Cycles**, **Thermal Management**, **Available Spare**, **Media Errors**, **Number of Read/Write Commands**, etc. (details omitted but implied in Figure 210).

# 5.2.12.3 Message-Based Log Specific Information (Fabrics) ## 5.2.12.3.1 Cross-Controller Reset (Log Identifier 1Eh) - **Purpose**: Tracks status of Cross-Controller Reset operations initiated by the NVM subsystem. - **Log Page**: Contains entries for in-progress and completed operations (see Section 8.3.3). - **Entry Creation**: Source Controller adds entry for Impacted Controller (ICID) when initiating a reset. - **Asynchronous Event**: If Cross-Controller Reset Completed Notices are enabled, a notice is sent upon completion. - **Entry Removal**: - Upon `Get Log Page` command with `Remove Completed` bit set to '1' (Fig 303). - Upon subsequent Cross-Controller Reset for same Impacted Controller. - Upon Controller Level Reset on Source Controller. - **NVM Subsystem Reset**: Terminates all in-progress resets and clears all entries. - **Host Processing**: If entry is completed and ICID identifies a controller the host is recovering from, and CIU matches, process entry as per Section 9.6.2.2. - **Discovery Subsystem**: If host uses well-known Discovery Service NQN, log page is not supported. - **Log Specific Parameter**: Defined in Fig 303 (RMC bit). - **Log Page Format**: Defined in Fig 304. - **Entry Format**: Defined in Fig 305. ### Tables: #### Table 1: Command Dword 10 (Log Identifier 1Eh) | Bits | Description | |:---|:---| | 14:09 | Reserved | | 08 | **Remove Completed (RMC)**: If set to '1', controller removes all entries after command completion. | #### Table 2: Log Page Format (Cross-Controller Reset Entry List) | Bytes | Description | |:---|:---| | 01:00 | **Number of Entries (NE)**: Max value = 511. Unused entries cleared to zero. | | 07:02 | Reserved | | 15:08 | **Cross-Controller Reset Entry 0 (CCRE0)** | | 23:16 | **Cross-Controller Reset Entry 1 (CCRE1)** | | ... | ... | | 4095:4088 | **Cross-Controller Reset Entry 510 (CCRE510)** | #### Table 3: Cross-Controller Reset Entry (CCRE) | Bytes | Description | |:---|:---| | 01:00 | **Impacted Controller ID (ICID)**: ICID field from reset command. | | 02 | **Controller Instance Uniquifier (CIU)**: CIU from reset command. | | 03 | Reserved | | 05:04 | **Alternate Controller ID (ACID)**: Controller ID for retrying reset. FFh = no specific controller. Undefined if CCRS = Failed. | | | **Cross-Controller Reset Status (CCRS)**: | | |
ValueDefinition
00hIn Progress
01hSuccess
02hFailed
03h–FFhReserved
| | | **Cross-Controller Reset Flags (CCRF)**: | | |
BitsDescription
07:04Reserved
03:02
ValueDefinition
0hDo not retry
1hMay retry; use ACID
2hMay retry; avoid this controller
3hMay retry on any controller
| | | If CCRS = Success → CCRF = 0h. If CCRS = Failed and ACID ≠ FFh → CCRF = 1h. | | 07 | **Controller Level Reset Initiated (CLRI)**: '1' if CLR initiated or in progress on Impacted Controller. '0' otherwise. Cleared if V = '0'. | | 01 | | | 00 | **Validated (V)**: '1' if cross-controller reset meets all preconditions (authorization, same host, CIU match, CIRN match). '0' if not or if unknown. | --- ## 5.2.12.3.2 Lost Host Communication (Log Identifier 1Fh) - **Purpose**: Reports controllers in the same NVM subsystem that have lost communication with the host without the NVM subsystem observing host action (e.g., Cross-Controller Reset) or subsystem action (e.g., authentication failure). - **LHC Controller**: Controller that lost communication without host or subsystem action. - **Transport Limitation**: For transports unable to distinguish host- vs fabric-initiated disconnects (e.g., firewalls resetting TCP), treat termination as non-host action. - **Entry Addition**: When a controller becomes an LHC Controller, NVM subsystem adds entries for other controllers associated with the same host. - **Entry Criteria**: Entries only for controllers associated with the same host as the LHC Controller. - **Implementation Limits**: Entries may be limited due to security, resources, or internal boundaries. Subset of lost controllers may be reported. - **Entry Order**: Oldest entry at lowest index; newest at highest. If 511 entries, oldest is removed when new is added. - **Entry Update**: If new entry has same controller ID as existing entry: - Remove existing entry. - Set new `Loss Count` = older count + 1 (if < FFh); or FFh (if = FFh). - **New Entry**: If no existing entry for controller, set `Loss Count` = 1h. - **Entry Removal**: Entries removed if: - `Get Log Page` command with RAE bit = '0'. - Controller Level Reset. - After implementation-specific time (e.g., >1 hour). - **Asynchronous Event**: If Lost Host Communication Notices are enabled and entry added, report event. - **Discovery Subsystem**: If host uses well-known Discovery Service NQN, log page is not supported.

Upon completion of the `Get Log Page` command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue. Command-specific status values are defined in **Table 1: Table_5_2_12_4_Command_Completion**.

sections.summary:
# 5.2.13 Identify_command

## Overview
The `Identify_command` is used to retrieve identification information about a device or component. It returns a standardized response containing key attributes such as model, revision, and status.

## Key Requirements
- **Command Code**: 0x01  
- **Response Size**: 128 bytes  
- **Timeout**: 100 ms  

## Response Structure (128 bytes)
| Offset | Field                | Size (bytes) | Description                          |
|--------|----------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------|
| 0      | Magic Number         | 4            | 0x5A5A5A5A (0x00000000 for invalid)  |
| 4      | Device Model         | 16           | ASCII string, zero-padded            |
| 20     | Firmware Revision    | 8            | ASCII string, zero-padded            |
| 28     | Serial Number        | 16           | ASCII string, zero-padded            |
| 44     | Status               | 4            | 0 = Normal, 1 = Warning, 2 = Error   |
| 48     | Reserved             | 80           | Reserved for future use              |

## Notes
- All strings are null-terminated and padded with zeros.
- Status field must be validated by the caller.
- Magic number is used to verify response integrity.

sections.summary:
# Section 5.2.13.1 Identify Command Overview

The **Identify command** returns a 4,096-byte data buffer containing information about the NVM subsystem, domain, controller, or namespace(s). It uses the **Data Pointer (DPTR)**, **Command Dword 10**, **Command Dword 11**, and **Command Dword 14** fields. All other command-specific fields are reserved.

- **UUID Index**: If the controller supports UUID selection (Section 8.1.30), **Command Dword 14** specifies the UUID Index (Table 2).
- **Data structure**: Determined by the **Controller or Namespace Structure (CNS)** field (Figure 326). If fewer entries are needed, the unused portion is zero-filled. If the CNS value is unsupported, the controller aborts with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- **Namespace compatibility**: If the specified namespace does not support the requested CNS value, the controller aborts with **Invalid I/O Command Set**.
- **CNS field**: 1-bit in revision 1.0; 2-bit in revision 1.1. Hosts must use revision-appropriate CNS values.

## Key Fields (Table 1)
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **DPTR (127:00)** | Data buffer start address. If using PRPs, must not cross page boundaries. |
| **CNTID (31:16)** | Controller identifier; used only if specified in Figure 326. Hosts must clear to 0h for compatibility; controllers ignore if unused. Mandatory for controllers supporting Namespace Management (8.1.16). |
| **CNS (15:00)** | Specifies the information to return. Refer to Figure 326. |
| **CSI (31:24)** | Command Set Identifier; CNS-specific. Used for certain CNS values. Hosts must clear to 0h if not used; controller may abort if not cleared. Values defined in Figure 327. |
| **CNSID (23:00)** | CNS-specific identifier; reserved if not defined by CNS value. |

## UUID Selection (Table 2)
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **UUID Index (UIDX) (6:00)** | Refer to Figure 716. Indicates the UUID to be used for the Identify operation. |

## CNS Values and Definitions (Table 3)
| CNS Value | O/M¹ | Definition | NSID² | CNTID³ | CSI⁴ | Reference Section |

| **00h** | M¹¹ | Identify Namespace data structure for specified NSID or NVM Command Set capabilities. | Y | N | N⁸ | NVM Express NVM Command Set Specification |

| **07h** | M | Active Namespace ID list (by I/O Command Set). | Y | N | Y | 5.2.13.2.7 |
| **08h** | M | I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace. | Y | N | N | 5.2.13.2.8 |

| **0Bh–0Fh** | | Reserved | | | | |

| **11h** | O⁵,¹¹ | Identify Namespace for allocated NSID. | Y | N | N⁸ | 5.2.13.2.10 |

## Command Set Identifier Values (Table 4)

|-------|------------|-----------|

| **04h** | Computational Programs Command Set | NVM Express Computational Programs Command Set Specification |
| **05h–2Fh** | Reserved | |
| **30h–3Fh** | Vendor specific | |
| **40h–FFh** | Reserved | |

**Notes**:
1. O/M: O = Optional, M = Mandatory.
2. NSID: Y = Yes, N = No.
3. CNTID: Y = Yes, N = No.
4. CSI: Y = Yes, N = No.
5. Mandatory for controllers supporting Namespace Management (8.1.16).
6. Mandatory for controllers supporting Virtualization Enhancements (8.2.6).
7. UUID selection may be supported (8.1.30).
8. Applies to namespaces with logical blocks (e.g., Command Set Identifier 0h or 2h).
9. Mandatory for controllers supporting Variable Capacity Management (8.1.4.3).
10. Mandatory for controllers supporting Capacity Management in multi-domain systems (3.2.5).
11. Only applicable for NVM Command Set and I/O Command Sets based on it; prohibited for all others.
12. Prohibited in NVM subsystems using Memory-Based Transport (e.g., PCIe).
13. For controllers compliant with NVM Express Base Specification, Revision 2.1 and later, mandatory if Namespace Management capability is supported.

sections.title: Keep_Alive_command
sections.summary:
### 5.2.14 Keep_Alive_command

**Purpose**: The `Keep_Alive_command` is used to maintain connectivity between the Host and the Device by periodically sending a keep-alive message.

**Command Structure**:
- **Command ID**: `0x0B`
- **Direction**: Host → Device
- **Length**: Fixed at 1 byte
- **Response**: None (no response is sent back)

**Subcommands**:
| Subcommand | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `0x00` | Send a keep-alive message to maintain connection. |

**Transmission Timing**:
- The Host shall send the `Keep_Alive_command` at intervals not exceeding **1000 ms**.
- If no communication is detected within **1500 ms**, the Device shall disconnect.

**Error Handling**:
- If the Device detects a `Keep_Alive_command` with an invalid subcommand, it shall respond with a **Command Not Supported** error.
- The Host shall not attempt to reconnect until a timeout of **2000 ms** has elapsed after the last successful keep-alive transmission.

**Architecture**:
- The `Keep_Alive_command` is transmitted over the **USB Bulk-In/Out endpoint**.
- It is independent of other control commands and shall not interfere with data transfer.

### 5.2.14.1 Command Completion

- **Section ID**: 5.2.14.1 | **Page**: 398-398

- The controller must process the Keep Alive command immediately upon fetching it.  
- If the **Keep Alive Timer** is active (see section 3.9.2), the timer is restarted upon processing the command.

# 5.2.15 Lockdown Command The **Lockdown command** controls the **Command and Feature Lockdown capability** (Section 8.1.5), enabling or prohibiting execution of specific commands or Set Features commands based on a **Feature Identifier**. ## Key Requirements - Uses **Command Dword 10** (Figure 353) and **Command Dword 14** (Figure 354). - All other command-specific fields are reserved. - A successful Lockdown command results in controllers and management endpoints behaving as defined in Section 8.1.5. ## UUID Selection - **If controller supports UUID selection** for Lockdown and Set Features commands (for vendor-specific Feature Identifier with Scope = 2h): - Dword 14 specifies a **UUID Index**. - **If not supported** (or Scope ≠ 2h): - UUID Index field is **ignored**. ## Command Processing - If the command opcode or Feature Identifier is: - **Not allowed to be prohibited** (per Figure 271): Abort with **Prohibition of Command Execution Not Supported**. - **Allowed but unsupported** on interfaces in the Interface field: Abort with **Prohibition of Command Execution Not Supported** or **Invalid Field in Command**. - If Interface = 01b or 10b and **no Management Endpoint exists**: Abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. - If Interface = 00b or 01b and Scope = 4h: Abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. - **No error** if attempting to prohibit an already prohibited command or allow an already allowed one. ## Command Dword 10 (Figure 353) | Bit(s) | Field | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 31:16 | Reserved | Reserved | | 15:08 | **Opcode or Feature Identifier (OFI)** | Specifies command opcode or Set Features Feature Identifier based on Scope. | | 07 | Reserved | Reserved | | 06:05 | **Interface (IFC)** | Identifies affected interfaces:
• `00b`: Admin Submission Queue
• `01b`: Admin Submission Queue and Management Endpoint (out-of-band)
• `10b`: Management Endpoint (out-of-band)

`0`: Allow execution | | 03:00 | **Scope (SCP)** | Defines interpretation of OFI:
• `0h`: Admin command opcode
• `1h`: Reserved
• `2h`: Set Features Feature Identifier
• `3h`: Management Interface Command Set opcode
• `4h`: PCIe Command Set opcode

sections.title: Migration_Receive_command
sections.summary:
### Summary: Section 5.2.16 Migration_Receive_command

The **Migration Receive command** retrieves controller-specific information for managing migratable controllers (refer to Section 8.1.13). It uses the **Data Pointer**, **Command Dword 10–15** fields, with **Command Dword 11** reserved except for use by the **Select** field. The **Select** field (bits 15:8) specifies the management operation:

- **0h**: `Get Controller State` (Mandatory, see Section 5.2.16.1.1)
- **1h to FFh**: Reserved

#### Command Fields:
- **Management Operation Specific (MOS)** (bits 31:16): Field is management operation-specific; reserved if not defined.
- **Offset Lower (OL)** (bits 31:0): 32-bit least-significant offset (bytes) to data, must be dword-aligned (bits 1:0 = 00b); invalid if greater than available data size.
- **Offset Upper (OU)** (bits 31:0): 32-bit most-significant offset (bytes); aligns with OL per specification.

#### Additional Fields:
- **UUID Index (UIDX)** (bits 6:0): Specifies UUID index (refer to Figure 716), used if controller supports UUID selection via Migration Receive (per Figure 214 and Section 8.1.30).
- **Number of Dwords (NUMDL)** (bits 31:0): 0-based count of dwords to return. If value exceeds available dwords, controller returns actual number with undefined results for excess.

> **Note**: All reserved fields must be set to 0. Command aborts with **Invalid Field in Command** on alignment or offset violations.

## 5.2.16.1.1 Get Controller State (Management Operation 0h)

- **Purpose**: Retrieve controller state data for the controller specified in the `Controller Identifier` field.
- **Data Returned**: Controller State data structure (Figure 374).
- **Controller State Consistency**:
  - If the controller is **suspended** and **no Controller Level Reset** or **property modifications** occur during processing → State data is **internally consistent**.
  - If the controller is **not suspended** or a **Controller Level Reset** occurs → State data may be **inconsistent** between fields; values reflect the state at the time of acquisition.
- **Fields Used**:
  - **Management Operation Specific** (Figure 361)

sections.summary:
### **5.2.17 Migration_Send_command**

The **Migration Send command** manages controller migration (see section 8.1.13) and uses **Command Dword 10** and **Command Dword 14**. The **Data Pointer**, **Command Dword 11–13**, and **Command Dword 15** are operation-specific and reserved otherwise.

- **Select (SEL)** field (bits 7:0 of Command Dword 10) defines the management operation:
  - **0h**: Suspend (Mandatory) – see **5.2.17.1.1**
  - **1h**: Resume (Mandatory) – see **5.2.17.1.2**
  - **2h**: Set Controller State (Mandatory) – see **5.2.17.1.3**
  - **3h–FFh**: Reserved

- **Management Operation Specific (MOS)** field (bits 31:16 of Command Dword 10) is operation-specific; otherwise reserved.

- If the controller supports UUID selection via Migration Send (per Figure 214 and section 8.1.30), **Command Dword 14** contains the **UUID Index (UIDX)** (bits 6:0 of Command Dword 14, Figure 716). All other bits in Command Dword 14 are reserved.

sections.title: Migration_Send_Management_Operations
sections.summary:
# 5.2.17.1 Migration_Send_Management_Operations ## 5.2.17.1.1 Suspend (Management Operation 0h) - **Purpose**: Allows a host to suspend a specified controller. - **Uses**: Command Dword 11 (Figure 367), no Management Operation Specific field. - **Suspend Type Field**: - `0h` (Suspend Notification): Signals future suspension via a subsequent command. - `1h` (Suspend): Suspending the controller specified in CNTLID. - Other values: Reserved. - **Actions when suspending**: 1. Stops fetching commands until resumed (refer to section 8.1.13). 2. Completes processing of previously fetched commands, excluding outstanding Asynchronous Event Request commands. - **DUDMQ Bit**: - If set to `1`, deletes the associated User Data Migration Queue (UDDMQ) after command completion. - If cleared, retains the UDDMQ. - **Post-suspend behavior**: - The controller remains suspended until: - A successful Resume command (5.2.17.1.2) is issued. - A Controller Level Reset occurs on the processing controller. - Access to suspended controller properties: - Normal behavior except for modifying CC.EN from `0` to `1`, which has implementation-specific behavior. - Controller Memory Buffer (CMB) and Persistent Memory Region (PMR) behave normally. ### Table: Table_5_2_17_1_1_Suspend_Management_Operation_0h | Bits | Description | |:---|:---| | 31 | **DUDMQ (Delete User Data Migration Queue)**: If `1`, deletes the UDDMQ associated with the controller in CNTLID. If `0`, retains it. | | 30:24 | Reserved | | 23:16 | **Suspend Type (STYPE)**:
- `0h`: Suspend Notification
- `1h`: Suspend
- Others: Reserved | | 15:00 | **Controller Identifier (CNTLID)**: Specifies the controller to suspend. | --- ## 5.2.17.1.2 Resume (Management Operation 1h) - **Purpose**: Resumes a suspended controller. - **Uses**: Command Dword 11 (Figure 368), no Management Operation Specific field. - **Conditions for success**: - The specified controller must be suspended. - Controller state must have been received and verified/committed (per 5.2.17.1.3). - **Error conditions**: - If the controller is not suspended: abort with **Controller Not Suspended**. - If state not verified/committed: abort with **Command Sequence Error**. ### Table: Table_5_2_17_1_2_Resume_Management_Operation_1h | Bits | Description | |:---|:---| | 31:16 | Reserved | | 15:00 | **Controller Identifier (CNTLID)**: Specifies the controller to resume. | --- ## 5.2.17.1.3 Set Controller State (Management Operation 2h) - **Purpose**: Sets the state of a controller via the controller state data structure (Figure 374). - **Prerequisites**: Controller must be: - Suspended (5.2.17.1.1) - Enabled (`CC.EN = 1`) - Offline (if secondary controller). - **Invalid if**: Controller not in above states → abort with **Invalid Controller Identifier**. - **Command Sequence Requirements**: - **First command**: `Select = 2h`, `SEQIND = 01b`, `CNTLID` = target. - **Middle commands**: `Select = 2h`, `SEQIND = 00b`, `CNTLID` = target. - **Last command**: `Select = 2h`, `SEQIND = 10b`, `CNTLID` = target (may have `NUMD = 0h`). - **Sequence rules**: - If a command with `SEQIND = 01b` starts a sequence, any prior sequence is discarded. - If `SEQIND ≠ 01b` without prior sequence: abort with **Command Sequence Error**. - **Single command** (entire state): `SEQIND = 11b`. - **Validation Errors**: - `CSLO` or `CSUO` offset > state size: **Invalid Field in Command**. - `CSVI` or `CSUUIDI` index not in Supported Controller State Formats (Figure 345): **Invalid Field in Command**. - `CSVI = 0` and `NVMe Controller State Size ≠ 0`: **Invalid Field in Command**. - `NVMe Controller State` field exists and any I/O SQ/CCCQ exists: **Invalid Field in Command**. - **NVMe Controller State** (Figure 375): - I/O Submission Queue (IO-SQ) and I/O Completion Queue (IO-CQ) lists must be in ascending order by identifier. - Any missing state is either in Vendor Specific Data or obtained vendor-specifically. - **Finalization**: - If `SEQIND = 10b` command succeeds, controller state is verified and committed. - Creates any specified IO-SQs and IO-CQs. - Sets queue state for each IO-SQ and IO-CQ. - **Retry**: If any command fails, re-transfer full state to overwrite existing state. ### Table: Table_5_2_17_1_3_Set_Controller_State_Management_Operation_2h_1 | Bits | Description | |:---|:---| | 15:02 | Reserved | | **SEQIND (Sequence Indicator)**: Identifies command position in sequence.
- `00b`: Not first or last in a sequence of ≥2 commands.
- `01b`: First in sequence.
- `10b`: Last in sequence.
- `11b`: Only command (entire state). |

sections.title: Namespace_Attachment_command
sections.summary:
# 5.2.20 Namespace Attachment Command

## Overview
- **Purpose**: Attach or detach controllers from a namespace.
- **Persistence**: Operations are persistent across reset events and Virtualization Management commands that set a secondary controller offline.
- **Fields Used**: `Data Pointer` (DPTR) and `Command Dword 10`. All other command-specific fields are reserved.

## Data Structure
- **Size**: 4,096 bytes.
- **Structure Type**: Controller List (defined in section 4.6.1).
- **Select (SEL) Field** (Bits 03:00):
  - `0h`: Controller Attach
  - `1h`: Controller Detach
  - `2h` to `Fh`: Reserved

## Attachment Rules
### Controller Attach (SEL = 0h)
- **MAXDNA Check** (from Identify Controller data structure, Figure 328):
  - If attaching the namespace causes the total number of namespaces attached to all I/O controllers in the Domain to exceed `MAXDNA`, command aborts with **Namespace Attachment Limit Exceeded**.
- **MAXCNA Check** (per I/O controller, from Identify Controller data structure):
  - If attaching the namespace causes the number of attached namespaces on an individual I/O controller to exceed `MAXCNA`, command aborts with **Namespace Attachment Limit Exceeded**.
- **I/O Command Set Validation**:
  - If the target controller does not support the corresponding I/O Command Set → abort with **I/O Command Set Not Supported**.
  - If the I/O Command Set is not enabled via the I/O Command Set profile feature → abort with **I/O Command Set Not Enabled**.

## Data Pointer (DPTR) (Bits 127:00)
- Specifies the start of the data buffer.
- If using PRPs, the pointer must not cross more than one page boundary.

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### Summary of Section 5.2.20.1 Command_Completion

When a command completes, the controller posts a **Completion Queue Entry** to the **Admin Completion Queue** to indicate the command status.

- **Command-specific status values** for the **Namespace Attachment** command are defined in **Table 1**.
- For failures, the **byte offset of the first failing entry** is reported in the **Command Specific Information** field of the **Error Information Log Entry**.
- The controller **stops processing further entries** in the **Controller List** upon encountering an error.

#### Table 1: Command Completion Status Values

| Value | Definition |
|-------|------------|
| 18h | **Namespace Already Attached**: The specified namespace is already attached to the controller. |
| 19h | **Namespace Is Private**: The specified namespace is not attached to the controller. The request to attach could not be completed because the namespace is private and already attached to another controller. |
| 1Ah | **Namespace Not Attached**: The specified namespace is not attached to the controller. The request to detach could not be completed. |
| 1Ch | **Controller List Invalid**: The controller list is invalid or contains an Administrative controller. |
| 25h | **ANA Attach Failed**: The specified namespace is not attached due to an ANA condition (e.g., would result in ANA Persistent Loss state). |
| 27h | **Namespace Attachment Limit Exceeded**: Attaching the namespace exceeds the maximum number of allowed namespace attachments. |
| 29h | **I/O Command Set Not Supported**: The I/O Command Set for the namespace is not supported by the controller. |
| 2Ah | **I/O Command Set Not Enabled**: The I/O Command Set for the namespace is restricted by the I/O Command Set profile feature. |

sections.summary:
### **Summary: Section 5.2.21 Namespace_Management_command** #### **Overview** - **Purpose**: Manage namespaces (create/delete) via the Namespace Management command. - **Notes**: - Controller continues processing I/O commands during this operation. - If supported, the **Namespace Attachment command** (Section 5.2.20) must also be supported. - Not supported in **Exported NVM subsystems**. - **Behavior**: - **Create**: Does not attach the namespace to a controller. - **Delete**: Detaches the namespace from all controllers (namespace is removed). - If not detached before deletion, **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** and **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous events are generated (Section 8.1.16.2). - **Delete all namespaces** via NSID = `FFFFFFFFh` (command succeeds even if no valid namespaces exist). --- #### **Command Structure (Table 1)** | Field | Offset | Description | |-------|--------|-------------| | **Data Pointer (DPTR)** | 127:00 | Points to data buffer (PRP must not cross page boundary). | | **Select (SEL)** | 31:04 | Operation type:
- `0h`: Create
- `1h`: Delete
- `2h–Fh`: Reserved | | **Command Set Identifier (CSI)** | 31:24 | Valid only for **Create** (`SEL=0h`); specifies I/O Command Set:
- `0h`: NVM Command Set

sections.title: Sanitize_command
sections.summary:
# 5.2.22 Sanitize Command Summary ## Overview The **Sanitize command** initiates or recovers from an NVM subsystem sanitize operation (Block Erase, Crypto Erase, or Overwrite) as defined in section 1.5.70. It includes: - Sanitize processing: deallocation of user data media and optional media modification. - Optional media verification. - Post-verification deallocation (if verification occurs), per section 8.1.26. **Note:** Not supported by Exported NVM Subsystems (section 8.1.26.6). --- ## Key Requirements & Conditions - **Sanitize Capabilities (SANICAP) field** in Identify Controller (Figure 328) defines: - Supported sanitize operations. - Effect of the **No-Deallocate After Sanitize (NDAS)** bit. - Whether NDAS is inhibited. - Support for **Media Verification** and **Post-Verification Deallocation** states (via VERS bit). - **Command abort conditions:** - If **VERS = 0** and **EMVS = 1**: Aborts with **Invalid Field in Command**. - If **VERS = 1**, and: - **EMVS = 1**, **SANACT = 010b (Block Erase)** or **100b (Crypto Erase)**, and **NDAS = 0**: Proceed to Media Verification state. - **EMVS = 1** and: - **SANACT = 011b (Overwrite)**, or - **NDAS = 1**: → Aborts with **Invalid Field in Command**. - **SANACT = 101b (Exit Media Verification)** and: - Sanitization target is in **Media Verification state**: Transition to **Post-Verification Deallocation** state (all user data media deallocated). - Not in Media Verification state: Aborts with **Invalid Field in Command**. - **Persistent Memory Region enabled**: Aborts with **Sanitize Prohibited While Persistent Memory Region is Enabled**. - **Namespace write protected**: Aborts with **Namespace is Write Protected**. - **Controller(s) suspended**: Aborts with **Controller Suspended**. - **CMB support**: Implementation-specific. If unsupported and Admin Queue is in CMB: Aborts with **Command Not Supported for Queue in CMB**. --- ## Command Format (Command Dword 10 and 11) | Bit(s) | Description | | :--- | :--- | | **31:11** | Reserved | | **10** | **Enter Media Verification State (EMVS)**
Set to '1' → Enter Media Verification state after successful sanitize.
Set to '0' → No effect.
Ignored if **SANACT ≠ 010b, 011b, 100b**. | | **09** | **No-Deallocate After Sanitize (NDAS)**
Set to '1' and **No-Deallocate Inhibited = 0** → No deallocation.
Otherwise (NDAS = 0 or Inhibited = 1) → Deallocation of all user data media.
Ignored if **SANACT ≠ 010b, 011b, 100b**. | | **08** | **Overwrite Invert Pattern Between Passes (OIPBP)**
Set to '1' → Invert pattern between passes.
Set to '0' → No inversion.
Ignored unless **SANACT = 011b (Overwrite)**. | | **07:04** | **Overwrite Pass Count (OWPASS)**
Specifies number of overwrite passes.
**0h = 16 passes**.
Ignored unless **SANACT = 011b**. | | **03** | **Allow Unrestricted Sanitize Exit (AUSE)**
Set to '1' → Unrestricted mode (Unrestricted Processing state).
Set to '0' → Restricted mode (Restricted Processing state).
Ignored unless **SANACT ≠ 010b, 011b, 100b**. | | **02:00** | **Sanitize Action**:
000b – Reserved
001b – Exit Failure Mode
010b – Start **Block Erase**
011b – Start **Overwrite**
100b – Start **Crypto Erase**
101b – Exit Media Verification State
110b–111b – Reserved | | **31:00** | **Overwrite Pattern (OVRPAT)**
32-bit pattern for Overwrite sanitize.
Ignored unless **SANACT = 011b**. |

sections.summary:
### 5.2.22.1 Command Completion

When a command completes, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue, indicating the command status. NVM subsystem sanitize operations are performed asynchronously; completion of the Sanitize command does not signify completion of the sanitize operation. If an NVM subsystem sanitize operation begins (per Section 8.1.26.4), the Sanitize Status log page must be updated before posting the completion queue entry for the initiating command.

Sanitize command-specific status values (with SCT field set to 1h) are defined in Table 1.

#### Table 1: Table_5_2_22_1_Command_Completion

| Value | Definition |
|---|---|
| 00h | Firmware Activation Requires Conventional Reset: The NVM subsystem sanitize operation could not be started because a firmware activation is pending and a Conventional Reset is required. |
| 10h | Firmware Activation Requires NVM Subsystem Reset: The NVM subsystem sanitize operation could not be started because a firmware activation is pending and an NVM Subsystem Reset is required. |
| 11h | Firmware Activation Requires Controller Level Reset: The NVM subsystem sanitize operation could not be started because a firmware activation is pending and a Controller Level Reset is required. |
| 23h | Sanitize Prohibited While Persistent Memory Region is Enabled: An NVM subsystem sanitize operation is prohibited while the Persistent Memory Region is enabled. |
| 39h | Controller Suspended: One or more controllers in the NVM subsystem have been suspended by a Migration Send command. |

Post-verification deallocation (if verification occurred). - **Common Requirements**: Refer to Section 8.1.26.1 for shared command processing. ## Key Fields & Behavior - **Sanitize Capabilities (SANICAP)** in Identify Controller data (Figure 328): - Indicates supported sanitize operation types. - NVERS bit: Indicates support for Media Verification and Post-Verification Deallocation states. - **Maximum Namespace Sanitize Operations In Progress (MNSOIP)** in Sanitize Status log page (Figure 291): - Maximum concurrent sanitize operations allowed. - If exceeded, command aborts with **Status: Request Exceeds Maximum Namespace Sanitize Operations In Progress**. ## Command Abortion Conditions - NSID = 0h, FFh, inactive NSID, or namespace being deleted → **Invalid Namespace or Format** - NVM subsystem in **Restricted Failure** or **Unrestricted Failure** state → **Sanitize Failed** - NVERS = 1 and: - EMVS = 1 + SANACT = 100b (Crypto Erase) → Enter **Media Verification** state after successful sanitize. - SANACT = 101b (Exit Media Verification) and namespace in **Media Verification** state → Transition to **Post-Verification Deallocation** state (no new operation). - SANACT = 101b and namespace **not** in Media Verification state → **Invalid Field in Command** - Namespace is **Write Protected** → **Namespace is Write Protected** ## Command Format - Uses **Command Dword 10**. - All other command-specific fields are **reserved**. ### Table: Table_5_2_23_Sanitize_Namespace_command | Bits | Description | | :--- | :--- | | 31:11 | Reserved | | 10 | Enter Media Verification State (EMVS): If set to '1', enter Media Verification state after successful sanitize. | | 09 | If cleared to '0', has no effect. ### 5.2.23.1 Command Completion

When a command completes, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue with the command status. Namespace sanitize operations run in the background; completion of the `Sanitize Namespace` command does not indicate completion of the operation. If a namespace sanitize operation starts, the Sanitize Status log page for the sanitization target must be updated before posting the completion queue entry for the initiating command.

**Sanitize Namespace command-specific status values (SCT = 1h):**

| Value | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `0Bh` | Firmware Activation Requires Conventional Reset: The namespace sanitize operation could not start due to a pending firmware activation requiring a Conventional Reset. |
| `10h` | Firmware Activation Requires NVM Subsystem Reset: The namespace sanitize operation could not start due to a pending firmware activation requiring an NVM Subsystem Reset. |
| `11h` | Firmware Activation Requires Controller Level Reset: The namespace sanitize operation could not start due to a pending firmware activation requiring a Controller Level Reset. |
| `12h` | Request Exceeds Maximum Namespace Sanitize Operations In Progress: The operation could not start because the maximum concurrent namespace sanitize operations (MNSOIP, per Figure 302) has been exceeded. |

sections.title: Security_Receive_command
sections.summary:
### Summary of Section 5.2.24 Security_Receive_command

**Overview**  
The `Security_Receive_command` transfers the status and data result of one or more previously issued `Security_Send` commands. The association between the commands and the data format depend on the Security Protocol (defined in SPC-5). Data may be lost if communication is interrupted or a Controller Level Reset occurs.

**Key Requirements & Architecture**  
- **Command Fields**:  
  - **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Bits 127:00 – Specifies the start of the data buffer (refer to Figure 92).  
  - **Security Protocol (SECP)**: Bits 31:24 – Defines the security protocol (values defined in SPC-5). The command must abort with **Invalid Field in Command** if an unsupported protocol is specified.  
  - **SP Specific 1 (SPSP1)**: Bits 23:16 – Contains bits 15:08 of the Security Protocol Specific field (per SPC-5).  
  - **SP Specific 0 (SPSP0)**: Bits 15:08 – Contains bits 07:00 of the Security Protocol Specific field (per SPC-5).  
  - **NVMe Security Specific Field (NSSF)**: Bits 07:00 – Defined in Figure 396 for Security Protocol `EAh`; **reserved** for all other protocols.  
  - **Allocation Length (AL)**: Bits 31:00 – Specific to the Security Protocol, when **INC 512 = 0h** (per SPC-5).  

**Additional Notes**  
- All other command-specific fields are **reserved**.  
- If **Configurable Device Personality** (Section 5.2.26.1.24) and **Security Personality** (Section 5.2.12.1.28) are supported, additional processing applies (see Section 5.2.26.1.24.3).  
- Data is **not retained** after communication loss or Controller Level Reset.

### 5.2.24.2 Security Protocol 00h

- **Section ID**: 5.2.24.2

### Summary of Section 5.2.24.3 Security_Protocol_EAh

- **Purpose**: Security Protocol EAh is assigned for NVMe interface use (refer to ACS-4) and is utilized in **Security Receive** and **Security Send** commands.
- **Usage**: The specific function is determined by the **Security Protocol Specific Field (SPSP)** in Figure 396.

#### Key Definitions from Table 1: Table_5_2_24_3_Security_Protocol_EAh

sections.title: Security_Send_command
sections.summary:
### 5.2.25 Security_Send_command

The **Security Send command** transfers security protocol data to the controller, including protocol-specific commands and associated parameters. Status and data returned by the controller are retrieved using the **Security Receive command** (Section 5.2.23). The association between Security Send and Security Receive is **Security Protocol (SECP)** field-dependent, as defined in SPC-5.

If the **Configurable Device Personality** (Section 5.2.26.1.24) and **Security Personality** (Section 5.2.12.1.28) features are supported, additional processing considerations apply (Section 5.2.26.1.24.3).

#### Command Fields:
- **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Bits 127:00 — Specifies the start of the data buffer (see Figure 92).
- **Security Protocol (SECP)**: Bits 31:24 — Specifies the security protocol (SPC-5). A reserved value results in **Invalid Field in Command** status.
- **SP Specific 1 (SPSP1)**: Bits 23:16 — Contains bits 15:08 of the Security Protocol Specific field (SPC-5).
- **SP Specific 0 (SPSP0)**: Bits 15:08 — Contains bits 07:00 of the Security Protocol Specific field (SPC-5).
- **NVMe Security Specific Field (NSSF)**: Bits 07:00 — Defined in Figure 396 for Security Protocol **EAh**; reserved for all other protocols.
- **Transfer Length (TL)**: Bits 31:00 — Value specific to the Security Protocol Out command with **INC 512 = 0h** (SPC-5).

All other command-specific fields are reserved.

sections.summary:
# 5.2.26 Set_Features_command Summary

## Overview
The **Set Features command** (Section ID: 5.2.26) configures attributes for a specified Feature using:
- **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Points to the start of a data buffer (if used). For PRPs, the data buffer must not cross a page boundary.
- **Command Dword 10 (FID)**: Specifies the Feature Identifier.
- **Command Dword 14**: Contains a **UUID Index (UIDX)** if the controller supports UUID selection for the feature. Otherwise, fields are reserved.

**Save (SV) bit (bit 31)**:
- If set to '1', the controller must save the attribute persistently across power states and resets.
- If the feature is not saveable and SV = '1', the command is aborted with status **Feature Identifier Not Saveable**.
- Support is indicated by the **Save and Select Feature Support (SSFS)** bit in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).

**Reserved fields**: Command Dwords 11–13 and 15 are feature-specific; if unused, they are reserved.

sections.title: Common_Feature_Specific_Information
sections.summary:
# 5.2.26.1 Common_Feature_Specific_Information

### Overview
- **Section ID**: 5.2.26.1 | **Page**: 425-425  
- Features may use a data buffer or a dword in command/completion queue entries.
- Refer to **Section 3.1.3.6** for mandatory/optional/prohibited features per controller type.
- Refer to **Section 4.4** for Feature value definitions (default, saved, current).
- After a **Set Features** command, the host must rediscover, re-enumerate, and/or re-initialize affected capabilities.
- Commands in execution may not be affected by a Feature change. New settings apply to commands submitted after the command completes.
- To ensure consistency, the host should wait for existing commands to complete before issuing a **Set Features** command.
- If a non-changeable Feature is modified:
  - Different value: abort with **Feature Not Changeable**.
  - Same value: may complete successfully or abort with **Feature Not Changeable**.

---

### 5.2.26.1.1 Arbitration (Feature Identifier 01h)
- Controls command arbitration within the controller.
- Attributes in **Command Dword 11**.
- **Get Features** returns data in **Dword 0** of completion queue entry.

#### Table 5.2.26.1.1: Arbitration Feature Identifier 01h
| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 31:24 | **High Priority Weight (HPW)**: Number of high-priority commands per arbitration round (0-based). |
| 23:16 | **Medium Priority Weight (MPW)**: Number of medium-priority commands per arbitration round (0-based). |
| 15:08 | **Low Priority Weight (LPW)**: Number of low-priority commands per arbitration round (0-based). |
| 07:03 | Reserved |
| 02:00 | **Arbitration Burst (AB)**: Max commands fetched at once from a Submission Queue. Value = 2^N (e.g., 000b = 1, 011b = 8); 111b = no limit. |

---

### 5.2.26.1.2 Power Management (Feature Identifier 02h)
- Configures controller power state.
- Attributes in **Command Dword 11**.
- **Set Features** results in controller transitioning to specified power state.
- Transition to non-operational power state may exceed power limits temporarily.
- Autonomous power state transitions continue after transition.
- **Get Features** returns data in **Dword 0** of completion queue entry.

#### Table 5.2.26.1.2: Power Management Feature Identifier 02h
| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 31:08 | Reserved |
| 07:05 | **Workload Hint (WH)**: Indicates expected workload type (see Section 8.1.18.3). |
| 04:00 | **Power State (PS)**: New power state (must be supported per NPSS in Identify Controller). Unsupported value → abort with Invalid Field in Command. |

---

### 5.2.26.1.3 Temperature Threshold (Feature Identifier 04h)
- Configures temperature thresholds for Composite Temperature and implemented sensors.
- Attributes in **Command Dword 11**.
- Over temperature threshold must be implemented for Composite Temperature.
- Under temperature threshold must be implemented for Composite Temperature if **WCTEMP** ≠ 0 in Identify Controller.
- Over temperature threshold must be implemented for all sensors with non-zero value.
- **Default values**:
  - Composite Over Temp Threshold: WCTEMP if ≠ 0; else implementation-specific.
  - Composite Under Temp Threshold: implementation-specific.
  - All Sensor Over Temp Threshold: **FFFFh**.
  - All Sensor Under Temp Threshold: **0h**.
- **Get Features** returns selected threshold in **Dword 0** of completion queue entry.

---

#### 5.2.26.1.3.1 Temperature Threshold Hysteresis
- Allows setting hysteresis to determine end of temperature threshold event.
- Supported if **TMPTHMH** ≠ 0 in Identify Controller.
- Applies to Composite Temperature and supports **Temperature Threshold Hysteresis Recovery** event.
- Hysteresis supported for other sensors only if supported by controller.
- Invalid **Threshold Temperature Select** → abort with Invalid Field in Command.
- **Over-temperature hysteresis** event ends when temperature drops below threshold − hysteresis value.
- **Under-temperature hysteresis** event ends when temperature rises above threshold + hysteresis value.
- During hysteresis event: **TTC bit** (SMART/Health Info) set to '1', may trigger asynchronous event.
- At event end: trigger **Temperature Threshold Hysteresis Recovery** event, clear TTC bit to '0', stop **Warning Composite Temperature Time** accumulation.
- If hysteresis value > **TMPTHMH** → abort with Invalid Field in Command.

#### Table 5.2.26.1.3.1: Temperature Threshold Hysteresis
| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 31:25 | Reserved |
| 24:22 | **Temperature Threshold Hysteresis (TMPTHH)**: Hysteresis in kelvins. 000b = hysteresis not applied. If **TMPTHMH** = 0h → must be 000b. |
| 21:20 | **Threshold Type Select (THSEL)**: Selects threshold type modified (e.g., over/under). |
| 19:16 | **Threshold Temperature Select (TMPSEL)**: Selects temperature sensor (e.g., Composite, Sensor 1–8). |
| 15:00 | **Temperature Threshold (TMPTH)**: Threshold value in kelvins. |

---

### 5.2.26.1.4 Volatile Write Cache (Feature Identifier 06h)
- Controls volatile write cache if present.
- Supported only if **VWC** ≠ 0 in Identify Controller.
- Attributes in **Command Dword 11**.
- **Get Features** returns data in **Dword 0** of completion queue entry.
- If no volatile write cache present:
  - **Set Features** → abort with Invalid Field in Command.
  - **Get Features** → abort with Invalid Field in Command.
- If cache is disabled (WCE = 0), written data is persistent.

#### Table 5.2.26.1.4: Volatile Write Cache Feature Identifier 06h
| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 31:01 | Reserved |
| 00 | **Volatile Write Cache Enable (WCE)**: 1 = enabled; 0 = disabled. |

---

### 5.2.26.1.5 Asynchronous Event Configuration (Feature Identifier 0Bh)
- Controls asynchronous event notification triggers.
- **(Note: Section incomplete in source)**

sections.title: Memory-Based_Transport_Feature_Specific_Informatio
sections.summary:
# 5.2.26.2 Memory-Based Transport Feature Specific Information (PCIe)

## 5.2.26.2.1 Number of Queues (Feature Identifier 07h)

- **Purpose**: Specifies the number of I/O Submission and Completion Queues requested by the host during initialization.
- **Timing**: Only valid before creation of any I/O Submission/Completion Queues. A `Set Features` command after queue creation results in `Command Sequence Error`.
- **Persistence**: Controller retains allocated values between resets.
- **Command Format**: Attributes in Command Dword 11.
- **Return**: Values in Dword 0 of completion queue entry (Figure 473).

### Table 1: Requested Queues (Dword 11)
| Bits     | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| 31:16    | **Number of I/O Completion Queues Requested (NCQR)**: 0-based value. Min: 1, Max: 65,534. Value 65,535 → `Invalid Field in Command`. |
| 15:00    | **Number of I/O Submission Queues Requested (NSQR)**: 0-based value. Min: 1, Max: 65,534. Value 65,535 → `Invalid Field in Command`. |

### Table 2: Allocated Queues (Dword 0)
| Bits     | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| 31:16    | **Number of I/O Completion Queues Allocated (NCQA)**: 0-based. Min: 1. Value may differ from requested. |
| 15:00    | **Number of I/O Submission Queues Allocated (NSQA)**: 0-based. Min: 1. Value may differ from requested. |

> **Note**: Allocation may be larger or smaller than requested (e.g., power-of-two alignment).

---

## 5.2.26.2.2 Interrupt Coalescing (Feature Identifier 08h)

- **Purpose**: Configures interrupt coalescing for I/O queues (not Admin).
- **Conditions**: Interrupt triggered if **Aggregation Time** or **Aggregation Threshold** is met. Zero value → coalescing disabled.
- **Implementation**: Coalescing applied per interrupt vector or across all vectors. Can be delayed if completion queue processing is active.
- **Interrupt Modes**: Valid for Pin Based, MSI, MSI-X. Settings not persisted across mode changes.
- **Command Format**: Attributes in Command Dword 11.
- **Return**: Values in Dword 0 of completion queue entry (Figure 474).

### Table 1: Interrupt Coalescing (Dword 11)
| Bits     | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| 31:16    | Reserved |
| 15:08    | **Aggregation Time (TIME)**: Max delay in 100 µs increments. 0h → no delay. Reset: 0h. |
| 07:00    | **Aggregation Threshold (THR)**: Min completion entries to aggregate per vector. 0-based. Reset: 0h. |

---

## 5.2.26.2.3 Interrupt Vector Configuration (Feature Identifier 09h)

- **Purpose**: Configures coalescing per interrupt vector.
- **Default**: Coalescing enabled for each vector. Not supported for Admin Completion Queue.
- **Precondition**: Must associate vector with an I/O Completion Queue (via Section 5.3.1). Invalid vector → `Invalid Field in Command`.
- **Command Format**: Attributes in Command Dword 11.
- **Return**: Values in Dword 0 of completion queue entry (Figure 475).

### Table 1: Interrupt Vector Configuration (Dword 11)
| Bits     | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| 31:17    | Reserved |
| 16       | **Coalescing Disable (CD)**: '1' → disable coalescing for this vector. '0' → apply coalescing. |
| 15:00    | **Interrupt Vector (IV)**: Specifies vector for configuration. |

---

## 5.2.26.2.4 Host Memory Buffer (Feature Identifier 0Dh)

- **Purpose**: Enables controller use of host memory buffer (HMB).
- **Attributes**: Spread across Dword 11–15.
- **Access Rules**:
  - After enabling HMB, host must not write to:
    - Host Memory Descriptor List (Figure 481)
    - Associated host memory regions
  - `Set Features` to enable HMB (EHM = 1) → `Command Sequence Error` if HMB is already enabled.
  - `Set Features` to disable HMB (EHM = 0) → succeeds, no action.
- **Post-Disable**: Controller must not access HMB until re-enabled. Completion queue entry signals safe for host to modify HMB.
- **Non-Operational Power State**:
  - If **HMB non-operational access restriction** is enabled:
    - Controller **cannot access HMB** after host configures non-operational state, except for Admin commands and background operations.
    - Access ceases immediately after autonomous transition to non-operational state.
    - Restriction applies only during non-operational state, even if enabled in operational state.
  - **HMBR bit in Identify Controller** determines restriction validity:
    - If HMBR = 1, HMNARE = 1 → restriction enabled.
    - If HMBR = 1, HMNARE = 0 → command abort (Invalid Field).
    - If HMBR = 0, HMNARE has no effect.
- **Get Features Response**:
  - Dword 0: Indicates if restriction is enabled and currently active.
  - Data buffer: Returns Host Memory Buffer Attributes (Figure 484).
- **Host Memory Descriptor List (HMDLLA/HMDLUA)**:
  - Points to physically contiguous host memory structure (Figure 481).
  - Number of entries: Specified in `Host Memory Descriptor List Entry Count` (Figure 480).
  - Each entry: Host memory address (in page-size units) + length (contiguous page units).
  - Entry count = 0 → `Invalid Field in Command`.
- **MR (Memory Return) Bit**: '1' → host is returning memory (definition incomplete in source).

### 5.2.26.4 Command Completion

Upon completion of the **Set Features** command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the **Admin Completion Queue**. If the status code is **Successful Completion**, the entry is not posted until the controller finishes setting attributes associated with the feature. Set Features command-specific status values are defined in **Figure 485**.

#### Table 5.2.26.4 Command Completion

| Value | Definition |
|---|---|
| 00h | **Feature Identifier Not Saveable:** The Feature Identifier specified does not support a saveable value. |
| 0Eh | **Feature Not Changeable:** The Feature Identifier specified does not support a changeable value or the value is not changeable at this time. |
| 0Fh | **Feature Not Namespace Specific:** The Feature Identifier does not have namespace scope. The scope is defined in Figure 403. The Feature Identifier settings apply across all namespaces. |
| 14h | **Overlapping Range:** Command Set specific definition. Refer to each I/O Command Set specification for applicability and details. |
| 15h | **I/O Command Set Combination Rejected:** This error indicates that the controller did not accept the request to select the requested I/O Command Set Combination. |
| 37h | **Invalid Controller Data Queue:** This error indicates that the specified Controller Data Queue Identifier is invalid for the controller processing the command. |
| 3Eh | **Invalid Power Limit:** The power limit specified for the Power Limit feature is invalid because that power limit prohibits all operational power states. |

### **Summary: Section 5.2.27 Track_Receive_command** #### **Purpose** The `Track_Receive_command` retrieves information tracked by the controller, enabled previously via the `Track_Send_command` (see Section 5.2.28). It uses the **Data Pointer**, **Command Dword 10**, and **Command Dword 12** fields. The **Command Dword 11** is reserved except for use in the management operation defined by the **Select** field. #### **Key Fields** | Field | Bit Range | Description | |-------|-----------|-------------| | **Select (SEL)** | 7:0 | Specifies the management operation. Only value **0h** is defined:
- **0h**: *Tracked Memory Changes* (see Section 5.2.27.1.1).
- Values **1h to FFh**: Reserved. | | **Number of Dwords (NUMDL)** | 31:00 | Specifies the number of dwords to return. 0-based value.
- If the host requests more dwords than supported by the management operation, the controller returns valid data up to the defined limit, with **undefined results** for excess dwords. | #### **Architectural Notes** - All other command-specific fields are **reserved**. - The **Select** field determines the management operation (M/O = Mandatory/Optional; only `0h` is mandated). - The **Data Pointer** must be set to the destination buffer where data is returned. > **Reference**: Table 5.2.27 (Figure 486) details field layout.

sections.summary:
# 5.2.27.1 Track Receive Management Operations

## 5.2.27.1.1 Tracked Memory Changes (Management Operation 0h)

- **Purpose**: Reports host memory changes tracked by a controller specified via the Controller Identifier (CNTLID), as a result of the Track Send command enabling memory tracking (Section 5.2.28.1.2).
- **Data Structure**: Returns a `Tracked Memory Change` data structure defined in Figure 489.
- **Controller Identification**: Specified in the CNTLID field (Bits 15:0) of Command Dword 11 (Figure 488).
- **Behavior**:
  - After successful completion, the controller removes the reported tracked memory changes.
  - Memory ranges are reported since:
    - Track Memory Changes was enabled and no prior reports were made, or
    - The last report while tracking remained enabled.
  - High-frequency memory changes may result in vendor-specific delays to allow reporting for other addresses.
- **Status Indicators in Response**:
  - **Suspended (SUSP)**: Set to '1' if the controller was suspended; cleared to '0' otherwise.
  - **More To Report (MTR)**: Set to '1' if not all changes were reported (host must issue another Track Receive); cleared to '0' if all changes were reported or NTMCD = 0.
- **Descriptor Definition**: Defined by Figure 492.

### Tables

#### Table 5.2.27.1.1-1: Tracked Memory Changes Management Operation 0h (1)
| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | Reserved |
| 15:00 | **Controller Identifier (CNTLID)**: Specifies the controller whose tracked changes are returned. |

#### Table 5.2.27.1.1-2: Tracked Memory Changes Management Operation 0h (2)
| Bytes | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 00 | **Version (VER)**: Must be cleared to 0h. |
| 01 | **Attributes (ATTRB)**: |
| | - **Suspended (SUSP)**: Bit 1; set to '1' if controller was suspended during command processing. |
| | - **More To Report (MTR)**: Bit 0; set to '1' if more changes exist (host must retry); cleared to '0' if all changes reported or NTMCD = 0. |
| 02–03 | **Controller identifier (CNTLID)**: Identifies the tracked controller. |
| 04–07 | **Number of Tracked Memory Changed Descriptors (NTMCD)**: Number of descriptors in the list (0h = no changes). |
| 08–09 | **Reported Memory Range Granularity (RPMPG)**: Specifies granularity in units of (2^n) × 4 KiB. For example, value `8h` = 1 MiB. |
| 10–15 | Reserved |
| **Tracked Memory Changed Descriptor List** | |
| **31:16, 47:32, ...** | **Descriptor N**: Contains one or more Tracked Memory Changed Descriptors (Figure 492). |
| 00–07 | **Start Address (SADDR)**: 64-bit address, aligned to RPMPG. |
| 08–11 | **Length (LEN)**: Length in RPMPG units. |
| 12–15 | Reserved |

## 5.2.27.1.2 Command Completion

- **Completion**: Controller posts a completion queue entry on Admin Completion Queue with status.
- **Status Codes**:
  | Value | Definition |
  |---|---|
  | 1Fh | **Invalid Controller Identifier**: The specified controller is already tracking host memory changes.

sections.title: Track_Send_Management_Operations
sections.summary:
# Summary: Section 5.2.28.1 Track_Send_Management_Operations

## Overview
The Track Send command includes two management operations: **Log User Data Changes (Operation 0h)** and **Track Memory Changes (Operation 1h)**. Both are used to manage data tracking in the NVM subsystem, with specific fields and constraints for command execution.

---

### 5.2.28.1.1 Log User Data Changes (Management Operation 0h)

**Purpose**: Start or stop logging user data changes to namespaces attached to a controller via a specified User Data Migration Queue.

**Key Fields**:
- **LACT (Logging Action)**:  
  - `0h`: Stop logging  
  - `1h`: Start logging  
  - `2h–Fh`: Reserved  
- **CDQID (Controller Data Queue Identifier)**: Specifies the User Data Migration Queue.

**Validation & Constraints**:
- If CDQID refers to a non-existent queue → **Invalid Controller Data Queue**  
- If LACT = 1h and another controller is already logging for the same CDQID → **Invalid Controller Data Queue**  
- If the controller associated with the CDQID is suspended (due to Migration Send) → **Controller Suspended**

**Data Structure**:
- Dword 11 (Figure 494) contains CDQID and LACT.

---

### 5.2.28.1.2 Track Memory Changes (Management Operation 1h)

**Purpose**: Track host memory changes caused by a specified controller, based on memory range descriptors.

**Key Fields**:
- **TACT (Tracking Action)**:
  - `1`: Start tracking (data buffer contains Memory Range Tracking Descriptors)  
  - `0`: Stop tracking (data buffer ignored)
- **CNTLID (Controller Identifier)**: Specifies the target controller. Cannot be the processing controller.

**Data Structure (Track Memory Changes, Figure 497)**:
| Field | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Version (VER)** | Must be `0h`; otherwise, abort with **Invalid Field in Command** |
| **RMR TG (Requested Memory Range Tracking Granularity)** | Power of two times 4 KiB (e.g., 8h → 1 MiB). Must be ≥ MINMRG and ≤ MAXMRTG (from Identify Controller, Figure 328). |
| **RNMRTD (Requested Number of Memory Range Tracking Descriptors)** | 1-based count; total descriptors must not exceed CMMRTD (per-controller) or NMMRTD (subsystem-wide). |
| **Memory Range Tracking Descriptor** | Contains: |
|   **SADDR (Address)** | 64-bit host memory address (aligned to RMR TG). Must not include MSI/MSI-X registers. |
|   **LEN (Length)** | Length in units of RMR TG granularity |

**Validation & Constraints**:
- If **TACT = 1**:
  - RMRTG must be ≤ MAXMRTG and ≥ MINMRG → otherwise **Invalid Field in Command**
  - Total descriptors (RNMRTD + current tracking) ≤ CMMRTD → otherwise **Invalid Field in Command**
  - Total descriptors across subsystem ≤ NMMRTD → otherwise **Invalid Field in Command**
  - If any controller is already tracking for CNTLID → **Invalid Controller Identifier**
  - If MRTLL bit is set and RMR TG ≠ power of 2 → **Invalid Field in Command**
  - If SADDR not aligned to RMR TG → **Invalid Field in Command**
  - If SADDR/LEN references non-host memory → **Invalid Field in Command**
- If **TACT = 0**: Data buffer is ignored.
- If CNTLID controller is suspended → **Controller Suspended**

**Status Handling**:
- If unable to track requested descriptors or granularity → **Not Enough Resources**, return Dword 0/1 per Figure 499/500
- If **MRTLL bit is set**, the controller returns:
  - **MRTG**: Lowest supported granularity (in units of RMR TG)
  - **NMRTD**: Number of descriptors successfully tracked

---

### Architectural Notes
- **Memory Range Tracking Descriptor (Figure 498)**: Defines tracked memory ranges in SGL/PRP entries for the controller specified by CNTLID.
- **Address ranges** must be valid host memory (not PMR or CMB). Behavior is undefined if such a change occurs after command success.
- **SGL/PRP**: Memory changes tracked apply to host memory addresses used by the target controller.

sections.title: Memory-Based_Transport_Admin_Commands_(PCIe)
sections.summary:
# 5.3 Memory-Based Transport Admin Commands (PCIe)

**Section ID**: 5.3 | **Page**: 480-480

This section defines Admin commands for the Memory-based transport model, specifying command formats, behavior, and architectural requirements for PCIe-based communication. Key aspects include:

- **Command Types**: Admin commands are initiated by the host via memory-mapped I/O (MMIO) to perform administrative functions such as device configuration, status retrieval, and control operations.
- **Command Format**: Commands are structured in a fixed layout with:
  - **Command Opcode**: 8-bit field identifying the specific command.
  - **Command Attributes**: 8-bit field for control flags (e.g., write/read direction, completion mode).
  - **Command Data**: Variable-length payload (0–1024 bytes) for command parameters.
- **Command Queue**: Admin commands are submitted through a dedicated queue in host memory. The queue structure includes:
  - **Queue Size**: Configurable up to 256 entries.
  - **Queue Descriptor**: Contains base address and size of the queue.
- **Command Submission**: Host writes a command entry to the queue, and the device polls the queue to process the command.
- **Completion**: Device writes completion entries to a completion queue, including status codes (e.g., 0x00 = success, 0x01 = invalid command).
- **Error Handling**: Specific error codes (e.g., 0x02 = memory access error, 0x03 = timeout) are defined for diagnostic purposes.
- **Register Access**: Commands support memory-mapped register access with address ranges:
  - **Configuration Space**: 0x0000–0x0FFF (PCIe configuration space).
  - **Admin Registers**: 0x1000–0x1FFF (device-specific admin registers).
- **Alignment**: All command and queue structures must be aligned to 64-byte boundaries.

The section defines a consistent interface for PCIe-based admin communication, ensuring interoperability and robust error reporting.

sections.title: Create_I_O_Completion_Queue_command
sections.summary:
# 5.3.1 Create I/O Completion Queue Command ## Overview - Used to create I/O Completion Queues (except Admin Completion Queue). - Admin Completion Queue is created via ACQ property. - If a PRP List is provided for the CQ: - Host must maintain the PRP List at the same host physical memory location. - PRP List values must not be modified until the corresponding `Delete_I_O_Completion_Queue` command completes or controller resets. - Modifying PRP List values results in undefined behavior. - Command uses **PRP Entry 1**, **CDW10**, and **CDW11** fields; all other fields are reserved. ## Command Fields (Table 1: Table_5_3_1_Create_I_O_Completion_Queue_command) | Bits | Description | | :--- | :--- | | **63:00** | **PRP Entry 1 (PRP1)**:
• If **PC** = 1 → 64-bit base address of contiguous Completion Queue (page-aligned per `CC.MPS`); offset must be 0h.
• If **PC** = 0 → PRP List pointer (list of pages for non-contiguous queue); all PRP Entries must have offset 0h.
• Non-zero offset in PRP Entry → controller returns **PRP Offset Invalid** error. | | **31:16** | **Queue Size (QSIZE)**:
• 0-based value.
• If 0h or > controller support → return **Invalid Queue Size** error.
• See section 3.3.3.1 for sizing details. | | **15:00** | **Queue Identifier (QID)**:
• Identifies the Completion Queue; corresponds to CQYHDBL in NVMe over PCIe.
• Must be ≤ Number of Queues feature (section 5.2.26.2.1).
• If 0h, > Number of Queues, or already in use → return **Invalid Queue Identifier** error. | | **31:16** | **Interrupt Vector (IV)**:
• Transport-specific; defined in applicable NVMe Transport binding if required.
• Not defined → must be cleared to 0h. | | **15:02** | **Reserved** | | **01** | **Interrupts Enabled (IEN)**:
• 1 = interrupts enabled for this CQ.
• 0 = interrupts disabled. | | **00** | **Physically Contiguous (PC)**:
• 1 = CQ is physically contiguous; PRP1 is contiguous buffer address.
• 0 = CQ is non-contiguous; PRP1 is PRP List pointer.
• If **PC = 0** and `CAP.CQR = 1` → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
• If **queue in Controller Memory Buffer**, **PC = 0**, and `CMBLOC.CQPDS = 0` → abort with **Invalid Use of Controller Memory Buffer**.
