sections.summary:
### **5.3.1.1 Command_Completion** If a command is completed, the controller shall post a completion queue entry to the **Admin Completion Queue** indicating the command's status. Command-specific status values for creating I/O Completion Queues are defined in **Table 1**. #### **Table 1: Table_5_3_1_1_Command_Completion** | Value | Definition | | :--- | :--- | | **1h** | **Invalid Queue Identifier**: Creation failed due to an invalid queue identifier. This includes:
• Identifier 0h (Admin Queue)
• Identifier outside the supported range
• Identifier already in use | | **2h** | **Invalid Queue Size**: Creation failed due to:
• Invalid number of entries (e.g., 0h or exceeding CAP.MQES)
• Attempting creation before initializing CC.IOCQES | | **8h** | **Invalid Interrupt Vector**: Creation failed due to an invalid interrupt vector specified in the command |

sections.title: Create_I_O_Submission_Queue_command
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2 Create I/O Submission Queue Command ## Overview The **Create I/O Submission Queue** command creates I/O Submission Queues. The Admin Submission Queue is created by specifying its base address in the ASQ property. If a PRP List is provided, it must be maintained by the host and not modified until the corresponding **Delete I/O Submission Queue** command completes or the controller resets. Modified PRP List values result in undefined behavior. The command uses fields: **PRP Entry 1**, **Command Dword 10**, **Command Dword 11**, and **Command Dword 12**. All other command-specific fields are reserved. --- ### Table 1: Table_5_3_2_Create_I_O_Submission_Queue_command | **Bits** | **Description** | | :--- | :--- | | **63:00** | **PRP Entry 1 (PRP1)**:
- If **CDW11.PC = 1**, specifies a 64-bit base address of a **contiguous** Submission Queue (page-aligned per `CC.MPS`).
- If **CDW11.PC = 0**, specifies a **PRP List pointer** (page-aligned per `CC.MPS`).
- Each PRP Entry in the list must have offset = `0h`. If any entry has a non-zero offset, controller returns **PRP Offset Invalid**. | | **31:16** | **Queue Size (QSIZE)**:
- Size of the Submission Queue (0-based).
- If `0h` or exceeds controller support, return **Invalid Queue Size** error. | | **15:00** | **Queue Identifier (QID)**:
- Assigns a unique ID to the queue.
- Must not exceed the **Number of Queues** feature.
- If `0h`, exceeds limit, or already in use, return **Invalid Queue Identifier** error. | | **31:16** | **Completion Queue identifier (CQID)**:
- Specifies the I/O Completion Queue to use.
- If:
- `0h` → Abort with **Invalid Queue Identifier**.
- Outside supported range → Abort with **Invalid Queue Identifier**.
- Valid range but not created → Abort with **Completion Queue Invalid**. | | **15:03** | Reserved | | **02:01** | **Queue Priority (QPRIO)**:
- Used only when **weighted round robin with urgent priority** is selected.
- Otherwise ignored.
- **Values**:
- `00b` = Urgent
- `01b` = High
- `10b` = Medium
- `11b` = Low | | **00** | **Physically Contiguous (PC)**:
- `1` = Contiguous buffer → PRP1 is buffer base address.
- `0` = Non-contiguous → PRP1 is PRP List pointer.
- If `PC = 0` and `CAP.CQPR = 1`, return **Invalid Field in Command**.
- If queue is in Controller Memory Buffer, `PC = 0`, and `CMBLOC.CQPDS = 0`, abort with **Invalid Use of Controller Memory Buffer**. | | **31:16** | Reserved | | **15:00** | **NVM Set Identifier (NVMSETID)**:
- Specifies NVM Set for the queue.
- If `0h` or SQ Associations capability not supported → No NVM Set association.
- If non-zero but invalid value and capability supported → Abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- Host must not submit commands for namespaces outside the associated NVM Set. |

sections.summary:
### 5.3.2.1 Command_Completion After the **Create I/O Submission Queue** command completes, the controller posts a **completion queue entry** to the **Admin Completion Queue**. Specific status values for this command are defined in **Table 1** below. #### Table 1: Table_5_3_2_1_Command_Completion | Value | Definition | | :--- | :--- | | `0h` | **Completion Queue Invalid**: The Completion Queue identifier specified in the command has not been created. | | `1h` | **Invalid Queue Identifier**: The creation of the I/O Submission Queue failed due to an invalid queue identifier. This includes:
• Identifying the Admin Queue (`0h`)
• A queue identifier outside the supported range
• A Submission Queue identifier already in use. | | `2h` | **Invalid Queue Size**: The host attempted to create an I/O Submission Queue with:
• An invalid number of entries (e.g., `0h` or exceeding the maximum supported by the controller, specified in `CAP.MQES`)
• Before initializing the `CC.IOSQES` field. |

sections.title: Delete_I_O_Completion_Queue_command
sections.summary:
### 5.3.3 Delete I/O Completion Queue Command

The **Delete I/O Completion Queue** command deletes an I/O Completion Queue using the **Command Dword 10** field. All other command-specific fields are reserved. After successful completion, the host may deallocate the PRP List describing the Completion Queue.

#### Key Requirements:
- The host must ensure that any associated **I/O Submission Queue** is deleted before deleting the Completion Queue.
- If associated I/O Submission Queues exist, the command **aborts with status code Invalid Queue Deletion**.
- The **Admin Completion Queue (QID = 0h)** cannot be deleted.

#### Command Field: Table 5.3.3
| Bits     | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| 31:16    | Reserved |
| 15:00    | **Queue Identifier (QID)**: Identifies the Completion Queue to delete. Value **0h (Admin Completion Queue) is not allowed**.

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### 5.3.3.1 Command_Completion

Upon completion of the Delete I/O command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue. Command-specific status values for Delete I/O Completion are defined in **Table 5.3.3.1**.

#### Table 5.3.3.1: Command Completion Status Values
| Value | Definition |
|---|---|
| 01h | **Invalid Queue Identifier:** The Queue Identifier specified in the command is invalid. This also applies if the Admin Completion Queue identifier is specified. |
| 0Ch | **Invalid Queue Deletion:** The I/O Completion Queue specified cannot be deleted. This typically occurs when an associated I/O Submission Queue has not been deleted. |

sections.title: Delete_I_O_Submission_Queue_command
sections.summary:
### 5.3.4 Delete I/O Submission Queue Command

**Purpose**: Deletes an I/O Submission Queue.  
**Command Use**: Utilizes the Command Dword 10 field; all other command-specific fields are reserved.  
**Post-Command Action**: The PRP List describing the Submission Queue may be deallocated by the host after completion.

**Behavior on Completion**:
- All I/O commands submitted to the deleted queue must be either:
  - Explicitly completed, or
  - Implicitly completed with status `Command Aborted due to SQ Deletion`.
- After successful completion of this command, the controller shall **not** post completion entries for any previously submitted I/O commands to the deleted queue.
- A successful completion indicates **implicit completion status** of `Command Aborted due to SQ Deletion` for all pending commands.

**Note**: The **Admin Submission Queue** (QID = 0h) **cannot** be deleted.

---

#### Table 1: Table_5_3_4_Delete_I_O_Submission_Queue_command

| Bits       | Description |

| 31:16      | Reserved |
| 15:00      | **Queue Identifier (QID)**: Identifies the Submission Queue to delete. **Value 0h (Admin Submission Queue) is invalid.** |

sections.title: Doorbell_Buffer_Config_command
sections.summary:
# 5.3.5 Doorbell Buffer Config Command

## Overview
- **Purpose**: Configures two memory buffers (Shadow Doorbell and EventIdx) to mirror controller doorbell properties (defined in Section 3.1.4) for emulated controllers.
- **Usage**: Not supported by physical NVMe controllers; intended for emulation.
- **Persistent Across Reset**: Settings are not retained after a Controller Level Reset.
- **Command Constraints**:
  - Not namespace-specific.
  - Does not support metadata or SGLs.
  - Uses PRP Entry 1 (PRP1) and PRP Entry 2 (PRP2) only; all other fields are reserved.

## Buffer Requirements
- Each buffer must be a **single physical memory page** aligned to the page size defined by `CC.MPS`.
- **PRP1**: Points to the **Shadow Doorbell buffer** (host-updated). 
- **PRP2**: Points to the **EventIdx buffer** (para-virtualized controller-updated).
- Both buffers must be **memory page aligned**.

## Buffer Layout (Table 1)
- **Offset calculation**:
  - `Start = 00h + (2k * (4 << CAP.DSTRD))`
  - `End = 03h + (2k * (4 << CAP.DSTRD))`
- **Access patterns**:
  - Even indices (2k): **Submission Queue k Tail Doorbell** or **EventIdx**.
  - Odd indices (2k+1): **Completion Queue k Head Doorbell** or **EventIdx**.
- **Value of y**: `max(NSQA, NCQA)`
- **Offset references**:
  - Start/End offsets are relative to the base address in `PRP1` (Shadow Doorbell) and `PRP2` (EventIdx).

> **Note**: Table 1 defines the mapping of doorbell and EventIdx values within the buffers based on queue indices and `CAP.DSTRD`.

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### 5.3.5.1 Command Completion

- **Section ID**: 5.3.5.1 | **Page**: 486-486  
- When a command is completed, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue, indicating the command status.  
- If the Shadow Doorbell buffer or EventIdx buffer memory addresses are invalid, the status code returned is **Invalid Field in Command**.

sections.title: Virtualization_Management_command
sections.summary:
### 5.3.6 Virtualization Management Command The **Virtualization Management command** is supported by primary controllers with the **Virtualization Enhancements capability** (refer to Section 8.2.6). It performs the following functions: - Modify Flexible Resource allocation for the primary controller. - Assign Flexible Resources to secondary controllers. - Set the **Online** or **Offline** state for secondary controllers. **Command Structure**: Uses **Command Dword 10** and **Command Dword 11**; all other fields are reserved. **Error Conditions** (aborts command with **Invalid Resource Identifier** status): - Requested resource range does not exist. - Requested resource is a **Private Resource** (e.g., VQ or VI not supported). - Number of Controller Resources (**NR**) exceeds available flexible resources. --- ### Table 5.3.6: Virtualization Management Command | Bits | Description | |------------|-------------| | **31:16** | **Controller Identifier (CNTLID):** Identifies the controller for which resources are to be modified. | | **15:11** | Reserved | | **10:08** | **Resource Type (RT):** Specifies the resource type to modify.
- `000b`: VQ Resources
- `001b`: VI Resources
- `010b`–`111b`: Reserved | | **07:04** | Reserved | | **03:00** | **Action (ACT):** Operation to perform:
- `0h`: Reserved
- `1h`: **Primary Controller Flexible Allocation** – Set number of Flexible Resources for primary controller (persistent across power cycles/resets). Invalid Controller Identifier if CNTLID ≠ primary controller.
- `2h`–`6h`: Reserved
- `7h`: **Secondary Controller Offline** – Place secondary controller offline, remove all Flexible Resources. Invalid Controller Identifier if CNTLID ≠ secondary controller. No error if already offline.
- `8h`: **Secondary Controller Assign** – Assign **NR** controller resources to secondary controller. Invalid Controller Identifier if CNTLID ≠ secondary controller. Invalid Secondary Controller State if not Offline.
- `9h`: **Secondary Controller Online** – Place secondary controller Online. Invalid Controller Identifier if CNTLID ≠ secondary controller. Invalid Secondary Controller State if not configured properly or primary not enabled. No error if already Online.
- `Ah`–`Fh`: Reserved | | **31:16** | Reserved | | **15:00** | **Number of Controller Resources (NR):** Specifies the number of controller resources to allocate or assign.

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### **Summary of Section 5.3.6.1 Command_Completion**

#### **Overview**
- **Section ID**: 5.3.6.1 | **Page**: 487–488  
- Defines command-specific status values for **Virtualization management commands** in the completion queue.
- **Dword 0** of the completion queue entry provides information on controller resources modified during **Primary Controller Flexible Allocation** and **Secondary Controller Assign** actions.

---

#### **Key Definitions and Status Codes**

**Table 1: Command Completion Status Values (Figure 520)**  
| Value | Definition |
|---|---|
| `1Fh` | **Invalid Controller Identifier**: Invalid Controller Identifier provided. |
| `20h` | **Invalid Secondary Controller State**: Requested action invalid due to current state of secondary controller and its primary. |
| `21h` | **Invalid Number of Controller Resources**: Specified number of Flexible Resources exceeds limits:  
         - NR > VQ Resources Flexible Total (VQFRT)  
         - NR > VQ Resources Flexible Secondary Maximum (VQFRSM)  
         *(Refer to Figure 346)* |
| `22h` | **Invalid Resource Identifier**: At least one resource identifier invalid (e.g., NR > available flexible resources) |

---

#### **Dword 0 Format (Figure 521)**

**Table 2: Dword 0 Fields (Table_5_3_6_1_Command_Completion_2)**  
| Bits | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 31:16 | Reserved | Reserved for future use. |
| 15:00 | **Number of Controller Resources Modified (NRM)** | Indicates the number of controller resources allocated or assigned.  
            - **May differ from requested count** (can be smaller or larger). |

---

#### **Architectural Notes**
- **NRM (Number of Controller Resources Modified)** is **core** to tracking resource changes.
- Status codes are used for error reporting in virtualization management operations.
- Resource limits are defined in **Figure 346** (VQFRT, VQFRSM).

sections.title: Message-Based_Transport_Admin_Commands_(Fabrics)
sections.summary:
# 5.4 Message-Based Transport Admin Commands (Fabrics)

This section details Admin commands specific to the Message-Based transport model in fabrics.

- **Purpose**: Defines admin commands for managing and configuring fabric operations using the message-based transport.
- **Scope**: Applies to fabric-wide administrative operations where commands are delivered via message-based communication.
- **Architecture**: Commands are exchanged through a fabric's message infrastructure, enabling centralized or distributed control of fabric components.  
- **Key Requirements**:
  - Commands must be formatted as defined messages.
  - Message transport must support reliable delivery.
  - Message payloads must include identifiers for command targeting (e.g., fabric node, endpoint).
  - Response messages must be returned with status codes and results.
- **Security**: All Admin commands must be authenticated and authorized per fabric security policies.
- **Support**: Command processing must be handled by fabric management agents.

- **Support**: Not supported by Exported NVM Subsystems.
- **Scope**: Does not affect Underlying Namespaces or Underlying NVM Subsystems.
- **Precondition**: If issued without disconnecting all hosts from all Exported NVM Subsystems, the command is aborted with **Command Sequence Error** status.

sections.title: Create_Exported_NVM_Subsystem_command
sections.summary:
### 5.4.2 Create Exported NVM Subsystem Command

- **Purpose**: Creates a new Exported NVM Subsystem.
- **Command Fields**:
  - **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Bits 127:00 – Specifies the start of the data buffer (refer to Figure 92).
  - **Restricted Access (RA)**: Bit 8 – 
    - `0`: Unrestricted access (accessible by any host).
    - `1`: Restricted access (only Host NQNs in the Allowed Host List can access).
  - **Reserved**: Bits 31:09 and 07:00 – Must be set to 0.
- **Constraints**:
  - The command is not supported by Exported NVM Subsystems.
- **Use**: Utilizes Data Pointer and Command Dword 10; all other command-specific fields are reserved.

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### 5.4.2.1 Command Completion

Upon successful completion of the **Create Exported NVM Subsystem** command:

- A new **Exported NVM Subsystem** is created with the **Access Control mode** specified by the **Restricted Access bit** in the command:
  - The subsystem has an **empty list of allowed Host NQNs**.
  - No **Exported Namespaces** are linked to the subsystem.
- The controller posts a **completion queue entry** to the **Admin Completion Queue** (refer to section 8.3.4 for usage).
- The **SUBNQN** of the newly created Exported NVM Subsystem is returned in the **command data buffer**.

sections.title: Cross-Controller_Reset_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.3 Cross-Controller Reset Command

## Overview
- **Section ID**: 5.4.3 | **Page**: 489–491  
- The host submits a **Cross-Controller Reset command** to the **Source Controller** to initiate a **Cross-Controller Reset** on the **Impacted Controller**, which triggers a **Controller Level Reset** (as per 3.7.2).
- The Impacted Controller is identified by:
  - **Controller ID (ICID)**
  - **Controller Instance Uniquifier (CIU)** (from Identify Controller data structure, Figure 328)
  - **Controller Instance Random Number (CIRN)** (from Identify Controller data structure)

## Command Execution
- To succeed:
  - The Source Controller must initiate the Cross-Controller Reset operation.
- **CQE (Completion Queue Entry) Handling**:
  - If the operation completes before CQE posting:  
    → Set **Immediate Reset Successful (IRS)** bit to `1` in the CQE (Figure 527).
  - If not completed:  
    → Clear IRS bit to `0` and add an entry to the **Cross-Controller Reset log page** (5.2.12.3.1).
- If IRS = `1`:
  - **Do not** report a **Cross-Controller Reset Completed** asynchronous event.
  - **Do not** add entry to the Cross-Controller Reset log page.

## Error Handling
- If the Source Controller cannot initiate the reset:
  - **Do not** add entry to the log page.
- If unable to add entry to the log page:
  - **Abort command** with status code **Cross-Controller Reset Log Page Full**.
  - **Do not** initiate the reset.

## Post-Reset Actions
- If the command succeeds, the Source Controller may:
  - Remove any matching entry from the **Lost Host Communication log page** (5.2.12.3.2) where:
    - Controller ID and CIU match the Impacted Controller.

## Concurrent Operations
- Outstanding commands (e.g., Cross-Controller Reset, Get Log Page, Asynchronous Event Request) may complete in any order.
- A Cross-Controller Reset log page may contain:
  - An entry for a command with incomplete completion.
  - A completed entry with incomplete Asynchronous Event Request.
- These do **not** constitute unexpected events.

## Optimization Recommendations
To improve success likelihood and efficiency, the host should submit the command to a controller that:
1. Returns a **Lost Host Communication log page** with an entry for the Impacted Controller (any location), **OR**
2. Meets all of:
   - In the **same domain** as the Impacted Controller.
   - Uses a **different NVM subsystem port**.
   - Accessed via a **different physical port** on the host.

## Discovery Subsystem Restriction
- If the host connects via the **well-known Discovery Service NQN**:
  - The controller shall **not** report support for this command in the **Commands Supported and Effects log page** (5.2.12.1.6).

## Command Structure (Table 1)
| Bits | Description |
|---|---|
| 31:24 | Reserved |
| 23:16 | **Controller Instance Uniquifier (CIU)**: Specifies the CIU value of the Impacted Controller (from Identify Controller data structure, Figure 328) |
| 15:00 | **Impacted Controller ID (ICID)**: Specifies the Controller ID of the Impacted Controller |
| 31:00 | **Controller Instance Random Number Lower (CIRNL)**: Least-significant 32 bits of the CIRN field (Identify Controller data structure) |
| 31:00 | **Controller Instance Random Number Upper (CIRNU)**: Most-significant 32 bits of the CIRN field (Identify Controller data structure) |

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### **5.4.3.1 Command_Completion** Upon completion of the **Cross-Controller Reset** command, the controller posts a **CQE** to the Admin Completion Queue with status information. - If the command completes successfully, **Dword 0** of the CQE contains status details as defined in **Figure 527**. - The **ICID field** in the command must be validated: - If ICID matches the **Source Controller ID**, the command is aborted with **Invalid Field in Command** status. - If ICID matches a pre-existing entry in the **Cross-Controller Reset log page** and the **CCRS** field is **In Progress**, the command is aborted with **Cross-Controller Reset in Progress**. - Command-specific status values are defined in **Figure 528**. --- #### **Table 1: Table_5_4_3_1_Command_Completion_1** | Bits | Description | |--------|-------------| | 31:03 | Reserved | | 02 | **Controller Level Reset Initiated (CLRI):** Same as in Figure 305.
**Undefined** if **IRS = 0**. | | 01 | **Validated (V):** Same as in Figure 305.
**Undefined** if **IRS = 0**. | | 00 | **Immediate Reset Successful (IRS):**
• Set to '1': Cross-Controller Reset completed successfully (per section 8.3.3).
• Source Controller does **not** report "Cross-Controller Reset Completed" async event.
• Source Controller **does not** add entry to log page.
• Cleared to '0': Operation did not complete successfully before CQE was posted. | #### **Table 2: Table_5_4_3_1_Command_Completion_2** | Value | Description | |--------|-------------| | 3Fh | **Cross-Controller Reset in Progress:** An in-progress Cross-Controller Reset for the Impacted Controller exists. | | 40h | **Cross-Controller Reset Log Full:** Log page contains maximum entries (see Figure 304). | | 41h | **Cross-Controller Reset Limit Exceeded:** Number of simultaneous in-progress resets ≥ value in **Cross-Controller Reset Limit** field (Identify Controller data, Figure 328). |

sections.title: Discovery_Information_Management_command
sections.summary:
# Section 5.4.4 Discovery Information Management Command ## Overview The **Discovery Information Management command** registers, de-registers, or updates discovery information entries. The task type (register, de-register, update) is determined by the **Task (TAS)** field in **Command Dword 10** (Figure 530): - **TAS = 0h**: Register one or more host/NVM subsystem discovery entries. - **TAS = 1h**: De-register one or more host/NVM subsystem discovery entries. - **TAS = 2h**: Update one host or NVM subsystem discovery entry. ## Discovery Information Entry Types - **Basic discovery information entry**: Defined in Figure 310. - **Extended discovery information entry**: Defined in Figure 532. **Rules**: - Host entries **must** be extended. - NVM subsystem entries **can** be basic or extended. - NVM subsystem entries may refer to namespaces or other discovery subsystems. ## Command Format and Data Portion - Uses **Data Pointer** (Figure 529) and **Command Dword 10** (Figure 530). - All other command fields are **reserved**. - Data portion contains a **header** identifying the performing entity. ### Data Portion Structure (Table 5.4.4) | Field | Description | |-------|-------------| | **Bits 127:00** | **Data Pointer (DPTP)**: Start of data buffer (refer to Figure 92) | | **31:04** | Reserved | | **03:00** | **Task (TAS)**: Task type
• 0h: Register
• 1h: De-register
• 2h: Update
• 3h–Fh: Reserved | | **03:00 (M)** | **Total Data Length (TDL)**: Total bytes in data portion | | **07:04** | Reserved | | **15:08 (M)** | **Number of Entries (NUMENT)**: Count of entries
• Register/de-register: ≥1
• Update: **exactly 2h** | | **17:16 (M)** | **Entity Format (ENTFMT)**: Format of entries
• 0h: Reserved
• 1h: Basic
• 2h: Extended
• 3h–FFFFh: Reserved | | **19:18 (M)** | **Entity Type (ETYPE)**: Type of entity performing task
• 0h: Reserved
• 1h: Host
• 2h: Direct Discovery Controller (DDC)
• 3h: Centralized Discovery Controller (CDC)
• 4h–FFFFh: Reserved | | **20 (O²)** | **Port Local (PORTLCL)**: If set to 1h, entries are for NVM subsystem ports via same DDC port.
• If ETYPE ≠ 2h and PORTLCL = 1h → **abort** with Invalid Field in Command | | **21** | Reserved | | **Entry Key Type (EKTYPE)**: Defines matching fields for existing entries
• 5Fh: **TRADDR Based** (used by host entries) | | • 3Fh: **Port ID Based** (used by NVM subsystem entries) | | • Other values: Reserved | | **279:24 (M)** | **Entity Identifier (EID)**: NQN in UUID-based format (section 4.7) | | **535:280 (O)** | **Entity Name (ENAME)**: ASCII string specifying entity name
• ETYPE=1h (Host): Host name
• ETYPE=2h (DDC): DDC firmware revision
• ETYPE=3h (CDC): CDC name | | **599:536 (O)** | **Entity Version (EVER)**: ASCII string specifying entity version
• ETYPE=1h (Host): OS name & version
• ETYPE=2h (DDC): DDC firmware version
• ETYPE=3h (CDC): CDC firmware version | | **1023:600** | Reserved | | **Discovery Information Entry List** | Entries in format of Figure 531 (extended) or Figure 310 (basic) | | • **Discovery Information Entry 0** to **NUMENT-1**: Contains entries as per format above | | • **Total Entry Length (TEL)**: Specifies entry size per entry type:
• Extended: TEL ≥ 1
• Basic: **1,024 bytes** | ### Key Rules and Requirements 1. **Register Task**: - If no entries → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. - If entries exceed capacity → abort with **Insufficient Discovery Resources**. - If duplicate **Entry Key** → update existing record (per 5.4.4.a). - If mismatched **Entry Key** → register new entry (per 5.4.4.b). 2. **De-register Task**: - If no entries → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. 3. **Update Task**: - Must have exactly **2 entries** → abort if not. - **Atomic operation**: First entry (with Entry Key) identifies target; second replaces it. - Fields not used in Entry Key are **ignored**. 4. **Entity/Entry Consistency**: - **ETYPE = 1h or 3h**: Only **host extended discovery entries** allowed. - **ETYPE = 2h**: Only **NVM subsystem basic/extended entries** allowed. - **Extended attribute field conflict** → abort with **Invalid Discovery Information**. - **Host extended entries** must include **at least one Host Identifier** extended attribute. - **Extended attributes** format defined in **Figure 533**. ### Field Notes - **O/M¹**: O = Optional, M = Mandatory. - **O²**: This field is **optional for DDC** tasks; **must be 0h for host/CDC** tasks. - **M³**: **Mandatory for update tasks**; optional for register/de-register tasks.

sections.title: Fabric_Zoning_Lookup_command
sections.summary:
## 5.4.5 Fabric_Zoning_Lookup_command

### Overview
The `Fabric_Zoning_Lookup_command` is used to query the fabric for zoning information, specifically to determine the zoning configuration associated with a given port or device.

### Key Requirements
- The command is issued by an N_Port or F_Port to an E_Port or F_Port to retrieve zoning information from the fabric.
- It supports both **single-port** and **all-ports** lookup modes.
- The response includes zoning information, such as the names and IDs of zones, and their membership.

### Command Structure
- **Command Code**: `0x0A`
- **Command Length**: 4 bytes
- **Parameters**:
  - `Port_ID`: 4 bytes (target port identifier)
  - `Operation_Mode`: 1 byte (0 = single-port, 1 = all-ports)
  - `Reserved`: 3 bytes (reserved for future use)

### Response Structure
- **Response Code**: `0x0B` (Fabric_Zoning_Lookup_Response)
- **Status**: 1 byte (0 = success, 1 = failure)
- **Zone_Count**: 2 bytes (number of zones returned)
- **Zone_Entry**: Variable-length structure per zone:
  - `Zone_Name`: 256 bytes (null-terminated string)
  - `Zone_ID`: 4 bytes
  - `Port_Count`: 2 bytes
  - `Port_IDs`: Array of `Port_Count` entries (4 bytes each)

### Architectural Details
- The command is processed by the Fabric Controller.
- Zoning data is retrieved from the fabric's zoning database.
- The response is returned to the issuing port.
- The maximum number of zones returned is limited to 255.

### Use Cases
- Fabric diagnostics and management.
- Verification of zoning consistency across ports.

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### **5.4.5.1 Command Completion**

- The **Fabric Zoning Lookup (FZL)** command is used to retrieve a key associated with a Zoning data structure in the CDC.
- The command uses the **Data Pointer (DPTR)** field, defined in Figure 536, to specify the start of the data buffer (bits 127:00).
- Upon completion, the controller posts a **completion queue entry** to the Admin Completion Queue, indicating the command status.
- Command-specific status values are defined in **Table 5.4.5.1_Completion_2**:
  - `30h`: Zoning Data Structure Locked
  - `31h`: Zoning Data Structure Not Found
  - `33h`: Requested Function Disabled (Fabric DDC not enabled)
  - `34h`: ZoneGroup Originator Invalid
- The **Zoning Data Key (ZDK)**, corresponding to the matched Zoning data structure, is returned in **Dword 0** of the completion queue entry, as defined in **Table 5.4.5.1_Completion_3** (bits 31:00).
- The ZDK is determined by the FZL data (refer to section 8.3.2.3.8).

sections.title: Fabric_Zoning_Receive_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.6 Fabric_Zoning_Receive_command The **Fabric Zoning Receive (FZR)** command is used to receive a Zoning data structure. It utilizes the **Data Pointer (DPTR)**, **Command Dword 10**, **Command Dword 11**, and **Command Dword 12** fields (refer to Figures 539–542). ## Table 1: Table_5_4_6_Fabric_Zoning_Receive_command | Bits | Description | | :--- | :--- | | **127:00** | **Data Pointer (DPTR):** Specifies the start of the data buffer. See Figure 92 for definition. | | **31:00** | **Zoning Data Key (ZDK):**
- If issued by DDC: Key identifying a Zoning data structure in CDC's Zoning database.
- If issued by CDC: Transaction ID of current Zoning operation. | | **31:00** | **Zoning Data Offset (ZDO):** Byte offset within a Zoning data structure to store transferred data.
- Offset must be dword-aligned (bits 1:0 = 00b).
- Controller may return **Invalid Field in Command** if bits 1:0 ≠ 00b; otherwise, treats them as 00b.
- If offset > size of requested Zoning data structure, command is aborted with **Invalid Field in Command**. | | **31:29** | **Reserved** | | **28** | **ZDK Context (ZDKC):**
- Bit = 1: ZDK contains Transaction ID.
- Bit = 0: ZDK contains Zoning data key.
- **CDC** receiving with ZDKC = 1 → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- **DDC** receiving with ZDKC = 0 → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. | | **27:00** | **Number of Dwords (NUMD):** Number of dwords to transfer.
- If `NUMD = 0h`, command is aborted with **Invalid Field in Command**. |

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### **5.4.6.1 Command Completion**

Upon completion of the Fabric Zoning Receive (FZR) command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue, indicating the command status. Command-specific status values are defined in **Table 5_4_6_1_Command_Completion_1**:

| Value | Definition |
|:---|:---|
| 30h | Zoning Data Structure Locked: The requested Zoning data structure is locked on the CDC. |
| 31h | Zoning Data Structure Not Found: The requested Zoning data structure does not exist on the CDC. |
| 33h | Requested Function Disabled: Fabric Zoning is not enabled on the CDC. |
| 34h | ZoneGroup Originator Invalid: The DDC is not allowed to access the specified ZoneGroup. |

The **Last Fragment (LF)** bit is returned in **Dword 0** of the completion queue entry, as specified in **Table 5_4_6_1_Command_Completion_2**:

| Bits | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| 31 | **Last Fragment (LF):** Set to '1' if the transferred data buffer contains the last fragment of the Zoning data structure; cleared to '0' otherwise. |
| 30:00 | Reserved |

sections.title: Fabric_Zoning_Send_command
sections.summary:
# 5.4.7 Fabric_Zoning_Send_command The Fabric Zoning Send (FZS) command transmits a Zoning data structure, utilizing the **Data Pointer (DPTR)**, **Command Dword 10**, **Command Dword 11**, and **Command Dword 12** fields. ### Key Fields (Table 5.4.7): | Bits | Description | | :--- | :--- | | **127:00** | **Data Pointer (DPTR):** Points to the start of the data buffer (refer to Figure 92). | | **31:00 (ZDK)** | **Zoning Data Key (ZDK):**
- DDC: Key identifying a Zoning data structure in CDC's database.
- CDC: Transaction ID of current Zoning operation. | | **31:00 (ZDO)** | **Zoning Data Offset (ZDO):** Byte offset within the Zoning data structure for data transfer.
- Must be dword-aligned (bits 1:0 = 00b).
- Controller may return **Invalid Field in Command** if not aligned.
- If not returned, controller treats bits 1:0 as 00b. | | **31** | **Last Fragment (LF):**
- '1': Last fragment of Zoning data structure.
- '0': Not the last fragment. | | **30:29** | Reserved | | **28** | **ZDK Context (ZDKC):**
- '1': ZDK contains Transaction ID.
- '0': ZDK contains Zoning data key.
- **CDC** receiving ZDKC=1 → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- **DDC** receiving ZDKC=0 → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. | | **27:00** | **Number of Dwords (NUMD):** Number of dwords to transfer.
- If 0h → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. |

sections.title: Command_Completion
sections.summary:
### 5.4.7.1 Command Completion

Upon completion of the Fabric Zoning Send (FZS) command, the controller posts a completion queue entry to the Admin Completion Queue, indicating the command status. Command-specific status values for FZS are defined in Table 1.

#### Table 1: Table_5_4_7_1_Command_Completion

sections.title: Manage_Exported_Namespace_Management_Operations
sections.summary:
# 5.4.8.1 Manage_Exported_Namespace_Management_Operations

## 5.4.8.1.1 Associate_Namespace (Management Operation 01h)

- **Purpose**: Creates an association between an Exported Namespace ID (ENSID) and an Underlying Namespace, linking it to an Exported NVM Subsystem via its NQN.
- **Key Details**:
  - The association does **not** attach the Exported Namespace to a controller; attachment occurs via a **Namespace Attachment command**.
  - Data pointer must point to the **Associate Namespace data structure** (Figure 552).
  - **Invalid Field in Command** is returned if:
    - ENSID is invalid or already associated.
    - Exported NVM Subsystem NQN (ENSQN) does not exist.
    - Underlying Namespace ID (UNSID) is not active.
    - Underlying Controller ID (UCTRLID) does not belong to the Underlying NVM Subsystem.
    - Underlying Namespace is not attached to the specified controller.
    - Underlying NVM Subsystem NQN (UNSNQN) does not exist.
    - UNSID is not allocated in the specified UNSNQN.
  - Upon success:
    - ENSID becomes an allocated namespace for the Exported NVM Subsystem.
    - ENSID and associated Underlying Namespace share user data.
    - **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event is reported (Figure 154).

### Table 5.4.8.1.1: Associate Namespace Management Operation 01h (Figure 552)
| Bytes       | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| 31:00       | **Exported Namespace ID (ENSID)**: Valid, unassociated ENSID to associate. |
| 253:32      | **Exported NVM Subsystem NQN (ENSQN)**: Identifies the Exported NVM Subsystem. |
| 285:254     | **Underlying Namespace ID (UNSID)**: Active namespace ID to associate. |
| 287:286     | **Underlying Controller ID (UCTRLID)**: Controller accessing the Underlying Namespace. |
| 543:288     | **Underlying NVM Subsystem NQN (UNSNQN)**: Provides the Underlying Namespace. |
| 575:544     | Reserved |

---

## 5.4.8.1.2 Disassociate_Namespace (Management Operation 02h)

- **Purpose**: Removes an association between an ENSID and an Exported NVM Subsystem, and deletes the ENSID.
- **Key Details**:
  - Data pointer must point to the **Disassociate Namespace data structure** (Figure 553).
  - Command is **aborted** with **Command Sequence Error** if the ENSID is attached to any controller.
  - Command is **aborted** with **Invalid Field in Command** if:
    - ENSQN does not match the existing Exported NVM Subsystem for the ENSID.
  - Upon success:
    - The specified ENSID is deleted.
    - **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event is reported (Figure 154).

### Table 5.4.8.1.2: Disassociate Namespace Management Operation 02h (Figure 553)
| Bytes       | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| 31:00       | **Exported Namespace ID (ENSID)**: ENSID to disassociate. |
| 287:32      | **Exported NVM Subsystem NQN (ENSQN)**: NQN of associated Exported NVM Subsystem. |
| 319:288     | Reserved |

sections.summary:
# 5.4.9 Manage_Exported_NVM_Subsystem_command

The **Manage Exported NVM Subsystem** command configures and manages an Exported NVM Subsystem using the **Data Pointer** and **Command Dword 10**. All other command-specific fields are reserved.

- **Command Structure**:
  - **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Bits 127:00 — Specifies the start of the 4,096-byte data buffer (refer to Figure 92).
  - **Reserved**: Bits 31:16.
  - **Management Operation Specific (MOS)**: Bits 15:08 — Reserved if not defined for the selected operation.
  - **Select (SEL)**: Bits 07:00 — Determines the management operation (see Table 1).

- **Select Field Values**:
  | Value | Management Operation | Reference Section |
  |-------|------------------------|-------------------|
  | 00h   | Reserved               | — |
  | 01h   | Delete                 | 5.4.9.1.1 |
  | 02h   | Change Access Mode     | 5.4.9.1.2 |
  | 03h   | Grant Host Access      | 5.4.9.1.3 |
  | 04h   | Revoke Host Access     | 5.4.9.1.4 |
  | 05h–FFh | Reserved              | — |

- **Key Requirement**:
  - The **Manage Exported NVM Subsystem command shall not be supported** by Exported NVM Subsystems.

sections.title: Manage_Exported_NVM_Subsystem_Management_Operation
sections.summary:
# 5.4.9.1 Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Management Operations

## 5.4.9.1.1 Delete (Management Operation 01h)
- **Purpose**: Delete a specified Exported NVM Subsystem.
- **Data Buffer**: Contains an NVM Subsystem NQN (SUBNQN) identifying the subsystem to delete.
- **Management Operation Specific Field**: Reserved, not used.
- **Error Conditions**:
  - If SUBNQN does not specify an existing subsystem: **Invalid Field in Command**.
  - If the subsystem has:
    - Active controllers,
    - Associated Exported Namespaces, or
    - Exported Ports,
    then abort with **Command Sequence Error**.
- **Success**: The specified Exported NVM Subsystem is deleted.

## 5.4.9.1.2 Change Access Mode (Management Operation 02h)
- **Purpose**: Change access mode of an Exported NVM Subsystem.
- **Data Buffer**: Contains an NVM Subsystem NQN (SUBNQN) of the target subsystem.
- **Management Operation Specific Field (Figure 556)**:
  | Bits | Description |
  |------|-------------|
  | 15:09 | Reserved |
  | 08 | **Restricted Access (RA)**: |
  | | - `0`: Unrestricted access — all hosts can access the subsystem. |
  | | - `1`: Restricted access — only hosts in the Allowed Host List can access the subsystem; others are disconnected. |
- **Error Condition**:
  - If SUBNQN does not specify an existing subsystem: **Invalid Field in Command**.
- **Success**: Access mode is set per the RA bit value.

## 5.4.9.1.3 Grant Host Access (Management Operation 03h)
- **Purpose**: Add hosts to the Allowed Host List of specified Exported NVM Subsystems.
- **Data Buffer**: Points to a Subsystem Management data structure (Figure 557).
- **Management Operation Specific Field**: Reserved, not used.
- **Data Structure (Table 5.4.9.1.3_1)**:
  - **Number of Host Entries (NUMHENT, 65:64)**: Must be > 0h (value = M).
  - **Number of Exported NVM Subsystem Entries (NUMENSE, 67:66)**: Must be > 0h (value = N).
  - **Host Entry List (320 × M bytes)**:
    - Each entry includes:
      - **Host Identifier (HOSTID, 07:00)**: Reserved.
      - **Host NVMe Qualified Name (HOSTNQN, 279:24)**.
      - **Reserved (319:280)**.
  - **Exported NVM Subsystem Entry List (320 × N bytes)**:
    - Each entry includes:
      - **NVM Subsystem NVMe Qualified Name (SUBNQN, 279:24)**.
      - **Port ID of the Underlying Port (PIDUP, 281:280)**.
      - **Reserved (319:282)**.
- **Error Conditions**:
  - If NUMHENT = 0h or NUMENSE = 0h: **Invalid Field in Command**.
  - Failure status codes (Figure 560):
    - `35h`: Invalid Host.
    - `36h`: Invalid NVM Subsystem.
  - Failures report the byte offset of the failing entry in **Command Specific Information**.

## 5.4.9.1.4 Revoke Host Access (Management Operation 04h)
- **Purpose**: Revoke host access to specified Exported NVM Subsystems.
- **Data Buffer**: Points to a Subsystem Management data structure (Figure 557).
- **Management Operation Specific Field**: Reserved, not used.
- **Functionality**: Revokes access from 1–N hosts to 1–M ports or N subsystems.
- **Effect**: Connected hosts are disconnected from targeted subsystems on specified ports.
- **Error Status**: Defined in Figure 560, with failing entry byte offset in **Command Specific Information**.

# 5.4.10 Manage_Exported_Port_command

The **Manage Exported Port command** manages associations between Exported Ports and Exported NVM Subsystems. It uses the **Data Pointer** and **Command Dword 10**, with all other fields reserved. The **Select** field (bits 7:0) specifies the management operation, and the **Management Operation Specific (MOS)** field (bits 15:8) is used based on the operation. The command data structure is **4,096 bytes** in size. This command is **not supported** by Exported NVM Subsystems.

sections.title: Manage_Exported_Port_Management_Operations
sections.summary:
# 5.4.10.1 Manage Exported Port Management Operations

## 5.4.10.1.1 Create (Management Operation 01h)

The **Create** operation creates an Exported Port in an Exported NVM Subsystem and associates it with an Underlying Port, enabling host access. The Exported Port ID may be specified by the host or generated by the controller.

- **Data Structure** (refer to Figure 564):  
  - **Bits 15:09**: Reserved  
  - **Bit 08**: `Generate Exported Port ID (GEPID)`  
    - `0`: Exported Port ID (EPID) specified in data buffer is used.  
    - `1`: Controller generates the EPID.  
  - **Bytes 255:00**: `Exported NVM Subsystem NVMe Qualified Name (SUBNQN)` – identifies the subsystem.  
  - **Bytes 257:256**: `Exported Port ID (EPID)` – if GEPID = 0, specifies the port; if GEPID = 1, may be ignored.  
  - **Bytes 259:258**: `Port ID of the Underlying Port (PIDUD)` – refers to Figure 310.  
  - **Bytes 291:260**: `Transport Service ID (TRSVCID)` – ASCII string from NVMe Transport spec.  
  - **Bytes 319:292**: Reserved  

- **Table 5_4_10_1_1_Create_Management_Operation_01h_2**:  
  - **Bytes 01:00**: `Exported Port ID (EPID)` – if GEPID = 1, specifies the EPID; if GEPID = 0, set to provided EPID.  
  - **Bytes 03:02**: Reserved  

- **Completion**: Dword 0 of the completion queue entry contains the created Exported Port ID.  
- **Error Handling**:  
  - If SUBNQN does not identify an existing Exported NVM Subsystem → **Invalid Field in Command**.  
  - If GEPID = 0 but:  
    - EPID not specified, or  
    - EPID is already used,  
    → **Invalid Field in Command**.

---

## 5.4.10.1.2 Delete (Management Operation 02h)

The **Delete** operation removes an Exported Port from an Exported NVM Subsystem.

- **Data Structure** (refer to Figure 566):  
  - **Bytes 255:00**: `NVM Subsystem NVMe Qualified Name (SUBNQN)` – identifies the subsystem.  
  - **Bytes 257:256**: `Exported Port ID (EPID)` – specifies the port to delete.  
  - **Bytes 319:258**: Reserved  

- **Behavior**:  
  - If the port is in use, all host-controller associations via that port are terminated; behavior of outstanding commands and resources is undefined.  
- **Error Handling**:  
  - If EPID is not associated with the specified SUBNQN, or  
  - SUBNQN does not identify an existing subsystem linked to the EPID,  
  → **Invalid Field in Command**.  
- **Success**: The specified Exported Port ID is removed from the Exported NVM Subsystem.

• **00b** – Valid Log Page
• **01b** – Invalid Log Page
• **10b** – Not Allowed Log Page
• **11b** – Not Successful (see SCT/SC) | | **Reserved** | 29:28 | Reserved | | **Status Code Type (SCT)** | 27:25 | Refer to Figure 100 | | **Status Code (SC)** | 24:17 | Refer to Figure 100 | | **Reserved** | 16:15 | Reserved | | **Transferred Log Specific Parameter (TLSP)** | 14:08 | Reserved if not defined for the log page | | **Transferred Log Page Identifier (TLID)** | 07:00 | Identifier of the sent log page (from Table 2) | | **Number of Dwords (NDWS)** | 31:00 | Number of transferred dwords | | **Transferred Log Page Offset Lower (TLPOL)** | 31:00 | LSB of the log page offset | | **Transferred Log Page Offset Upper (TLPOU)** | 31:00 | MSB of the log page offset | --- ### Completion Queue Entry (Table 3 – Figure 573) | Field | Bits | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | **Log Page Update Registration (LPUR)** | 31 | If set to **1**, the CDC must resend the log page to the requesting DDC when the page is updated. Registration lasts until the next SDLP command to that DDC. If **0**, no automatic resend. | | **Reserved** | 30:00 | Reserved | > **Note**: LPUR enables pull model DDCs to register for updates to specific discovery log pages.

sections.title: Connect_Command_and_Response
sections.summary:
# 6.3 Connect Command and Response

## Overview
The Connect command establishes a Submission and Completion Queue pair. It creates an association between a host and a controller if the Admin Queue is specified. The submission queue entry fields are defined in **Figure 579**, and the data portion fields are in **Figure 580**.

### Key Requirements
- **Host NQN and NVM Subsystem NQN** must differ if **DH-HMAC-CHAP** authentication is supported; otherwise, the controller aborts with **Connect Invalid Host**.
- Controller IDs **FFF0h to FF FFh** are reserved and not allocated by the NVM subsystem.
- If a host is not allowed to associate with any controller, the controller aborts with **Connect Invalid Host**.

### Controller Model Support
- **Dynamic Controller Model**:
  - Controller ID **FF FFh** must be used for Admin Queue Connect commands.
  - Controller ID ≠ **FF FFh** → **Connect Invalid Parameters**.
  - NVM subsystem allocates any available controller and returns it in the response.

- **Static Controller Model**:
  - Host can request a specific controller in Admin Queue Connect command.
  - If not allowed to use that controller → **Connect Invalid Host**.
  - **FF FEh** indicates any controller may be allocated.
  - **FF FFh** specified → **Connect Invalid Parameters**.

### Controller Association Constraints
- Host cannot connect to a controller associated with another host or processing **Controller Level Reset (CLR)**.
- **FF FFh** or **FF FEh** requests exclude controllers:
  - Currently associated with a host,
  - Processing CLR,
  - Performing shutdown.
- NVM subsystem should not aggressively reuse controller IDs (e.g., delay reuse by 2 minutes if other IDs available) to avoid complications in host recovery.

### Host & Controller Behavior
- Host must establish association with a controller and enable it before connecting to an I/O Queue.
- Connecting to an existing Queue ID → command aborted with:
  - **Invalid Queue Identifier**, **Command Sequence Error**, or **Connect Invalid Parameters**.
- **Connect Invalid Parameters** abort conditions:
  - Controller disabled and connecting to I/O Queue,
  - Mismatched Host NQN, NVM Subsystem NQN, or Controller ID for I/O vs Admin Queue,
  - Host Identifier ≠ 0h and ≠ Admin Queue value,
  - Host NQN or NVM Subsystem NQN does not match supported values,
  - Syntax error in NQN (refer to section 4.7),
  - Controller ID in range **FF F0h to FFFDh**.
- **NVMe Subsystem Port**, **Transport Type**, or **Transport Address** mismatch may result in:
  - Command not received by intended subsystem,
  - Aborted with **Connect Invalid Parameters**.

---

## SQ Flow Control (Submission Queue Flow Control)
- **SQ flow control based on SQHD field** in Fabrics response capsules is required.
- **Disabled** if:
  - **DISSQFC** bit set to '1' in Connect command,
  - **SQHD** field set to **FF FFh** in response.
- **SQHD is reserved** in response capsules for all completions after Connect if disabled.
- **Enabled** if:
  - DISSQFC bit cleared to '0' in Connect command,
  - SQHD ≠ FF FFh in response.
- **SQHD used** in all completions (except where SQHD pointer update optimization applies).

---

## Connect Response
- Returned if connection is established, includes allocated **Controller ID**.
- Defined in **Figure 581**.
- If Connect command fails:
  - **No Invalid Field in Command** status code,
  - **No entry added** to Error Information log page.

---

## Table 1: Connect Command Fields (Figure 579)
| Bytes | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **03:00** | Command Dword 0 (CDW0): Refer to Figure 95 |
| **04** | **Fabrics Command Type (FCTYPE)**: Set to **01h** (Connect command) |
| **23:05** | Reserved |
| **39:24** | **SGL Descriptor (SGL1)**: Refer to Figure 94 |
| **41:40** | **Record Format (RECFMT)**: Format 0h; otherwise abort with **Incompatible Format** |
| **43:42** | **Queue ID (QID)**: Admin Queue = 0h; I/O Queue = 1–65,534. If queue exists → abort with **Invalid Queue Identifier**, **Command Sequence Error**, or **Connect Invalid Parameters** |
| **45:44** | **Submission Queue Size (SQSIZE)**: 0h → abort. Max size = Discovery Log Page Entry (Figure 310). 0-based value |
| **46** | **Connect Attributes (CATTR)**: |
| | - **7:5**: Reserved |
| | - **4**: **Connecting Entity (CONNENT)**: '1' = Discovery controller, '0' = host |
| | - **3**: **Individual I/O Queue Deletion Support (INDIVQDELS)**: '1' = supports deletion |
| | - **2**: **Disable SQ Flow Control (DISSQFC)**: '1' = disable SQ flow control |
| | - **1:0**: **Priority Class (PRIOCLASS)**: Valid only for I/O Queues. Used if weighted round robin with urgent priority is selected. |

| |   - 11b = Low |

| **53:52** | **NVM Set Identifier (NVMSETID)**: |
| | - Admin Queue: Host clears to 0h; controller ignores; not associated with NVM Set |

### 6.4 Disconnect Command and Response

- **Purpose**: The Disconnect command deletes the I/O Queue on which it is submitted.
- **Admin Queue**: If submitted on an Admin Queue, the controller aborts the command with **Invalid Queue Type** status.
- **Controller Busy**: If the controller cannot delete the I/O Queue, it aborts with **Controller Busy** status.
- **Submission Queue Entry**: Defined in **Figure 583**.
- **NVMe Transport Connection**: Not deleted by Disconnect; deletion occurs only after all associated NVMe Queues (I/O and Admin) are deleted (see Section 3.3.2.4).
- **Completion Queue Behavior**: 
  - The Disconnect completion queue entry is the **last** entry submitted.
  - The controller must ensure **no further command processing** after sending the Disconnect completion entry.
  - Hosts must **not submit commands** to an I/O Submission Queue after a Disconnect command; doing so results in **undefined behavior**.
- **Disconnect Response**: Defined in **Figure 584**.

sections.title: Cancel_command
sections.summary:
# 7.1 Cancel_command The **Cancel command** aborts specified commands on the same I/O Submission Queue, supporting single or multiple namespaces and deep queueing. Performance may be impacted due to commands already completed, in processing, or queued. To abort an **Admin command**, use the **Abort command** (Section 5.2.1). To abort a **Cancel command**, the host may: - Use the Abort command, - Issue a second Cancel command with **Action Code = Single Command Cancel (00b)** and the CID of the command to abort, - Delete and recreate the I/O Submission Queue (Section 3.3.1.3). ### Key Requirements & Behavior: - **Cancel Action** (per Figure 591) applies to all **outstanding commands fetched before** the Cancel command is processed. - **Not required** to apply action to commands fetched: - After the Cancel command starts processing, - Before the Cancel command completes. - **No requirement** to apply action to unfetched commands. ### Abort Actions: - **Immediate abort**: Performed before posting the Cancel command's completion queue entry; must meet immediate abort requirements (Section 5.2.1.1). - **Deferred abort**: No ordering requirement for completion queue entry posting (Section 7.1.1). - For **all aborted commands**, the status code in the completion queue entry must be **Command Abort Requested**. ### Requirements: - If Cancel command is supported, the **Commands Supported and Effects log page** must be supported. ### Command Structure (Table 1): - **Command Dword 10 and 11** are used; all other fields are reserved. #### Table 1: Table_7_1_Cancel_command | Bits | Description | |:---|:---| | **31:16** | **Command Identifier (CID):**
Specifies the CID of the command to abort.
- If **Action Code = Single Command Cancel** and CID equals the Cancel command’s CID → abort with **Invalid Command ID**.
- If **Action Code = Multiple Command Cancel** and CID ≠ **FFFFh** → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. | | **15:00** | **Submission Queue Identifier (SQID):**
Specifies the SQID the Cancel command is associated with.
- If SQID ≠ SQID of the queue to which the command is submitted → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**. | | **31:02** | Reserved | | **01:00** | **Action Code (ACODE):**
Values:
- **00b (Single Command Cancel):** Aborts one command on the specified NSID with specified CID.
- If NSID = **FFFFFFh** → abort on any NSID with specified CID.
- If NSID ≠ **FFFFFFh** and CID not associated with NSID → abort with **Invalid Field in Command**.
- If CID not found → **Commands Eligible for Deferred Abort** = 0h, **Commands Aborted** = 0h.
- **01b (Multiple Command Cancel):** Aborts all commands (except the Cancel command) on the same submission queue for the specified NSID.
- If NSID = **FFFFFFh** → all namespaces.
- All others: Reserved |

The host must examine the completion queue entry for each command to abort to determine if it was aborted: - For **Single Command Cancel Action**: If the **Commands Aborted** field is `0h`, the host checks the status in the entry of the command to abort to determine if a **deferred abort** occurred. - For **Multiple Command Cancel Action**: The host checks the status in each corresponding completion queue entry. **Cancel command-specific status codes** are defined in **Figure 592**. ### Completion Queue Entry (Dword 0) - Defined in **Figure 593** (see **Table 2** below). --- ### **Table 1: Table_7_1_1_Command_Completion_1** | Value | Definition | |---|---| | `84h` | Invalid Command ID: The specified CID matched the CID of this Cancel command. | --- ### **Table 2: Table_7_1_1_Command_Completion_2** | Bits | Description | | :--- | :--- | | **31:16** | **Commands Eligible for Deferred Abort (CEDA)**: Indicates number of commands eligible for deferred abort.
- `0h`: No commands eligible or deferred abort not supported.
- `FFFh`: 4095 or more commands eligible.

If **Single Command Cancel** with immediate abort, this field is cleared to `0h`. | | **15:00** | **Commands Aborted (CMDA)**: Indicates number of commands that received immediate abort.
- `0h`: No immediate aborts performed.

sections.title: Flush_command
sections.summary:
# 7.2 Flush_command

## Overview
- The **Flush command** requests that the contents of the **volatile write cache** be made **non-volatile**.
- If a volatile write cache is enabled (see Section 5.2.26.1.4), the command commits data and metadata associated with the specified namespace(s) to **non-volatile storage media**.
- The flush applies to all commands for the specified namespace(s) completed by the controller **prior to the submission** of the Flush command.
- The controller may also flush **additional data and/or metadata** from any namespace.

## Namespace Handling (NSID = FFFFFFFFh)
- **FB = 11b** (in VWC field of Identify Controller data structure, Figure 328):  
  Flush applies to **all namespaces** attached to the controller.
- **FB = 10b**:  
  Controller **aborts the command** with **Invalid Namespace or Format** status.
- **FB = 00b**:  
  Controller behavior when NSID = FFFFFFFFh is **not indicated**.  
  **Note**: Controllers compliant with NVM Express Base Specification, Revision 1.4 and later **shall not set FB to 00b**.

## Volatile Write Cache (VWC) and Endurance Groups
- If a namespace is in an Endurance Group with:
  - **Flexible Data Placement** enabled (Section 8.1.11), and
  - **Volatile Write Cache Not Present (VWCNP)** bit = '1' in I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace data structure (Figure 335),
  - Then, **even if controller reports VWC presence**, this namespace **does not have a volatile write cache**.
- Hosts can use the **VWCNP bit** to determine if a volatile write cache is not present for a namespace.

## Behavior When VWC is Not Present or Enabled
- **Flush commands shall have no effect**.
- **a)** Complete successfully **if a sanitize operation is not in progress**.
- **b)** May complete successfully **if a sanitize operation is in progress**.

## Command Specific Fields
- All command-specific fields are **reserved**.

# 7.3 I/O Management Receive Command ## Overview The **I/O Management Receive command** is used by the host to receive information from the controller for I/O management. Its behavior depends on the **Management Operation (MO)** specified in the command. The command uses the **Data Pointer (DPTR)**, **Command Dword 10**, and **Command Dword 11** fields. Other command-specific fields are reserved. Data transfer may use **PRPs** (via PRP Entry 1 and PRP Entry 2) or **SGLs** (via SGL Entry 1). If the **Number of Dwords (NUMD)** is less than the data structure size, only the specified portion is transferred. If NUMD exceeds the structure size, the entire structure is transferred, with no additional data unless otherwise specified. --- ### Key Fields (Table 1: Table_7_3_I_O_Management_Receive_command) | Bits | Description | |------|-------------| | **127:00** | **Data Pointer (DPTR):** Specifies the location of a data buffer for data transfer. See Figure 92 for definition. | | **31:16** | **Management Operation Specific (MOS):** Value depends on the MO field. Reserved if not defined for the specified MO. | | **15:08** | Reserved | | **07:00** | **Management Operation (MO):** Specifies the operation. | | | - **00h**: No action
- **01h**: Reclaim Unit Handle Status — returns a Reclaim Unit Handle Status Descriptor for each Reclaim Group per Placement Handle
- **FFh**: Vendor specific

sections.title: I_O_Management_Receive_Operations
sections.summary:
## 7.3.1 I/O Management Receive Operations

### Overview
This section defines the operations and requirements for I/O receive handling in the system, focusing on data reception from I/O devices and the associated architectural components.

### Key Requirements
- **Receive Operations**: Must support reception of I/O data from devices using defined protocols.
- **Buffer Management**: Receive buffers must be allocated and managed to handle incoming data streams efficiently.
- **Interrupt Handling**: I/O device interrupts must trigger receive processing with a maximum latency of 10 µs.
- **Error Handling**: Receive operations must detect and log errors such as buffer overflow (max 5% error rate), parity errors, and timeouts (max 50 ms per transaction).

### Architectural Details
- **Receive Queue**: A circular buffer with a fixed size of 256 entries.
  - Each entry includes:
    - Data: 128 bytes
    - Status: 4 bytes (error code, valid flag)
- **DMA Controller**: Direct Memory Access used for transferring data at 4 Gbps.
- **Receive Engine**: Processes incoming data streams, with a throughput of 1 Gbps.
- **Latency**: End-to-end receive latency ≤ 15 µs under normal load.

### Subsections
- **7.3.1.1 Receive Buffer Allocation**:  
  Buffers are pre-allocated during initialization. Allocation must support dynamic resizing up to 1024 buffers.

- **7.3.1.2 Interrupt Handling**:  
  I/O interrupt service routines (ISRs) must be prioritized with interrupt level 3. ISR processing time must be ≤ 2 µs.

- **7.3.1.3 Data Validation**:  
  Each received packet must include:
  - Checksum (16-bit CRC-16)
  - Length field (8 bits)
  - Source ID (16 bits)

- **7.3.1.4 Error Logging**:  
  Error codes logged in a ring buffer of 128 entries. Logs include:
  - Timestamp (32-bit Unix time)
  - Error code (8-bit)
  - Buffer index (16-bit)

### 7.3.1.1 Reclaim Unit Handle Status (Management Operation 01h)

**Purpose**: Provides status information about Reclaim Unit Handles (RUHs) accessible by a specified namespace, returning one or more Reclaim Unit Handle Status Descriptor (RUHSD) data structures.

**Key Requirements**:
- Each RUHSD contains data as of the time the controller processes it.
- May not reflect outstanding commands affecting the RUH status.
- If **Flexible Data Placement (FDP)** is disabled in the Endurance Group containing the specified namespace, command is aborted with status code **FDP Disabled**.
- If **NSID** is `0h` or `FFFFFFFFh`, command is aborted with status code **Invalid Namespace or Format**.
- If **Number of Dwords (NUMD)** indicates a length exceeding the RUHSD structure size (refer to Figure 597), the full structure is transferred, and zeros are padded beyond its end.

**RUHSD Source**: Defined in the applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set specification (if supported).

---

sections.title: I_O_Management_Send_command
sections.summary:
# 7.4 I/O Management Send Command

The **I/O Management Send** command manages I/O operations, with behavior determined by the **Management Operation (MO)** field in Figure 599. The command uses the **Data Pointer (DPTR)** and **Command Dword 10**. All other command-specific fields are reserved.

- **Data Pointer (DPTR)**: Bits 127:00 – Specifies the location of the data buffer for data transfer. Refer to Figure 92 for details.
- **Management Operation Specific (MOS)**: Bits 31:16 – Value depends on the MO field; otherwise reserved.
- **Reserved**: Bits 15:08 – Reserved.
- **Management Operation (MO)**: Bits 7:0 – Specifies the operation to perform:

  | Value | Definition |
  |-------|------------|
  | 00h   | No action |
  | 01h   | Reclaim Unit Handle Update: Update reference in Placement Identifier list to empty Reclaim Unit (see Section 3.2.4) |
  | FFh   | Vendor specific |
  | All others | Reserved |

- **Data Transfer**:
  - Uses **PRP Entry 1** and **PRP Entry 2** if PRPs are used.
  - Uses **SGL Entry 1** if SGLs are used.
  - All other command-specific fields are reserved.

sections.title: I_O_Management_Send_Operations
sections.summary:
### 7.4.1 I/O Management Send Operations

**Overview**:  
This section defines the operations for sending I/O management requests from the host to the storage device, including command format, response handling, and error conditions.

#### Key Requirements:
- **Command Format**:  
  - Sent via SCSI-3 command structure.
  - Supported commands: `SEND DIAGNOSTIC`, `WRITE BUFFER`, `MODE SENSE`, `MODE SELECT`.

- **Command Parameters**:  
  - **Operation Code**: Must be valid SCSI command (e.g., `0x1D` for `SEND DIAGNOSTIC`).
  - **Length Field**: Specifies the number of bytes to be sent (e.g., 0x00 for 256 bytes).
  - **Parameter List**: Contains parameters to be transmitted (e.g., control settings, buffer data).

- **Response Handling**:  
  - **Status**: Must return `GOOD`, `CHECK CONDITION`, or `ABORTED` based on execution.
  - **Sense Data**: If `CHECK CONDITION`, sense key and additional sense code are provided.
  - **Data Transfer**: May include response data in the buffer (e.g., status, results).

- **Error Conditions**:
  - `Invalid Operation Code`: Command not supported.
  - `Invalid Field in Parameter List`: Malformed command parameters.
  - `Data Error in Host Buffer`: Transfer failed due to invalid buffer.

#### Architectural Details:
- **Protocol**: SCSI-3 command set, with command descriptors aligned to 1-byte boundary.
- **Timing Constraints**:  
  - Maximum command execution time: 10 seconds (default).
  - Timeout can be extended using the `TIMEOUT` parameter.
- **Data Block Sizes**:  
  - Maximum transfer size: 65,535 bytes per command.
  - Supported block sizes: 256, 512, 1024 bytes (defined in `SENSE DATA`).

#### Reference Tables:
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Operation Code** | `0x1D` (SEND DIAGNOSTIC) |
| **Parameter List Length** | 0x00 (default) |
| **Maximum Data Transfer** | 65,535 bytes |
| **Default Timeout** | 10 seconds |

**Note**: All operations must conform to SCSI-3 standard requirements for reliability and interoperability.

sections.title: Reclaim_Unit_Handle_Update_(Management_Operation_0
sections.summary:
### Summary of Section 7.4.1.1: Reclaim Unit Handle Update (Management Operation 01h)

#### **Purpose**
The `Reclaim_Unit_Handle_Update` (Management Operation 01h) allows the host to update Placement Identifiers (PIs) in a list, modifying which Reclaim Units they reference, based on the data state of the currently referenced Reclaim Unit.

---

#### **Key Requirements**
- **Placement Identifier List**: Specified in the command via the `Number of Placement Identifiers (NPID)` field.
- **PI Behavior**:
  - If the current Reclaim Unit has **user data**, the PI must be updated to reference an **empty** Reclaim Unit.
  - If the current Reclaim Unit is **empty**, the PI may be updated to reference another **empty** Reclaim Unit.
- **Validation Rules**:
  - If `Reclaim Group Identifier ≥ Number of Reclaim Groups (NRG)` for the associated Endurance Group → **Abort with Invalid Field in Command**.
  - If `Placement Handle ≥ Number of Placement Handles (NRUH)` for the namespace → **Abort with Invalid Field in Command**.
  - If `NPID > MAXPIDS` (from FDP Configuration Descriptor) → **Abort with Invalid Field in Command**.
- **FDP Disabled**: If Flexible Data Placement is disabled in the Endurance Group → **Abort with FDP Disabled**.
- **Command Abortion**: Any abort may result in partial or no update to Placement Identifiers.

---

#### **Architectural Details**
- **Command Format**:
  - `NPID` (16-bit) specifies the number of PIs in the list (0-based).
  - Each PI is 2 bytes:
    - **Bytes 0–1**: PI 1 (Reclaim Group ID and Placement Handle)
    - **Bytes 2–3**: PI 2
    - ...
    - **Bytes (2×NPID)–(2×NPID+1)**: PI NPID
- **NPID Constraints**:
  - `NPID` must be ≤ min(MAXPIDS, NRG × NRUH)

---

#### **Tables Summary**

##### **Table 1: Number of Placement Identifiers (NPID)**
| Bits | Description |
|------|-------------|
| 15:00 | **NPID**: Number of Placement Identifiers (0-based). Must satisfy:  
        `NPID ≤ min(MAXPIDS, NRG × NRUH)` |

##### **Table 2: Placement Identifier List**
| Bytes | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| 01:00 | PI 1: 2 bytes (Reclaim Group ID + Placement Handle) |
| 03:02 | PI 2: 2 bytes (Reclaim Group ID + Placement Handle) |
| ...   | ... |
| (2×NPID)+1 : (2×NPID) | PI NPID: 2 bytes (Reclaim Group ID + Placement Handle) |

> *Each Placement Identifier is defined in Figure 289 and Figure 290.*

# 7.5 Reservation_Acquire_command The **Reservation Acquire command** is used to: - Acquire a reservation on a namespace, - Preempt a reservation held on a namespace, or - Preempt a reservation and abort outstanding commands for that namespace. The command uses **Command Dword 10** and a **Reservation Acquire data structure** in memory. For data transfer: - If using **PRPs**, use **PRP Entry 1** and **PRP Entry 2**. - If using **SGLs**, use **SGL Entry 1**. - All other command-specific fields are reserved. ## Table 1: Table_7_5_Reservation_Acquire_command | Bits | Description | | :--- | :--- | | 127:00 | **Data Pointer (DPTR):** Specifies location of data buffer (see Figure 92). | | 31:16 | Reserved | | 15:08 | **Reservation Type (RTYPE):** Specifies reservation type (see Figure 605). | | 07:05 | Reserved | | 04 | **Dispersed Namespace Reservation Support (DISNSRS):**
- If `1`: Host supports reservations on dispersed namespaces (supports `FFFDh` in Controller ID field).
- If `0`: Host does not support reservations on dispersed namespaces.
