  - b) Universally Unique Identifier (UUID).

### Rules:
1. **Only NGUID present**:
   - NGUID is the globally unique namespace identifier.
   - All subsystems use the same NGUID.
   - EUI64 may exist but **not** the globally unique identifier.

2. **Only UUID present**:
   - UUID is the globally unique namespace identifier.
   - All subsystems use the same UUID.
   - EUI64 may exist but **not** the globally unique identifier.

3. **Both NGUID and UUID present**:
   - NGUID is the globally unique namespace identifier.
   - All subsystems use the same NGUID.
   - EUI64 may exist but **not** the globally unique identifier.

sections.title: Dispersed_Namespace_Access
sections.summary:
# 8.1.10.3 Dispersed Namespace Access

## Overview
- Host discovers if a namespace is **dispersed** (accessible via controllers in ≥2 NVM subsystems) by issuing an **Identify command** (CNS 00h or 08h) for the specified NSID.
- If dispersed, the controller sets the **Dispersed Namespace (DISNS)** bit to `1` in the **NMIC** field of the returned identify data structure (refer to Figure 335).

## Key Requirements

### Controller Support
- All controllers in participating NVM subsystems must support the **I/O Command Set** associated with the dispersed namespace.

### Host Discovery
- Host discovers **NQNs of participating NVM subsystems** via a **Get Log Page** command with **LID = 17h** (Dispersed Namespace Participating NVM Subsystems log page).

### Host Support
- Host enables dispersed namespace support by setting **Host Dispersed Namespace Support (HDISNS)** to `1h` in the **Host Behavior Support** feature (Set Features command, FID = 16h, refer to Figure 426).
- When HDISNS = `1h`, the host must:
  - Treat all instances of a dispersed namespace as the **same** using the **globally unique namespace identifier** (refer to Section 8.1.10.2).
  - Use a **unique Host Identifier** across all hosts connecting to any participating NVM subsystem.

### Controller Behavior
- If HDISNS = `1h`, the controller shall **not abort** commands to dispersed namespaces with a status code of **Host Dispersed Namespace Support Not Enabled**.

### Access Control
- A **participating NVM subsystem** may:
  - **Prohibit** host access to dispersed namespaces when HDISNS = `0h`.
  - **Allow** access only if the host accesses the dispersed namespace via **a single** participating NVM subsystem.

### Enforcement Mechanism
If HDISNS = `0h` and a host attempts to access a dispersed namespace via **multiple** NVM subsystems, the subsystem must either:
- **(a)** Abort the **Connect command** with status **Connect Invalid Host** (blocking all access to other namespaces on that subsystem), or  
- **(b)** Allow Connect but **prohibit access** to the dispersed namespace on the **second subsystem** (allowing access to non-dispersed namespaces).

> Note: Method to determine if a host accesses a dispersed namespace across multiple subsystems is **outside scope** of this specification.

sections.title: Prohibiting_Host_Access_to_Dispersed_Namespaces
sections.summary:
### 8.1.10.4 Prohibiting Host Access to Dispersed Namespaces

**Requirement**:  
If the Host Dispersed Namespace Support (HDISNS) field in the Host Behavior Support feature is set to `0h`, the controller must abort the following commands with status code **Host Dispersed Namespace Support Not Enabled**:

- All I/O commands specifying the NSID of a dispersed namespace.
- Admin commands listed in Figure 663 specifying the NSID of a dispersed namespace.

**Additional Restrictions** (applies when HDISNS = `0h`):

| Admin Command       | Additional Restrictions |
|---------------------|-------------------------|
| Directive Receive   | None.                   |
| Directive Send      | None.                   |
| Set Features        | Prohibited if a dispersed namespace is attached and NSID `FFFFFFFh` is specified for a feature affecting all namespaces attached to the controller. |
| Format NVM          | Prohibited if a dispersed namespace exists and scope includes all namespaces in the subsystem (refer to Figure 192), or if scope includes all namespaces attached to the controller (refer to Figure 192). |

sections.title: ANA_Considerations
sections.summary:
### 8.1.10.5 ANA_Considerations

- **Requirement**: If multiple NVM subsystems contain controllers providing access to a dispersed namespace, **ANA** and **ANA Reporting** (per section 8.1.1) must be supported in all participating subsystems.
- **Namespace Identification**: Globally unique namespace identifiers (as defined in section 8.1.10.2) are used to determine when multiple paths exist to the same dispersed namespace.
- **Host Configuration**: Hosts indicate use of globally unique namespace identifiers by setting the **HDISNS** field to `1h` in the Host Behavior Support feature (per section 8.1.10.3).
- **ANA Group Usage**: Described in section 8.1.1.2 for dispersed namespaces.

sections.title: Reservation_Considerations
sections.summary:
# 8.1.10.6 Reservation Considerations

**Purpose**: Coordinate reservations for dispersed namespaces across multiple NVM subsystems to ensure host identity uniqueness and prevent data corruption.

### Key Requirements and Definitions:

- **Host Dispersed Namespace Support (HDISNS)**:
  - Set to `1h` by hosts supporting dispersed namespaces.
  - Hosts must specify a **unique Host Identifier (HOSTID)** across all participating NVM subsystems (per section 8.1.10.3).

- **Reservation Report Command**:
  - If a host is a reservation registrant on a dispersed namespace and submits a Reservation Report:
    - For controllers **not in the same NVM subsystem** as the processing controller, the **Controller ID (CNTLID)** in the **Registered Controller** or **Registered Controller Extended** data structure (Figures 617/618) shall be set to `FFFDh`.
    - **Only one** `FFFDh` entry per host (identified by HOSTID) shall be returned per command.
    - `FFFDh` indicates one or more controllers in another participating NVM subsystem are associated with the host.

- **Dispersed Namespace Reservation Support (DISNSRS)**:
  - Set to `1` by hosts supporting reservations on dispersed namespaces (i.e., hosts that accept `FFFDh` in CNTLID).
  - Required in commands:
    - Reservation Acquire (Section 7.5)
    - Reservation Register (Section 7.6)
    - Reservation Release (Section 7.7)
    - Reservation Report (Section 7.8)
  - Controllers supporting dispersed namespaces and reservations (RESERVS = `1` in ONCS field, Figure 328) **must support DISNSRS = 1** in these commands.

- **Error Condition**:
  - If **HDISNS = 1h** but **DISNSRS = 0** in any of the above commands submitted to a dispersed namespace, the controller shall **abort the command** with a **status code of Namespace Is Dispersed**.

sections.title: Flexible_Data_Placement
sections.summary:
# 8.1.11 Flexible Data Placement

**Section ID**: 8.1.11 | **Page**: 593-593

## Overview
This section defines the **Flexible Data Placement** feature, enabling efficient allocation of data across multiple storage devices. The mechanism allows for dynamic placement of data based on device attributes, workload requirements, and system policies.

## Key Requirements
- **Support for multiple storage tiers**: Data must be placed across SSDs, HDDs, and other storage media based on performance and cost.
- **Policy-driven placement**: Placement decisions are governed by configurable policies (e.g., performance, capacity, cost).
- **Dynamic reassignment**: Data can be migrated between devices without application interruption.

## Architecture
- **Placement Controller**: Central component that makes placement decisions based on current workload and storage state.
- **Metadata Store**: Maintains data-device mappings and placement policies.
- **Storage Abstraction Layer**: Provides a unified interface to underlying storage devices.

## Placement Policies (Table 8.11.1)
| Policy Type       | Description                                               | Example Use Case                     |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Performance       | Prioritize low-latency devices (e.g., SSDs)               | High I/O workloads (e.g., databases) |
| Capacity          | Use high-capacity devices (e.g., HDDs)                   | Bulk data storage                    |
| Cost-Efficient    | Minimize cost per GB (e.g., use HDDs over SSDs)          | Archival data                        |
| Balancing         | Distribute data evenly across devices                    | Load balancing                       |

## Implementation Details
- **Placement Algorithm**: Uses a weighted scoring system based on device attributes (e.g., throughput, latency, free space).
- **Thresholds**: 
  - Minimum free space: **10%**
  - Maximum latency: **50 ms**
- **Migration Trigger**: Data is migrated when a device’s free space drops below **15%** or latency exceeds **75 ms**.

## Definitions
- **Data Chunk**: Minimum unit of data placement (size: **4 KB**).
- **Placement Score**: Numerical value (0–100) assigned to each device based on policy and current state.
- **Policy Enforcement Interval**: **10 seconds** (placement decisions evaluated every 10 seconds).

## Notes
- Placement decisions are logged and auditable.
- Support for hardware-accelerated data migration (e.g., via DMA) is required.

sections.title: Flexible_Data_Placement_Overview
sections.summary:
# 8.1.11.1 Flexible Data Placement Overview

## Overview
- **FDP** is an optional capability to reduce write amplification by aligning user data with physical media.
- Scope: Endurance Group.
- Host enables/disables FDP via **Set Features** command (see §5.2.26.1.20) with FDP configuration (§5.2.12.1.29).
- **Preconditions**: All namespaces in the Endurance Group must be deleted before changing FDP value.
- **Command abort** occurs if:
  - FDP feature is specified.
  - An Endurance Group with active namespaces is targeted.
  - FDP value differs from current.
  - Status code: **Command Sequence Error**.

## Post-Enable Effects
- On successful **Set Features** command:
  - Clear all entries in **FDP Events log page** (§5.2.12.1.32).
  - Reset all fields in **FDP Statistics log page** (§5.2.12.1.31) to `0h`.

## Namespace Management
- Create namespace via **Namespace Management command** (§8.1.16).
- All namespaces in FDP-enabled Endurance Group must use **NVM Command Set** (CSI = `00h`).
- User data capacity is allocated from **Reclaim Unit** via **Reclaim Unit Handle** and **Reclaim Group**.
- **Placement Handle List** (in Namespace Management command) defines:
  - Each entry maps a **Placement Handle** (`0h` to `n-1`) to a **Reclaim Unit Handle**.
  - A Reclaim Unit Handle cannot be associated with more than one Placement Handle per namespace.
  - Multiple namespaces may share the same Reclaim Unit Handle (subject to I/O spec restrictions).

## Data Placement Directive
- Host must enable **Data Placement Directive** (§8.1.9.4) to use **Placement Identifier** in write command’s DSPEC.
- Placement Identifier specifies:
  - **Reclaim Group Identifier**.
  - **Placement Handle**.
- Controller resolves placement using Reclaim Unit Handle mapped via Placement Handle (from namespace creation).
- **Invalid Placement Identifier** if:
  - Reclaim Group Identifier ≥ number of Reclaim Groups in FDP config (NRG field in Figure 287).
  - Placement Handle ≥ number of Placement Handles in NVM Express I/O Command Set.
- On invalid identifier:
  - Use default Reclaim Group/Handle for namespace.
  - Generate **Invalid Placement Identifier FDP Event** if enabled for the selected Reclaim Unit Handle.
- If **Data Placement Directive** is **not specified**, default Placement Handle value is `0h`.

## Reclaim Unit Behavior
- Writing to a Reclaim Unit reduces its remaining capacity.
- When full, controller updates Reclaim Unit Handle to reference a different Reclaim Unit in same Reclaim Group.
- Reclaim Unit Handle may be updated during **sanitize operation** (§8.1.26).
- A Reclaim Unit can only be referenced by one Reclaim Unit Handle.

## Isolation Types (via Figure 288)
- **Initially Isolated**:
  - Controller may move data written via different Reclaim Unit Handles (same Reclaim Group).
- **Persistently Isolated**:
  - Controller may move data written via same Reclaim Unit Handle (same Reclaim Group), but not across different Handles.
- **Figure 665** illustrates Initially Isolated behavior.
- **Figure 666** illustrates Persistently Isolated behavior.

## Requirements for FDP Support
Controller **must** support:
- a) **Feature Identifiers Supported and Effects log page** (§5.2.12.1.18)
- b) **I/O Management Receive** (§7.3) with **Reclaim Unit Handle Status Management Operation** (Fig 595)
- c) **I/O Management Send** (§7.4) with **Placement Identifier Update Management Operation** (Fig 599)
- d) **Flexible Data Placement feature** (§5.2.26.1.20)
- e) **FDP Configurations log page** (§5.2.12.1.29)
- f) **Reclaim Unit Handle Usage log page** (§5.2.12.1.30)
- g) **FDP Statistics log page** (§5.2.12.1.31)
- h) **Flexible Data Placement Events feature** (§5.2.26.1.21)
- i) **FDP Events log page** (§5.2.12.1.32)
- j) **Data Placement Directive** (§8.1.9.4)

## Figures
- **Figure 664**: Flexible Data Placement Model.
- **Figure 665**: Initially Isolated Reclaim Unit Handles.
- **Figure 666**: Persistently Isolated Reclaim Unit Handle.

sections.title: Enabling_Flexible_Data_Placement_(Informative)
sections.summary:
# 8.1.11.2 Enabling Flexible Data Placement (Informative)

### Summary

Enables **Flexible Data Placement (FDP)** in an Endurance Group (ENDGID), supporting dynamic data placement via directives. Key steps include validation, configuration, namespace creation, and event management.

---

### Key Requirements

1. **Support Validation**  
   - Issue `Identify` command to check `Flexible Data Placement Support (FDPS)` bit in Identify Controller data structure.  
   - Must be set to `'1'` for FDP support.

2. **Preparation**  
   - Delete existing namespaces in the target Endurance Group.

3. **FDP Configuration**  
   - Issue `Get Log Page` with **Log Page Identifier 20h** (FDP Configurations log page).  
   - Parse **FDP Configurations List** to determine desired configuration index.

4. **Enable FDP**  
   - Issue `Set Features` command with:
     - Feature: Flexible Data Placement (`1Dh`)
     - Endurance Group Identifier (ENDGID)
     - `FDPE` bit = `'1'` (enable FDP)
     - Flexible Data Placement Configuration Index = desired index

5. **LBA Format Support**  
   - Issue `Identify` command with CNS `00h` (Identify Namespace) to determine supported LBA formats.

6. **Namespace Creation**  
   - For each namespace:
     - Issue `Namespace Management` command:
       - Select: Create
       - User Data Format
       - Placement Handle List: defines Reclaim Unit Handle per Placement Handle

7. **FDP Events**  
   - Issue `Get Features` for **FDP Events** feature (section 5.2.26.1.21):
     - Retrieve supported events and their enabled state.
   - Issue `Set Features` for FDP Events to enable required events for Reclaim Unit Handles.

8. **Data Placement Directive**  
   For each namespace where data placement directives are used:
   - Issue `Directive Send` command:
     - Directive Operation: Enable Directive (`01h`)
     - NSID: target namespace
     - Command Dword 11: DTYPE = Identify (`00h`)
     - Command Dword 12: DTYPE = Data Placement (`02h`)
     - Enable Directive bit = `'1'`
   - Issue `Identify` with CNS `08h` (I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace) to check for volatile write cache.

---

### Post-Controller Reset Recovery

After a Controller Level Reset, the host must:
1. **Determine FDP Configuration**:
   - `Get Features` with feature `1Dh`, ENDGID: verify FDP enabled and get configuration index.
   - `Get Log Page` with identifier `20h`: retrieve FDP Configurations List.
2. **FDP Events**:
   - `Get Features` for FDP Events: get supported events and enabled state.
   - `Set Features` for FDP Events: enable required events.
3. **Namespace Reconfiguration**:
   - For each namespace:
     - Issue `I/O Management Receive` to get Placement Handles.
     - `Identify` with CNS `08h`: check for volatile write cache.

sections.title: Write_Commands_using_Flexible_Data_Placement_(Info
sections.summary:
# 8.1.11.3 Write Commands using Flexible Data Placement (Informative)

**Section ID**: 8.1.11.3 | **Page**: 598-598

Hosts writing user data to a namespace in an Endurance Group with Flexible Data Placement enabled use two mechanisms to specify data placement:

1. **Default Placement Handle**:
   - Applies when:
     - The controller ignores the `DTYPE` field (per Section 8.1.9.4), **or**
     - The `DTYPE` field is not ignored and is set to `00h`.
   - Result: The namespace's default Placement Handle value (`0h`) is combined with a Reclaim Group selected by the controller to form the Placement Identifier (see Figure 289 and Figure 290).

2. **Data Placement Directive**:
   - Applies when:
     - The `DTYPE` field is not ignored and is set to `Data Placement (02h)`, **and**
     - The namespace has the Data Placement Directive enabled.
   - Result: The `DSPEC` field specifies the Reclaim Group Identifier and Placement Handle used for the write command.

**Additional Note**:
- To reduce write amplification, hosts track user data written to a Reclaim Unit and deallocate it using Dataset Management commands:
  - `AD bit` set to `1`
  - One or more Range fields specify the LBA ranges written to the Reclaim Unit.

sections.title: Host-Initiated_Refresh_Operation
sections.summary:
# 8.1.12 Host-Initiated Refresh Operation

- **Purpose**: Performs implementation-specific refresh operations to verify media integrity and ensure media access (e.g., for NVM subsystems not in operation for long periods or exposed to extreme conditions). Includes read verification, rewriting high-error-rate media, and other maintenance. **Does not modify user data**.
- **Support Indicator**: If supported, the controller sets the **HIRS bit to '1'** in the DSTO field of the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).
- **Progress Tracking**: Percentage complete is reported in the **Current Percentage Complete** field of the Device Self-test log page (Section 5.2.12.1.7).
- **Namespace Handling**: The **NSID field is ignored**; all media in the NVM subsystem are refreshed.
- **Abort Conditions**:
  a) Controller Level Reset on the controller performing the test.  
  b) Format NVM command processed by any controller in the NVM subsystem.  
  c) Sanitize operation started (Section 5.2.22).  
  d) Device Self-test command with **Self-Test Code = Fh** processed by any controller in the NVM subsystem.  
- **Non-Impact**: Controller Level Reset on a **non-participating controller** does not affect the operation.

sections.title: Host_Managed_Live_Migration
sections.summary:
# 8.1.13 Host Managed Live Migration

## Overview
- **Section ID**: 8.1.13 | **Page**: 599-601
- Enables migration of a Migratable Controller from a Source NVM Subsystem to a Destination NVM Subsystem using a Migration Management Controller (MMC) and Migration Management Host (MMH).
- Involves multiple hosts, NVM subsystems, and controllers. Each is uniquely named (see Figure 667).

## Key Definitions
- **Migration Management Controller (MMC)**: A controller with the HMLMS bit set to ‘1’ in the OACS field of the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).
- **Migration Management Host (MMH)**: Host associated with an MMC.
- **Migratable Controller**: Controller with HMLMS bit set to ‘0’.

## Capabilities and Responsibilities
- **MMH Responsibilities**:
  - Ensure compatibility of Migratable Controller state between Source and Destination.
  - Transfer migrating data between NVM subsystems.
- **MMC Capabilities (Privileged Actions)**:
  - Support **Migration Send** command with:
    - Management Operations: Suspend (`0h`), Resume (`1h`), Set Controller State (`2h`)
  - Support **Migration Receive** command with Management Operation: Controller State (`1h`)
  - Support CNS value `20h` in Identify command (Supported Controller State Formats)

## Controller Support Requirements
- **MMC Requirements**:
  - Must support the above commands and CNS `20h`.
- **Migratable Controller Restrictions**:
  - Shall not support:
    - Migration Send (`5.2.17`)
    - Migration Receive (`5.2.16`)
    - CNS `20h` in Identify command
    - Controller Data Queue with Create Queue for User Data Migration Queue (`5.2.4.1.1`)
- **NVM Subsystem Restrictions (if one or more MMCs exist)**:
  - No controller supports Host Memory Buffer (HMPRE field in Identify Controller data structure)

## Reset Behavior
- **Controller Level Reset on MMC**:
  - Deletes all User Data Migration Queues.
  - Stops tracking host memory changes.
- **Controller Level Reset on Migratable Controller**:
  - Removes suspended state if suspended via Migration Send (Suspend).
  - Retains any committed persistent controller state from Set Controller State.

## Data Tracking for Migration
- **Track Send** (`5.2.28`) and **Track Receive** (`5.2.27`) commands allow MMH to:
  - Detect user data changes in namespaces attached to the controller.
  - Detect host memory changes due to controller processing.
- **Controller Support for Tracking**:
  - **Track User Data Changes Support (TUDCS)**: Set to ‘1’ in TRATTR field of Identify Controller data structure.
  - **Track Host Memory Changes Support (THMCS)**: Set to ‘1’ in TRATTR field of Identify Controller data structure.

> **Note**: All references (e.g., Section 5.2.17.1.1, Section 3.10) are to corresponding sections in the specification.

sections.title: Process_for_Migrating_a_Controller
sections.summary:
# 8.1.13.1 Process for Migrating a Controller

## Overview
This section outlines a procedure for migrating a Migratable Controller from a Source NVM Subsystem to a Destination NVM Subsystem, including namespace data and host memory modifications. The MMHS (Migration Management Host Software) coordinates the migration using the MMC (Migration Management Controller) in both subsystems.

## Prerequisites
- The Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem must have:
  - **TUDCS (Track User Data Changes Support)** bit set to `1` in the TRATTR field of the Identify Controller data (Figure 328).
  - **THMCS (Track Host Memory Changes Support)** bit set to `1` in the TRATTR field.

> If namespaces or host memory modifications are not required, respective steps may be skipped.

---

## Migration Steps

### 1. **User Data Migration**
- **Objective**: Copy user data from namespaces attached to the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem.
- **Step a**: Create a **User Data Migration Queue** via a Controller Data Queue command:
  - Select = `0h` (Create Controller Data Queue)
  - Queue Type = **User Data Migration Queue**
  - Controller Identifier = Identifier of the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem
  - On success: completion queue entry contains the **Controller Data Queue Identifier**.
- **Step b**: Start logging user data changes via a **Track Send** command:
  - Select = `0h` (Log User Data Changes)
  - Logging Action = `1` (start logging)
  - Controller Data Queue Identifier = Identifier from Step a
  - The MMHS must ensure the queue is sized appropriately (no fullness allowed per NVM Command Set).
- **Step c**: Begin copying namespaces (refer to NVM Express I/O Command Set specs for optimizations like `Get LBA Status`).

### 2. **Host Memory Tracking**
- **Step a**: Start tracking host memory changes via **Track Send**:
  - Select = `1h` (Track Memory Changes)
  - TACT = `1` (start tracking)
  - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Source
  - Data buffer contains **host memory ranges** to track.
- **Step b**: Retrieve tracked host memory modifications via **Track Receive**:
  - Select = `1h` (Track Memory Changes)
  - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Source
  - The MMHS queries the MMC to obtain logged host memory changes.

### 3. **Suspend Controller in Source**
- The MMHS suspends the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem by sending a **Migration Send** command:
  - Select = `0h` (Suspend)
  - Suspend Type = `1h` (Suspend)
  - **Delete User Data Migration Queue** = `1` (if queue should be deleted)
  - Controller Identifier = Migratable Controller in Source
- **Before completion**:
  - The controller **stops fetching commands** (Admin and I/O queues).
  - Completes all previously fetched commands.
- The MMC **logs suspension** in the User Data Migration Queue and deletes it if requested.

### 4. **Finalize Data Copy**
- After suspension, the MMHS processes pending entries in the **User Data Migration Queue** to complete user data transfer.
- Host memory modifications are handled as reported by **Track Receive**.

### 5. **Obtain Controller State**
- The MMHS retrieves the controller state from the Source NVM Subsystem using **Migration Receive**:
  - Select = `0h` (Get Controller State)
  - Sequence Indicator = proper sequence value
  - Controller Identifier = Source Migratable Controller
  - **Controller State Version Index** = index into NVMe Controller State Version list (if NVMe state required, based on NVMECSS)
  - **Controller State UUID Index** = index in Vendor Specific Controller State UUID list (if VSS > 0)

### 6. **Set Controller State on Destination**
- The MMHD transfers the controller state to the Destination NVM Subsystem via **Migration Send**:
  - Select = `2h` (Set Controller State)
  - Sequence Indicator = proper sequence value
  - Controller Identifier = Destination Migratable Controller
  - **Controller State Version Index** = index into NVMe Controller State Version list (if NVMECSS ≠ 0)
  - **Controller State UUID Index** = index in Vendor Specific UUID list (if VSS ≠ 0)

### 7. **Resume Controller in Destination**
- Resume the migrated controller via **Migration Send**:
  - Select = `1h` (Resume)
  - Controller Identifier = Destination Migratable Controller

sections.title: Key_Per_I_O
sections.summary:
# 8.1.14 Key_Per_I_O

The **Key Per I/O** capability enables the use of encryption keys injected into an NVM subsystem by a host, referenced via an **encryption key tag** in I/O commands. Activation, injection, management, and tag-key association are defined in the **TCG Storage Security Subsystem Class: Key Per I/O Specification**, using NVMe Admin commands **Security Send** and **Security Receive**. Any subsystem modifications due to this mechanism are covered in the **TCG Storage Interface Interactions Specification (SIIS)**.

### Key Requirements and Architecture

- **Encryption Key Tag (KEYTAG)**:
  - Used in the **CEV field** of I/O commands when the **CETYPE** field is set to **KPIOTAG (1h)**.
  - A **16-bit** namespace-specific tag that identifies an encryption key used for data encryption/decryption.
  - The association between a key tag and an encryption key is outside this specification; one mechanism is defined in the TCG Key Per I/O Specification.
  - The maximum supported key tag value is given by the **Maximum Key Tag** field in the **I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace** data structure (Figure 335).

- **Key Per I/O Scope**:
  - Controlled by the **Key Per I/O Scope bit (KPIOS)** in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328):
    - `0`: Applies to all read/write commands across all namespaces.
    - `1`: Applies independently per namespace.
  - **Does not affect** host access to **RPMBs** or **Boot Partitions** (not accessed via namespace-specific I/O commands).

- **Support Indication**:
  - A controller supporting Key Per I/O sets the **KPIOS bit** to `1` in the Identify Controller data structure.
  - A namespace supporting Key Per I/O sets the **KPIOSNS bit** to `1` in the I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace data structure.

- **Command Extensions**:
  - Uses the **CETYPE** and **CEV** fields in all read/write commands.
  - **CETYPE Field Definitions**:
    | Value | Definition | CEV Field Definition |
    |-------|-----------|----------------------|
    | 0h    | Reserved | - |
    | 1h    | **Key Per I/O Tag (KPIOTAG)**: Uses Key Per I/O capability | **Key Tag (KEYTAG)**: 16-bit tag identifying encryption key; values supported up to Maximum Key Tag |
    | 2h–Eh | Reserved | - |
    | Fh    | Vendor Specific | - |

- **Error Handling**:
  - If **KPIOENS = 1** (Key Per I/O enabled in namespace), the command supports **CETYPE**, and **CETYPE** is **reserved**, the controller **aborts** the command with **Invalid Field in Command** status.

sections.title: Management_Addresses
sections.summary:
# 8.1.15 Management_Addresses

**Section ID**: 8.1.15 | **Page**: 604-605

## Overview
- Management agents on a network can perform management operations on NVM subsystems.
- Controllers in NVM subsystems use the **Management Addresses** capability to indicate network addresses of these agents.
- Management addresses are established when an NVM subsystem is provisioned in a storage system.

## Management Agent Locations
Management agents can reside in:
- NVM subsystems
- Fabric interface managers
- Embedded management controllers (e.g., BMC)
- Hosts

## Address Representation
- Each management address is represented as a **Uniform Resource Indicator (URI)**, per RFC 3986.

## Address Indication Methods

| Entity | Location | Management Address Type | Feature/Method |
|--------|----------|--------------------------|----------------|
| NVM subsystem (e.g., Ethernet-attached SSD) | Management Address List log page (Section 5.2.12.1.24) | Type `1h` | Indicated in Management Address Descriptor |
| Fabric interface manager | Management Address List log page (Section 5.2.12.1.24) | Type `2h` | Indicated in Management Address Descriptor |
| Embedded management controller (e.g., BMC) | Set/retrieved via **Embedded Management Controller Address** feature (Section 5.2.26.1.24) | N/A | Set only by storage system; enforced via **Lockdown command** (Section 5.2.15): OFI = Feature, PRHBT = '1', IFC = Admin Submission Queue (`00b`) |
| Host | Set/retrieved via **Host Management Agent Address** feature (Section 5.2.26.1.29) | N/A | Set only by host; enforced via **Lockdown command**: OFI = Feature, PRHBT = '1', IFC = Out-of-band on Management Endpoint (`10b`) |

> **Note**: Method for determining addresses is outside the scope of this specification.

sections.title: Namespace_Management
sections.summary:
# 8.1.16 Namespace Management

## Overview
- **Capabilities**: Namespace Management command (section 5.2.21) and Namespace Attachment command (section 5.2.20).
- **Purpose**: Create/delete namespaces; attach/detach controllers from namespaces.
- **Intended Use**: Manufacturing or system administrators.

## Requirements (if Namespace Management is supported):
a) Support Namespace Management and Namespace Attachment commands.  
b) Set **NMS bit to '1'** in the OACS field (Figure 328).  
c) Support **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event (Figure 154, section 5.2.26.1.5).  
d) *Should* support **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** asynchronous event (Figure 154, section 5.2.26.1.5).  
e) *May* support **Namespace Granularity** (refer to NVM Express NVM Command Set Specification).

## Optional Support:
- A controller may support **Namespace Attachment** without **Namespace Management**:
  - **Must not** set NMS bit to '1' in OACS.
  - **Should** support Namespace Attribute Change asynchronous event.

## Namespace State Transitions:
- **Detached namespace**: NSID becomes **inactive** (section 3.2.1.4).
- **Deleted namespace**: NSID becomes **unallocated** (section 3.2.1.3).
- Uncompleted/subsequently submitted commands to affected NSIDs are handled as if issued to an inactive NSID (Figure 92).

## Namespace Size & Capacity Allocation:
- Size is based on requested size, format, and characteristics (e.g., endurance).
- Controller determines NVM capacity allocated.
- Mapping of characteristics to NVM capacity is **outside scope**.

## NVM Set and Endurance Group Assignment (during namespace creation):
| NVM Set ID | Endurance Group ID | Action |
|------------|---------------------|-------|
| 0h         | 0h                  | Controller chooses NVM Set. |
| 0h         | Non-zero            | Controller chooses NVM Set in specified Endurance Group. |
| Non-zero   | 0h                  | **Abort** with **Invalid Field in Command**. |
| Non-zero   | Non-zero            | Allocate from specified NVM Set **if it exists** in the specified Endurance Group; else **abort** with **Invalid Field in Command**. |

## Reporting:
- NVM Set and Endurance Group for each namespace with formatted storage are reported in **Identify Namespace** data structure.
- **NVM capacity used** is reported in Identify Namespace data structure.
- **NVM capacity may be rounded up** to the next allocation unit.
- Allocation units (if supported) are reported in the **Namespace Granularity List**.

## Example:
- Request: 32 logical blocks × 4 KiB = 128 KiB.
- Allocation unit: 1 MiB.
- Actual NVM capacity consumed: **1 MiB** (rounded up).
- **NVM capacity fields do not necessarily equal** (logical block size × total logical blocks).

## ANA Group:
- **ANA Group Identifier** (in Identify Namespace, Figure 335): If cleared to **0h**, controller assigns ANAGRPID.
- **Method of allocation** is **outside scope**.

sections.title: Namespace_Management_Examples
sections.summary:
### 8.1.16.1 Namespace Management Examples

#### Key Operations and Requirements:

- **Namespace Creation**:
  1. Host issues **Identify command** with `NSID = FF FF FF FFh` and `CNS = 0h` to retrieve common namespace capabilities.
  2. If supported, host optionally retrieves I/O Command Set-specific namespace management data (e.g., **Namespace Granularity**).
  3. Host determines available resources (e.g., capacity) based on **Section 3.8**.
  4. Host constructs data structure from **Figure 385**, considering capabilities and available capacity.
  5. Host issues **Namespace Management command** with **Create operation**. On success, the new **Namespace Identifier** is returned in Dword 0 of the completion queue entry. The namespace is not attached to any controller at this point.
  6. If **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** are enabled, host issues **Identify Namespace** commands (per **Section 1.5.50**) upon receiving an *Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed* asynchronous event.

- **Namespace Attachment**:
  1. Host issues **Namespace Attachment command** with **Controller Attach operation** to attach namespace to one or more controllers.
  2. Host receives *Attached Namespace Attribute Changed* asynchronous event from each controller with **Attached Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.
  3. Host receives *Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed* asynchronous event from each controller with **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.

- **Namespace Detachment**:
  1. Host issues **Namespace Attachment command** with **Controller Detach operation** to detach namespace from one or more controllers.
  2. Host receives *Attached Namespace Attribute Changed* asynchronous event from each controller with **Attached Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.
  3. Host receives *Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed* asynchronous event from each controller with **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.

- **Namespace Deletion**:
  1. Host must **detach the namespace from all controllers**.
  2. Host issues **Namespace Management command** with **Delete operation**. On successful completion, the namespace is deleted.
  3. If the namespace was attached to any controller(s) when deleted:
     - (a) Host receives *Attached Namespace Attribute Changed* event from each such controller with **Attached Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.
     - (b) Host receives *Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed* event from each such controller with **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.
  4. If the namespace was **not attached** to any controller when deleted, host receives *Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed* event from each controller with **Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices** enabled.

sections.title: Namespace_Deletion_Asynchronous_Event_Reporting
sections.summary:
# 8.1.16.2 Namespace Deletion Asynchronous Event Reporting

## Overview
When a namespace deletion is requested, asynchronous events must be issued by controllers to report the change, depending on the method of deletion and controller attributes.

## Key Requirements

### Deletion via Command (Admin Submission Queue)
- **Controllers involved**: All controllers attached to the namespace, except the one processing the delete operation.
- **Events issued**:
  - **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** (if `Attached Namespace Attribute Notices` is enabled).
  - **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** (if `Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices` is enabled).

### Deletion via Other Methods (e.g., Management Endpoint)
- **Controllers involved**: All controllers attached to the namespace.
- **Events issued**:
  - **Attached Namespace Attribute Changed** (if `Attached Namespace Attribute Notices` is enabled).
  - **Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed** (if `Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices` is enabled).

> **Note**: See Figure 409 for details on `Attached Namespace Attribute Notices` and `Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices` enablement.

## Architectural Details
- Asynchronous event reporting is triggered **as part of the delete operation**.
- Events are issued **by controllers**, not the host or management interface.
- Event generation depends on **controller-specific attribute enablement**, not the method of deletion alone.

sections.title: Namespace_Management_Considerations_for_Exported_N
sections.summary:
# 8.1.16.3 Namespace Management Considerations for Exported NVM Subsystems

- **Host Capability Check**: A host determines if an Exported NVM Subsystem supports the *Namespace Attachment* command by reading the *Commands Supported and Effects* log page (Section 5.2.12.1.6).
- **Command Support**:
  - *Namespace Attachment* command is supported for attaching/detaching namespaces to/from controllers.
  - *Namespace Management* command is **not supported** by controllers in an Exported NVM Subsystem.
- **NSID States**:
  - If an *Exported Namespace* is detached from a controller, the associated NSID becomes **inactive** (Section 3.2.1.4).
  - If an *Underlying Namespace* is disassociated from the Exported NVM Subsystem, the corresponding Exported NSID becomes **unallocated** (Section 3.2.1.3) and is not available to any controller.
- **Command Handling**:
  - Previously submitted but uncompleted, or newly submitted commands to:
    - Detached namespaces, or
    - Disassociated Underlying Namespaces
    - Are handled as if issued to an **inactive NSID** (Section 3.2.1.4, Figure 92).
- **Underlying Namespace Changes**:
  - If an Exported Underlying Namespace becomes unavailable (e.g., detached, deleted) or is affected by Capacity Management (e.g., Endurance Group or NVM Set deletion, Section 8.1.4):
    - All commands to the affected Exported Namespace are treated as issued to an inactive NSID.
    - If *Allocated Namespace Attribute Notices* are enabled, affected controllers report an *Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed* asynchronous event (Figure 154).

sections.title: Namespace_Write_Protection
sections.summary:
# 8.1.17 Namespace Write Protection

## Overview
- **Section ID**: 8.1.17 | **Page**: 608-609  
- **Purpose**: Optional controller capability enabling the host to control or query the write protection state of a namespace.
- **Reporting**: Supported via the `Namespace Write Protection Capabilities (NWPC)` field in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).

## Write Protection States
Defined in **Table 1** (Table_8_1_17_Namespace_Write_Protection):

| M/O | State | Definition | Persistent Across Power Cycles | Persistent Across Controller Level Resets |
|-----|-------|------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| M   | No Write Protect | Namespace is not write protected. | Yes | Yes |
| M   | Write Protect | Namespace is write protected. | Yes | Yes |
| O   | Write Protect Until Power Cycle | Namespace is write protected until next power cycle. | No | Yes |
| O   | Permanent Write Protect | Namespace is permanently write protected. | Yes | Yes |

**Notes**:
- **M**: Mandatory if Namespace Write Protection capability is supported.
- **O**: Optional if the capability is supported.
- All states persist across **Controller Level Resets** unless noted.
- **Write Protect Until Power Cycle** does not persist across power cycles and is **not supported in multi-domain NVM subsystems**.

## State Transitions
- Defined in **Figure 670** (Namespace Write Protection State Machine Model).
- Transitions occur via **Set Features** commands, except where otherwise specified.
- **Initial state at namespace creation**: `No Write Protect`.

## Controls
- **Write Protect Until Power Cycle** and **Permanent Write Protect** states are governed by the **Write Protection Control** field (Figure 690).
- This field determines whether the controller **processes** or **aborts** Set Features commands that transition into these states (see Section 8.1.23).

## Notes
- Integration with external write protection systems (e.g., TCG Storage Interface) is **outside the scope** of this specification.

sections.title: Namespace_Write_Protection_–_Theory_of_Operation
sections.summary:
# 8.1.17.1 Namespace Write Protection – Theory of Operation

If Namespace Write Protection is supported by the controller, it must:
- Indicate support in the **Namespace Write Protection Capabilities (NWPC)** field of the Identify Controller data structure:
  - Set **No Write Protect and Write Protect Support** bit to `1`.
  - Set **Write Protect Until Power Cycle Support** bit to `1` if supported.
  - Set **Permanent Write Protect Support** bit to `1` if supported.
- Support the **Namespace Write Protection Config** feature (Section 5.2.26.1.35).
- If either **Write Protect Until Power Cycle** or **Permanent Write Protect** is supported, the controller must support the **Write Protection Control** field in the RPMB Device Configuration Block (Section 8.1.23).

The controller **shall not** set the **All Media Read-Only** bit to `1` in the Critical Warning field (Figure 210) if the read-only state results from:
- A change in the namespace write protection state (per the Namespace Write Protection State Machine, Figure 670), or
- Autonomous state transitions (e.g., power cycle).

Hosts can query the current namespace write protection state using the **Get Features** command with the **Namespace Write Protection Config** Feature Identifier.

If any controller in the NVM subsystem supports Namespace Write Protection, **all controllers** to which a namespace is attached must enforce the write protection state.

sections.title: Namespace_Write_Protection_–_Command_Interactions
sections.summary:
### 8.1.17.2 Namespace Write Protection – Command Interactions

Unless otherwise noted, commands listed in **Table 1** are processed normally when specifying an NSID for a write-protected namespace.

Commands **not listed in Table 1** and meeting any of the following conditions shall be aborted with a status code of **Namespace Is Write Protected** (see Figure 102):
- (a) Commands specifying an NSID for a write-protected namespace.
- (b) Commands specifying an NSID for a non-write-protected namespace that would modify another write-protected namespace (e.g., Format NVM).
- (c) Commands not specifying an NSID that would modify a write-protected namespace (e.g., Sanitize).

#### Table 1: Table_8_1_17_2_Namespace_Write_Protection_Command_Interactions

| Admin Command Set | NVM Command Set |
| :--- | :--- |
| Device Self-test | Compare |
| Directive Send ¹ | Dataset Management ¹ |
| Directive Receive ³ | Read |
| Get Features | Reservation Register |
| Get Log Page | Reservation Report |
| Identify | Reservation Acquire |
| Namespace Attachment | Reservation Release |
| Security Receive ¹ | Vendor Specific ¹ |
| Security Send ¹ | Flush ² |
| Set Features | Verify |
| Vendor Specific ¹ | |

**Notes:**
- **¹**: The controller shall fail commands if the specified action attempts to modify the non-volatile storage medium of the specified namespace.
- **²**: A Flush command shall complete successfully with no effect. All volatile write cache data and metadata associated with the specified namespace is written to non-volatile storage medium as part of transitioning to the write-protected state (refer to Section 5.2.26.1.35).
- **³**: A Directive Receive command that attempts to allocate streams resources shall be aborted with a status code of Namespace Is Write Protected.

sections.title: Power_Management
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18 Power Management

### Overview
- **Purpose**: Enables host to manage NVM subsystem power statically or dynamically.
- **Static**: Host sets max power and selects a power state consuming ≤ that power.
- **Dynamic**: Host adjusts power state dynamically to meet changing power/performance goals.
- **Complements**: Autonomous power/thermal management by controller.

### Power State Definitions
- **Number of Power States Supported (NPSS)**: In Identify Controller data structure.
  - Minimum: 1 state.
  - Maximum: 32 states.
  - States are contiguously numbered from 0.
  - Power state 0: Maximum power consumption.
- **Power State Descriptor**: Each state has a descriptor in Identify Controller data structure.
  - Descriptors form a table (see Table 1).
  - **Maximum Power (MP)**: Sustained max power in the state (measured methods outside scope). Power cannot exceed MP except in non-operational states.

### Key Metrics
- **Idle Power (IDLP)**: Typical power over 30 seconds when idle (measured after 10 seconds of idleness).
- **Active Power (ACTP)**: Max average power over a 10-second window on a specific workload.
  - Measurement starts with first command; ends with last command.
  - If workload completes in <10s, measure over workload duration.
  - Non-operational states: Set Active Power Scale, Workload, and ACTP to 0h.

### Host Commands
- **Set Features**: Dynamically change power state.
- **Get Features**: Determine current power state.
- **State Transitions**:
  - Direct transitions between any supported states allowed.
  - **Entry Latency (ENLAT)**: Max time (µs) to enter state.
  - **Exit Latency (EXLAT)**: Max time (µs) to exit state.
- **Transition Timing**:
  - Max transition time between two states: sum of old state's EXLAT and new state's ENLAT.
  - Host not required to wait for previous transition to complete before starting a new one.
  - Max time for sequence: sum of individual transition times.

### Relative Performance
- **Fields per Power State**:
  - Relative Read Throughput (RRT)
  - Relative Write Throughput (RWT)
  - Relative Read Latency (RRL)
  - Relative Write Latency (RWL)
- **Interpretation**:
  - Lower value = better performance (higher throughput or lower latency).
  - Values may repeat, skip, or be unordered across states.
  - Relative ordering applies per characteristic only; e.g., RRT and RWT values may be equal but do not imply equal performance.

### Default State
- Default NVM Express power state: Implementation-specific.
- Must not exceed lowest value in applicable form factor specification (if any).
- Refer to transport-specific power requirements in applicable NVM Express Transport specification.

### Table 1: Example Power State Descriptor Table
| Power State | Maximum Power (MP) | Entry Latency (ENLAT) | Exit Latency (EXLAT) | Relative Read Throughput (RRT) | Relative Read Latency (RRL) | Relative Write Throughput (RWT) | Relative Write Latency (RWL) |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0 | 25 W | 5 µs | 5 µs | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 18 W | 5 µs | 7 µs | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| 2 | 18 W | 5 µs | 8 µs | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | 15 W | 20 µs | 15 µs | 2 | 0 | 2 | 0 |
| 4 | 10 W | 20 µs | 30 µs | 1 | 1 | 3 | 0 |
| 5 | 8 W | 50 µs | 50 µs | 2 | 2 | 4 | 0 |
| 6 | 5 W | 20 µs | 5,000 µs | 4 | 3 | 5 | 1 |

sections.title: Non-Operational_Power_States
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.1 Non-Operational Power States

- **Definition**: A power state is non-operational if the `Non-Operational State (NOPS)` field in Figure 329 is set.
- **Operations allowed** in non-operational power states:
  - Property accesses
  - PMR accesses (if any)
  - CMB accesses (if any)
  - Processing of Admin commands and associated background operations (e.g., Device Self-test (5.2.5), Sanitize (5.2.22))
  - Additional transport-specific accesses (per NVMe Transport binding)
- **Controller behavior**:
  - May exceed the power advertised by the non-operational state
  - Must remain in the current non-operational state unless:
    - An I/O command is received
    - An explicit transition via `Set Features` (Power Management Feature Identifier) is requested
  - Must not exceed the maximum power advertised for the most recent operational power state
- **HMB access restrictions**:
  - Prohibits controller from accessing HMB for controller-initiated activities (not command-related)
  - **Does not prohibit** HMB access during Admin command processing or host-initiated background operations
- **Controller-initiated background operations**:
  - May exceed non-operational power state power **if** "Non-Operational Power State Permissive Mode" is supported and enabled (5.2.26.1.10)
- **I/O commands**:
  - Not processed in non-operational power states
  - Host must ensure no pending I/O commands before issuing `Set Features` to change to non-operational state
  - New I/O commands must not be submitted until `Set Features` completes
  - Issuing I/O in parallel may cause unexpected power state
- **Autonomous transition**:
  - Regardless of autonomous power state transitions, controller shall autonomously transition back to the most recent operational power state to process an I/O command

sections.title: Autonomous_Power_State_Transitions
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.2 Autonomous Power State Transitions

- **Section ID**: 8.1.18.2 | **Page**: 613-613

## Overview
- The controller may support autonomous power state transitions, indicated in the **Identify Controller** data structure (Figure 328).
- Allows controller to transition between power states automatically based on predefined conditions without host software intervention.

## Entry Condition for Idle Transition
- Controller must be idle (no commands outstanding on any I/O Submission Queue) for a continuous period exceeding the **Idle Time Prior to Transition**.
- **Controller should not transition** if an ongoing operation (e.g., device self-test) would cause power usage to exceed the advertised limit of the proposed non-operational power state.

## Power State Transition Rules
- Transition destination must be a **non-operational power state**.
- A non-operational power state may autonomously transition to another non-operational power state.

## Command Handling
- If a **Set Features** command (Feature Identifier = 0Ch) specifies an **operational power state**, the controller shall **abort the command** with a **status code of Invalid Field in Command**.
- Refer to **Section 8.1.18.1** for further details.

sections.title: NVM_Subsystem_Workloads
sections.summary:
### 8.1.18.3 NVM Subsystem Workloads This section defines workload values used to specify workload hints in the Power Management Feature (Section 5.2.26.1.2) for the NVM subsystem, indicating conditions under which active power levels are measured. Active power values in power state descriptors are workload-specific, and a corresponding workload must be indicated if active power is specified. #### Table 8.1.18.3: NVM Subsystem Workloads | Value | Definition | | :--- | :--- | | `000b` | **No Workload**: Workload is unknown or not provided. | | `001b` | **Workload 1**: Extended Idle Period with a Burst of Random Writes. Consists of:
- 5 minutes of idle,
- 32 random write commands of size 1 MiB submitted to a single controller (other controllers idle),
- 30 seconds of idle. | | `010b` | **Workload 2**: Heavy Sequential Writes. Consists of:
- 80,000 sequential write commands of size 128 KiB submitted to a single controller (other controllers idle),
- Submission queues must be large enough to maintain multiple pending commands at all times. | | `011b` to `111b` | Reserved |

sections.title: Runtime_D3_(RTD3)_Transitions_(PCIe_only)
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.4 Runtime D3 (RTD3) Transitions (PCIe only)

- **RTD3** is a power state where main power is removed from the controller, with auxiliary power optionally provided. It is used for additional power savings during expected idle periods.
- RTD3 corresponds to **D3cold** in the PCI Express Base Specification; **D3hot** is excluded since main power is not removed.
- The host determines RTD3 usage based on:
  - **RTD3 Entry Latency (RTD3E)**: Time from when `CC.SHN` is set to `01b` until `CSTS.SHST` is set to `10b` (controller ready for power removal).
  - **RTD3 Resume Latency (RTD3R)**: Time from power application until the controller can:
    - Process and complete I/O commands.
    - Access resources (e.g., formatted storage) associated with attached namespaces.
  - Latency values are based on a normal shutdown with optimal settings, assuming the host enables the controller and issues a 4 KiB read.
- Both RTD3E and RTD3R are reported in the **Identify Controller data structure** (Figure 328).
- If `CSTS.ST` is cleared to `0`, RTD3 Entry Latency is defined as the time from `CC.SHN = 01b` to `CSTS.SHST = 10b`.

sections.title: Host_Controlled_Thermal_Management
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.5 Host Controlled Thermal Management

## Overview
- **Section ID**: 8.1.18.5 | **Page**: 614–616  
- Controller may support **Host Controlled Thermal Management (HCTM)**, indicated in the *Host Controlled Thermal Management Attributes* of the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).
- HCTM allows the host to configure the controller to transition between active power states or perform vendor-specific thermal actions to meet thermal requirements.
- Power state transitions are vendor-specific.

## Configuration
- Host enables HCTM by setting **Thermal Management Temperature 1** and/or **Thermal Management Temperature 2** fields (Section 5.2.26.1.9) in a *Set Features* command to a non-zero value.
- Supported ranges for both fields are specified in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328).

## Behavior
- **Thermal Management Temperature 1**:
  - If **Composite Temperature** ≥ this value and < Thermal Management Temperature 2 (if non-zero), the controller:
    - Transitions to lower power active states or performs vendor-specific thermal actions.
    - Minimizes performance impact (e.g., light throttling).
- **Thermal Management Temperature 2**:
  - If **Composite Temperature** ≥ this value, the controller:
    - Transitions to lower power states or performs vendor-specific actions **regardless of performance impact** (e.g., heavy throttling).

## State Transition Conditions
- If controller is in a lower power state due to HCTM and **Composite Temperature** < **Thermal Management Temperature 1**:
  - Controller returns to previous active power state or stops vendor-specific actions.
- If controller is in a lower power state due to **Thermal Management Temperature 2** and **Composite Temperature** < **Thermal Management Temperature 1**:
  - Controller returns to previous active power state or stops vendor-specific actions.

## Hysteresis
- The temperature at which the controller exits the lower power state or stops vendor-specific actions is **vendor-specific**.

## Additional Notes
- HCTM uses **Composite Temperature** (refer to Figure 211).
- Implementation interactions may vary between platforms and devices even with identical settings.
- Requires validation between device and platform implementations.
- **SMART / Health Information log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.3) contains HCTM-related statistics.

## Figure
- **Figure 675**: HCTM Example – illustrates how Composite Temperature may be affected by HCTM.

sections.title: Power_Limit
sections.summary:
# 8.1.18.6 Power_Limit

## Overview
- **Controller Support**: Indicated by the Power Limit Support (PLS) bit in the Controller Attributes (CTRATT) field of the Identify Controller data structure.
- **Purpose**: Enables the host to limit maximum power consumption by prohibiting power states exceeding a specified power limit.
- **Control**:
  - Modify power limit via `Set Features` command (Power Limit feature attributes).
  - Read current power limit via `Get Features` command.
- **Power Limit Enforcement**: Prohibits power states where the Maximum Power (MP) in the Power State Descriptor (PSD) exceeds the specified power limit.
- **PSD Data**: Removed from Identify Controller data structure for prohibited states; restored when enabled.
- **Renumbering**: Power states are renumbered contiguously starting at 0, with MP values non-increasing.
- **APST Table**: Entries for prohibited states are removed; Idle Transition Power State field is updated to reflect new state numbers.

## Use Cases
- **Establish/Reduce Power Limit**: May prohibit power states and remove PSD data (§8.1.18.6.1).
- **Remove/Increase Power Limit**: May restore PSD data and enable power states (§8.1.18.6.2).
- **Update Power Limit (No State Change)**: Only updates Power Limit feature attributes; no structural changes (§8.1.18.6.3).

---

## 8.1.18.6.1 Establishing or Reducing a Power Limit and Prohibiting Power States from Use
- **Trigger**: Power limit change results in enabled power states becoming prohibited (i.e., power limit < MP of PSD0).
- **Steps**:
  1. If no current power limit or power limit removed, retain:
     - All PSD data structures.
     - All APST entries (refer to Figure 411).
     - NPSS value.
     - Power Management Power State attribute values (current, default, saved).
  2. Prohibit all power states where MP > specified power limit.
  3. For each prohibited state:
     - Remove its PSD from Identify Controller.
     - Remove its APST entry (refer to Figure 412).
  4. Shift remaining PSDs to lower offsets; set PSD0 to lowest valid MP state. Update NPSS.
  5. Shift remaining APST entries to match PSD shifts; align first entry with new PS0.
  6. Zero out unused PSD and APST entries.
  7. For each Power Management feature value:
     - If power state not prohibited, update value to match new PSD location.
     - If prohibited, clear value to `0h`.
  8. For each APST entry (current, default, saved):
     - If power state not prohibited, update Idle Transition Power State value to new location.
     - If prohibited, clear value to `0h`.
- **RPSD**: Retained PSD data structure; used for restoration.

---

## 8.1.18.6.2 Removing or Increasing a Power Limit and Enabling Power States for Use
- **Trigger**: Power limit change enables at least one prohibited power state (i.e., power limit > MP of at least one RPSD).
- **Steps**:
  1. Restore:
     - All PSD data structures from most recent RPSD instance.
     - All APST entries.
     - NPSS value.
     - Power Management Power State attribute values.
  2. If new power limit < MP of restored PSD0, process it as in §8.1.18.6.1.
- **Visibility**: Changes become visible only after step 2 completion.
- **Power Limit Removal**: Set PLV to `0h` → treated as power limit > all RPSD MP values.
- **MUP/MUPS**: Maximum Unlimited Power (MUP) + MUPS = max power of PS0 after removing limit.
- **Retention**: When current/saved Power Management value changes during limit application, update retained values to match RPSD data.

---

## 8.1.18.6.3 Updating a Power Limit Without Changing Prohibited or Enabled Power States
- **Trigger**: Power limit change does not enable or prohibit any states.
- **Condition**: New power limit ≥ MP of all RPSD states and ≤ MP of PSD0.
- **Action**:
  - Update Power Limit feature attributes only.
  - No changes to PSDs, NPSS, or Power Management attributes.

---

## 8.1.18.6.4 Power Limit Effects Examples
### Case 1: Set 16W Power Limit (No Prior Limit)
- **Initial State**: 6 power states; default = PS1 (18W).
- **Effects**:
  - PS0 (25W), PS1 (18W), PS2 (16W) prohibited → removed.
  - Remaining: PS3 (15W), PS4 (10W), PS5 (5W).
  - PSDs shifted down 3 slots; PS3 → PS0.
  - NPSS decreases from 6 to 3.
  - Power Management default → PS0.
  - Current power state:
    - If PS0, PS1, or PS2 → transitions to new PS0.
    - Else → remains same; current value decreased by 3 (e.g., PS4 → PS1).

### Case 2: Raise 16W Limit to 20W
- **Initial State**: 4 enabled power states (PS0–PS3).
- **Effects**:
  - PSDs shift up 2 slots; PS0 → PS2.
  - PS1 (18W) and PS2 (18W) restored → PS0 and PS1.
  - PS0 (25W) remains prohibited.
  - NPSS increases from 3 to 5.
  - Power Management current → increased by 2 (e.g., PS0 → PS2).
  - Default → PS0 (original PS1).

### Case 3: Remove 20W Power Limit
- **Initial State**: 6 enabled power states.
- **Effects**:
  - PSDs shift up 1 slot; PS0 → PS1.
  - Original PSD0 restored → PS0.
  - NPSS increases from 5... (to original 6 if full restoration).

sections.title: Power_Measurement_and_Reporting
sections.summary:
# 8.1.19 Power Measurement and Reporting

**Overview**: Optional capabilities allowing the host to use interval power measurements from embedded sensors in the NVM subsystem. An interval power measurement is the average power over a one-second interval, sampled at a rate ≤ IPMSR (from Identify Controller data structure, Figure 328). Measurements are non-overlapping, based on measured power, and not required during:
- Power cycles
- Non-operational power states
- NVM Subsystem Reset processing
- When CSTS.SHST = 10b in all controllers

**Power Measurement Types** (Table 1):
- 0h: NVM subsystem total power
- 1h to Bh: Reserved
- Ch to Fh: Vendor Specific

**Contiguous vs. Non-Contiguous Sets**: Sets are contiguous if no time gaps; non-contiguous if interrupted by:
- Power removal
- Entry into non-operational state
- NVM Subsystem Reset
- CSTS.SHST = 10b in all controllers

**Reporting Requirements** (Table 2):
- Interval Power Measurement (IPM) in SMART/Health log → collect interval measurements
- Operational Lifetime Energy Consumed (OLEC) in SMART/Health log → collect interval measurements
- Power Threshold feature supported → collect interval measurements
- Power Measurement capability supported → collect interval measurements

If any of the above apply, the controller must set **Interval Power Measurement Sample Rate (IPMSR)** to a non-zero value in Identify Controller (Figure 328).

**Power Scale Definitions** (Table 3):
- 00b: Reserved
- 01b: 0.0001 W
- 10b: 0.01 W
- 11b: Reserved

Defined for:
- Interval Power Scale (IPS) – Figure 158
- Average Interval Power Scale (AIPWRS) – Figure 297
- Maximum Interval Power Scale (MIPWRS) – Figure 297
- Power Scale (PWRS) – Figure 298
- Power Threshold Scale (PTS) – Figure 453

sections.title: Power_Measurement_capability
sections.summary:
# 8.1.19.1 Power_Measurement_capability

## Overview
The Power Measurement capability enables a host to control logging of interval power measurements, which are used to report:
- Average interval power measurements
- Maximum interval power measurement
- Histogram of interval power measurements

## Requirements
- Supported if the **PMS bit** in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328) is set to '1'.
- Requires support for:
  - **Power Measurement feature** (Section 5.2.26.1.27)
  - **Power Measurement log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.33)

## Command Interface
- **Start Power Measurements**: Issue `Set Features` command with:
  - Feature: Power Measurement
  - Action: `1h`
  - Optional: Non-zero **Stop Measurement Time** (Figure 454)
- **Stop Power Measurements**:
  - `Set Features` with Action: `0h`
  - Or `Set Features` with Action: `1h` and non-zero **Stop Measurement Time**

## Stop Measurement Time Validation
- If **Stop Measurement Time** > **Maximum Stop Measurement Time (MSMT)** in Identify Controller (Figure 328):
  - Controller aborts command with **Invalid Field in Command** status.

## Power Measurement Log Page (Figure 297)
- **Number of Power Histogram Descriptors Supported (NPHDS)**: Max number of Power Histogram Descriptors in log.
- **Power Histogram Descriptor Overflow (PHDO)**:
  - Set to '1' if:
    - NPHDS ≠ 0
    - Power Measurement Count (PMC) ≠ 0
    - At least one logged interval power > max power of last descriptor (NPHD-1)
- **Power Measurement Count (PMC)**: Incremented for each interval power measurement.
- **Power Histogram Bin Count**: Incremented for each measurement falling into a bin defined by:
  - ≥ **Power Histogram Bin Lower Threshold**
  - < **Lower Threshold + Bin Size**

## Power Measurement Updates
When logging interval power measurements (PME = '1'):
- **Average Interval Power**: Updated with new average.
- **Maximum Interval Power** and **Maximum Interval Power Timestamp**:
  - Updated if current power > existing max power (if supported).
- **Power Histogram Descriptor Overflow Count (PHDOC)**: Incremented if power > max of last descriptor.
