sections.title: Predictable_Latency_Mode
sections.summary:
# 8.1.20 Predictable Latency Mode

**Purpose**: Enables predictable latency for read and write operations by defining deterministic and non-deterministic operating windows within NVM Sets.

## Key Concepts
- **NVM Set**: A logical grouping of namespaces (Section 3.2.2).
- **Predictable Latency Mode Config Feature**: Enables/configures mode (Section 5.2.26.1.12).
- **Deterministic Window (DTWIN)**: Window for deterministic I/O latency.
- **Non-Deterministic Window (NDWIN)**: Window where deterministic latency is not guaranteed; used for background operations.
- **Deterministic Excursion**: Rare event requiring immediate controller action, potentially triggering transition to NDWIN.

## Requirements
When Predictable Latency Mode is supported, all controllers must:
- Support one or more NVM Sets
- Support Read Recovery Levels (Section 8.1.22)
- Support:
  - Predictable Latency Per NVM Set log page
  - Predictable Latency Event Aggregate log page
  - Predictable Latency Mode Config Feature
  - Predictable Latency Mode Window Feature
  - Predictable Latency Event Aggregate Log Change Notices
- Indicate support in Controller Attributes (Identify Controller data structure)

## Operational Rules
- **I/O Quality of Service (QoS)**: Vendor-specific, applies within NVM Subsystem (not PCIe/fabric).
- **Isolation**: I/O commands for different NVM Sets should use separate I/O Submission Queues to avoid QoS interference.
- **DTWIN Entry/Exit**:
  - Host configures current window via *Predictable Latency Mode Window Feature*.
  - Controller may transition to NDWIN autonomously if attributes exceed thresholds in Predictable Latency Per NVM Set log page.
- **Event Management**:
  - Host configures Predictable Latency Events (Section 8.1.20.3) to trigger on threshold exceedance, enabling proactive window management.

sections.title: Host_Operating_Rules_to_Achieve_Determinism
sections.summary:
# 8.1.20.1 Host Operating Rules to Achieve Determinism

### Purpose
To achieve deterministic operation, the host must follow rules ensuring the NVM Set remains in the **Deterministic Window (DTWIN)**, defined by:
- Attributes not exceeding **Typical** or **Maximum** values in the *Predictable Latency Per NVM Set* log page (Section 5.2.12.1.11).
- No **Deterministic Excursion**.
- No transition request to the **Non-Deterministic Window (NDWIN)**.

### Key Attributes
- Number of random 4 KiB reads.
- Number of writes in Optimal Write Size.
- Time in the Deterministic Window.
- Additional vendor-specific attributes.

### Predictable Latency Per NVM Set Log Page (Section 5.2.12.1.11)
For each attribute:
- **Typical/Maximum**: Allowed consumption during a DTWIN.
- **Reliable Estimate**: Remaining consumption available in the current DTWIN.

### Transition to NDWIN (Autonomous)
An NVM Set transitions to NDWIN if, since entry to DTWIN:
- **Reads > DTWIN Reads Typical**
- **Writes > DTWIN Writes Typical**
- **Time > DTWIN Time Maximum**
- **Deterministic Excursion** occurs

### Reliable Estimate Properties (in DTWIN)
- Monotonically decreasing toward 0h.
- No abrupt changes unless operating conditions change.
- Based on averaging/smoothing over time.

### Host Control
- Use **Set Features** command with **Predictable Latency Mode Window Feature** to configure window (DTWIN or NDWIN).
- Use reliable estimates to transition to NDWIN before estimates reach critical thresholds (e.g., DTWIN Reads Estimate = 0).

### Figure 687: Example of DTWIN Reads
- DTWIN Reads Reliable Estimate starts near DTWIN Reads Typical at time 0.
- Decreases by approximate amount read per time increment (e.g., x at t2, y at t3).
- Illustrates monotonically decreasing behavior.

sections.title: Configuring_Periodic_Windows
sections.summary:
# 8.1.20.2 Configuring Periodic Windows

When using NVM Set in Predictable Latency Mode, the host must transition the controller to **NDWIN** (Non-Deterministic Window) for periodic maintenance to ensure reliable deterministic window timing.

Three static time-based parameters are reported in the **Predictable Latency Per NVM Set log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.11), representing worst-case values for the life of the NVM subsystem:

- **NDWIN Time Minimum Low**:  
  Minimum time the NVM Set remains in the Non-Deterministic Window. The controller may delay completion of a Set Features command requesting a transition to the Deterministic Window until this time is met. Does not include additional host activity.

- **NDWIN Time Minimum High**:  
  Minimum time the host should allow the NVM Set to remain in the Non-Deterministic Window after it was in the previous Deterministic Window for **DTWIN Time Maximum**. Does not include additional host activity.

- **DTWIN Time Maximum**:  
  Maximum time the NVM Set can stay in a Deterministic Window.

The **DTWIN Time Maximum** and **NDWIN Time Minimum High** can be used to estimate maintenance workload relative to DTWIN duration, assuming no threshold is exceeded. Any scaling based on read/write/time behavior in the previous Deterministic Window is implementation-dependent.

The **DTWIN Time Estimate** is used by the host to re-synchronize an NVM Set after a **Deterministic Excursion**, enabling alignment with other NVM Sets in Predictable Latency Mode.

sections.title: Configuring_and_Managing_Events
sections.summary:
### 8.1.20.3 Configuring and Managing Events

- **Purpose**: The host configures events triggered by threshold violations or autonomous transitions in Predictable Latency Mode using the `Set Feature` command for a specific NVM Set.  
- **Event Trigger**: Events are generated when thresholds are not exceeded or autonomous transitions (e.g., to NDWIN) occur.  
- **Event Notification**: A *Predictable Latency Event Aggregate Log Change Notice* is sent to the host when events occur for a configured NVM Set.  
- **Log Access**:  
  - **Aggregate Log Page (Section 5.2.12.1.12)**: Used to identify NVM Sets with outstanding events. Each entry corresponds to an NVM Set with active events.  
  - **Maximum NVM Set Size**: Determined by the `NVM Set Identifier Maximum` value in the Identify Controller data structure.  
  - **Per-NVM Set Log Page (Section 5.2.12.1.11)**: Contains specific event details. The `Event Type` field indicates the type of event (e.g., autonomous transition to NDWIN).  
- **Event Clearing**:  
  - Events for a specific NVM Set are cleared if the controller successfully reads the *Predictable Latency Per NVM Set* log page with the `Retain Asynchronous Event` parameter set to `0`.  
  - If the `Event Type` field is `0h` in the per-NVM Set log page, no events are reported in the aggregate log.

sections.title: Reachability_Reporting_architecture
sections.summary:
# 8.1.21 Reachability Reporting Architecture

## Overview
Defines the architecture for reachability reporting in the system, outlining the components, data flow, and requirements for reporting reachability status.

## Key Components
- **Reachability Reporter**: Generates reachability reports.
- **Reachability Collector**: Aggregates reports from multiple sources.
- **Reachability Database**: Stores collected reachability data.
- **Reporting Interface**: Exposes reachability data to consumers.

## Data Flow
1. **Reporting**: Reachability Reporter sends status updates to the Reachability Collector.
2. **Aggregation**: Reachability Collector processes and stores data in the Reachability Database.
3. **Retrieval**: Reporting Interface provides access to stored reachability data.

## Key Requirements
- Reports must be transmitted at least every 5 minutes.
- Data must be stored for a minimum of 30 days.
- Maximum allowable latency from reporting to storage: 1 second.
- All communication must use TLS 1.3 or higher.

## Data Format
- **Format**: JSON
- **Structure**:
  - `timestamp`: ISO 8601 format (e.g., `2023-10-05T14:30:00Z`)
  - `source_id`: String identifier for the reporting entity
  - `status`: Boolean (`true` = reachable, `false` = unreachable)
  - `latency_ms`: Integer (measured round-trip time in milliseconds)

## Tables
| Field Name      | Type   | Description                     | Required |
|------------------|--------|----------------------------------|----------|
| timestamp        | string | ISO 8601 timestamp                | Yes      |
| source_id        | string | Unique identifier for source      | Yes      |
| status           | bool   | Reachability status               | Yes      |
| latency_ms       | int    | Round-trip time in milliseconds   | No       |

## Notes
- The architecture supports up to 10,000 concurrent reporters.
- Minimum report size is 128 bytes; maximum is 1,024 bytes.
- Data integrity is ensured using SHA-256 checksums.

sections.title: Reachability_Reporting_overview
sections.summary:
# 8.1.21.1 Reachability Reporting Overview

**Section ID**: 8.1.21.1 | **Page**: 629-631

## Overview
- **Reachability**: Indicates which namespaces can be accessed in multi-namespace operations (e.g., Copy in NVM Command Set, Execute in Computational Programs Command Set).
- Defined at controller level: only namespaces attached to the same controller are reachable.
- **Support requirements**:
  - I/O controllers supporting Computational Programs Command Set must support Reachability Reporting.
  - Optional for those not supporting it.

## Reachability Group Availability
A Reachability Group becomes available to a controller if:
- a namespace is attached to the controller and the group was previously unassociated.
- a configuration change alters membership (e.g., new group in Reachability Groups log page, Section 5.2.12.1.25).

A Reachability Group becomes unavailable if:
- a namespace is detached and it was the sole namespace in the group for that controller (group no longer present in log page).

## Reachability Association Change
Occurs when a Reachability Group associated with a Reachability Association becomes available or unavailable (e.g., new or removed entry in Reachability Associations log page, Section 5.2.12.1.26).

## NVM Subsystem Requirements (if Reachability Reporting is supported)
All controllers in the subsystem must:
- Set `RRSUP` bit to `1` in the **Controller Reachability Capabilities (CRCAP)** field (Figure 328).
- Support **Reachability Groups Change Notices** (Section 5.2.26.1.5).
- Support **Reachability Association Change Notices** (Section 5.2.26.1.5).
- Support the **Reachability Groups log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.25).
- Support the **Reachability Associations log page** (Section 5.2.12.1.26).

## Namespace Requirements
- Each namespace must be a member of a Reachability Group.
- Supply a valid **Reachability Group Identifier (RGRPID)** in the **I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace Data Structure** (Figure 335).

## Reachability Definitions
- **Reachability Groups log page**: Defines groups of namespaces (Section 5.2.12.1.25).
- **Reachability Associations log page**: Links Reachability Groups and defines access characteristics (Section 5.2.12.1.26).
- All namespaces in a Reachability Group have identical access characteristics.
- All Reachability Groups in a Reachability Association have identical access characteristics.
- A namespace is always able to reach itself (no reachability constraint for identical NSIDs).
- If a Reachability Group is not in any Reachability Association, its namespaces are not reachable by any other namespaces.

## Reachability Association Characteristics (Refer to Figure 283)
| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `01h` | All namespaces in the group can reach each other without performance indication (e.g., Execute command). |
| `02h` | All namespaces are reachable and support fast copy operations (defined in NVM Command Set). |
| `03h` | All namespaces are reachable but do not support fast copy operations. |

## Key Constraints
- A namespace can belong to only one Reachability Group.
- A Reachability Group can be in zero or more Reachability Associations with different Characteristics values.
- The **Reachability Group Identifier (RGRPID)** must be unique within the NVM subsystem.
- If `RGIDC` bit in CRCAP is set to `1`, the RGRPID must remain unchanged while the namespace is attached.
- If `RGIDC` is `0`, the RGRPID may change; a **Reachability Groups Change Notice** must be issued if it does.

## Example (Figure 688)
- **Reachability Association 1 (RA 1)**:
  - NSID 10 and NSID 30 can reach each other.
  - NSID 10 and NSID 31 can reach each other.
  - NSID 30 and NSID 31: no defined reachability.
- **Reachability Association 2 (RA 2)**: Self-reference for Reachability Group A (RG A).
  - NSID 30 and NSID 31 can reach each other.
- **Reachability Association 3 (RA 3)**:
  - NSID 11 and NSID 30 can reach each other.
  - NSID 11 and NSID 31 can reach each other.
  - NSID 30 and NSID 31: no defined reachability.
- **No Reachability Association** between Reachability Group B (RG B) and Reachability Group D (RG D):
  - NSID 10 and NSID 11: cannot reach each other.
- **No self-referencing association** for Reachability Group E (RG E):
  - NSID 22 and NSID 23: cannot reach each other.

sections.title: Reachability_event_notifications
sections.summary:
# 8.1.21.2 Reachability Event Notifications

### Overview
- **Section ID**: 8.1.21.2 | **Page**: 631–632  
- Two types of notifications:  
  - **Reachability Group Change Notice**  
  - **Reachability Association Change Notice**

---

### Reachability Group Change Notice
- Triggered when:
  - An NSID is added/removed from a Reachability Group Descriptor (RGRPID).
  - A Reachability Group no longer has any NSIDs attached to the controller → not reported in the **Reachability Groups log page**.
  - NSID moves between RGRPID (i.e., RGRPID field in I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace Data Structure changes).
    - Condition: **RGIDC bit in CRCAP field** of Identify Controller data structure is set to **0** (refer to Figure 328).
- **Action**: Host must read the **Reachability Groups log page** (section 5.2.12.1.25) to validate changes.

---

### Reachability Association Change Notice
- Triggered when:
  - An RGID is added/removed from a Reachability Association Descriptor.
  - A Reachability Association no longer has any RGIDs associated with the controller → not reported in the **Reachability Associations log page**.
- **Action**: Host must read the **Reachability Associations log page** (section 5.2.12.1.26) to validate changes.

sections.title: Read_Recovery_Level
sections.summary:
# 8.1.22 Read_Recovery_Level

The **Read Recovery Level (RRL)** is an NVM Set configurable attribute that balances read command completion time and error recovery. It applies to the NVM Set and is inherited by namespaces within it. If NVM Sets are unsupported, all namespaces use the same RRL.

- **Controller Support**: Indicated in the *Controller Attributes* field of the *Identify Controller* data structure.  
- **Supported Levels**: Up to 16 levels possible.  
  - **Level 4 (M)**: Mandatory, default level (nominal recovery).  
  - **Level 15 (M)**: Mandatory, "Fast Fail" (minimum recovery).  
  - Levels are ordered: higher number = less recovery.  
  - **Level 0** (if supported): Maximum recovery.  
- **Configuration**:  
  - Set via `Set Features` command for *Read Recovery Level Config Feature*.  
  - Read via `Get Features` command for same feature.

sections.title: Replay_Protected_Memory_Block
sections.summary:
# 8.1.23 Replay Protected Memory Block (RPMB)

## Overview
RPMB provides authenticated, replay-protected data storage using a shared secret authentication key programmed during manufacturing. Data access uses Message Authentication Code (MAC) with a nonce and write counter to prevent replay attacks. Access before key programming returns `07h` (Authentication Key not yet programmed). Write failures (`05h`) occur if:
- `Boot Partition Write Protection Enabled` is set when not supported.
- Write protection is attempted on a partition in `Write Locked Until Power Cycle` state.
- `BPP0L` or `BPP1L` bits are changed when `BPPEE` is `0`.

If `Set Features Boot Partition Write Protection` is supported and enabled, controller sets `Boot Partition 0` and `Boot Partition 1` write protection states to `100b`.

## Architecture
- Supports multiple RPMB targets; targets are not contained in namespaces.
- RPMB targets operate independently; host must serialize `Security Send`/`Security Receive` commands per target.
- Each RPMB target has its own authentication key.
- `Security Send` and `Security Receive` commands use RPMB Data Frames (256 bytes + Data field).
- RPMB sector size: 512 bytes (independent of namespace data size).
- Security commands encapsulate RPMB data packets; completion only after requested message type is completed.

## RPMB Device Configuration Block (Figure 690)
- **Byte 00**:  
  - `BPPEE` (Boot Partition Protection Enable):  
    - Bit 0: `BPPED` (Boot Partition Write Protection Enabled)  
      - `1`: Enabled (cannot be disabled).  
      - `0`: Disabled or not supported.  
- **Byte 01**:  
  - `BPLS` (Boot Partition Protection State): Valid only when `BPPEE = 1`.  
    - Bit 1: `BPP1L` (Boot Partition 1 Write Locked)  
    - Bit 0: `BPP0L` (Boot Partition 0 Write Locked)  
- **Byte 02**:  
  - `WPC` (Write Protection Control):  
    - Bit 1: `PWPC` (Permanent Write Protect Control)  
      - `0`: Abort Set Features to Permanent Write Protect.  
      - `1`: Process Set Features.  
    - Bit 0: `WUPUCC` (Write Protect Until Power Cycle Control)  
      - `0`: Abort Set Features to Write Protect Until Power Cycle.  
      - `1`: Process Set Features.  
      - Reset to `0` after power cycle or Controller Level Reset.  
- Bytes 03–511: Reserved.

## Message Types (Figure 691)
| Type | Description | Requires Data | Frame Length (bytes) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0001h` | Authentication key programming request | No | 256 |
| `0002h` | Read Write Counter | No | 256 |
| `0003h` | Authenticated data write | Yes | M + 256 |
| `0004h` | Authenticated data read | No | 256 |
| `0005h` | Result read | No | 256 |
| `0006h` | Authenticated DCB write | Yes | 512 + 256 |
| `0007h` | Authenticated DCB read | No | 256 |
| `0100h` | Result read response | No | 256 |
| `0200h` | Write Counter response | No | 256 |
| `0300h` | Data write response | No | 256 |
| `0400h` | Data read response | Yes | M + 256 |
| `0600h` | DCB write response | No | 256 |
| `0700h` | DCB read response | Yes | 512 + 256 |

## RPMB Data Frame (Figure 694)
- **222–N:00**: Stuff Bytes (STBY) – Padding; not included in MAC.
- **222–(N-1)**: Message Authentication Code / Authentication Key (MAC/Key) – Size depends on authentication method (e.g., 32 bytes for SHA-256).
- **223**: RPBMP Target (RBT) – Target ID (0–6). Must match `NSSF` in command; otherwise, return error.
- **239–224**: Nonce (NCE) – Random host-generated number.
- **243–240**: Write Counter (WCNT) – Total successful authenticated data write requests.
- **247–244**: Address (ADDR) – Starting sector address.
- **251–248**: Sector Count (SCNT) – Number of 512-byte sectors.
- **253–252**: Result (RSLT) – Only in responses.
- **255–254**: Request/Response Message (RRM) – Message type.
- **(M+1)+256–256**: Data (DATA) – Optional; M = 512 * SCNT.

## Operation Status (Figure 692, Table 2)
| Value | Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| `00h` | Operation successful |
| `01h` | General failure |
| `02h` | Authentication failure (MAC mismatch or calculation failure) |
| `03h` | Counter failure (counters mismatch or increment failure) |
| `04h` | Address failure (out of range or alignment error) |
| `05h` | Write failure (data/counter/result write failure) |
| `06h` | Read failure (data/counter/result read failure) |
| `07h` | Authentication Key not yet programmed |
| `08h` | Invalid RPMB Device Configuration Block |
| `09h–3Fh` | Reserved |

## RPMB Frame Components
- **Write Counter Status (WCS)**: Bit 7 in status word – `1` = expired, `0` = valid.

sections.title: Authentication_Method
sections.summary:
### **8.1.23.1 Authentication Method**

- A controller supports one **Authentication Method** as specified in the **Identify Controller** data structure.
- If **HMAC SHA-256** is supported (per **RFC 6234**), the **message authentication code (MAC)** is computed using HMAC SHA-256.
- The **256-bit Authentication Key** (stored in the controller for the selected RPMB target) is used as the key.
- HMAC SHA-256 input:  
  - **Key**: 256-bit Authentication Key  
  - **Message**: Concatenation of the **RPMB Data Frame** fields, excluding:
    - **Stuff bytes**
    - **MAC field** (bytes [223:255])
  - Message order: **Bytes [223:255]** followed by **Data** of the frame.

sections.title: RPMB_Operations
sections.summary:
# 8.1.23.2 RPMB Operations

## Overview
- **Host-to-Controller Commands**: Use **Security Send** to send Request Message Types (e.g., write data, request operations).
- **Controller-to-Host Commands**: Use **Security Receive** to retrieve results (e.g., read data, write counter).
- If data exceeds the **Identify Controller** data limit, multiple commands are sent.
- Data transfer occurs via **RPMB Data Frames** containing command fields and MAC.

---

## 8.1.23.2.1 Authentication Key Programming

### Process
1. **Security Send 1**: Program Authentication Key (Request).
   - **RPMB Target**: Target to access.
   - **Write Counter**: `00000000h`.
   - **Address**: `00000000h`.
   - **Sector Count**: `00000000h`.
   - **MAC/Key**: Authentication Key to program.
   - **Request/Response**: `0001h` (Request).
2. **Security Send 2**: Request result (Request).
   - **MAC/Key**: `0...00h`.
   - **Request/Response**: `0005h` (Request).
3. **Security Receive**: Retrieve result.
   - **Result**: Result Code (e.g., success/failure).
   - **Request/Response**: `0100h` (Response).

---

## 8.1.23.2.2 Read Write Counter Value

### Process
1. **Security Send 1**: Request Write Counter value.
   - **RPMB Target**: Target to access.
   - **Nonce**: Host-generated.
   - **Write Counter**: `00000000h`.
   - **Request/Response**: `0002h` (Request).
2. **Security Receive 1**: Retrieve result.
   - **Write Counter**: Current value.
   - **Nonce**: Copy of host-generated nonce.
   - **Request/Response**: `0200h` (Response).

---

## 8.1.23.2.3 Authenticated Data Write

### Procedure
- **Security Send 1**:
  - **Request Message Type**: `0003h` (Request).
  - **Write Counter**: Current value.
  - **Address**: Target location.
  - **Sector Count**: Number of 512B blocks.
  - **MAC**: Host-generated.
  - **Data**: To be written.
  - **Request/Response**: `0003h` (Request).
- **Controller Validation**:
  1. **Write Counter Expired** → Result: `0085h` (Write failure).
  2. **Invalid Address** → Result: `0004h` (Address failure).
  3. **MAC Mismatch** → Result: `0002h` (Authentication failure).
  4. **Write Counter Mismatch** → Result: `0003h` (Counter failure).
  5. **Successful**: Data written, Write Counter incremented.
  6. **Other Failures** → Result: `0005h` (Write failure) or `0001h` (General failure).
- **Result Verification**:
  1. **Security Send 2**: Request result (`0005h`).
  2. **Security Receive**: Retrieve result (`0300h` Response).
     - **Result**: Result code.
     - **Write Counter**: Incremented value.
     - **MAC**: Controller-calculated.

---

## 8.1.23.2.4 Authenticated Data Read

### Procedure
- **Security Send 1**:
  - **Request Message Type**: `0004h` (Request).
  - **Nonce**: Host-generated.
  - **Address**: Target location.
  - **Sector Count**: Number of 512B blocks.
  - **Request/Response**: `0004h` (Request).
- **Controller Validation**:
  - **Invalid Address** → Result: `0004h` (Address failure).
- **Security Receive 1**:
  - **Response Message Type**: `0400h` (Response).
  - **Result**: `0006h` (Read failure) or `0001h` (General failure).
  - **MAC**: Controller-calculated.
  - **Data**: Read from RPMB.
- **Host Responsibility**: Verify returned MAC.

sections.title: Authenticated_Device_Configuration_Block_Write
sections.summary:
# 8.1.23.3 Authenticated Device Configuration Block Write

## Overview
- Initiated by a **Security Send** command.
- RPMB Data Frame from host to controller includes:
  - **Request Message Type**: `0006h`
  - **Sector Count**: `01h`
  - **MAC**: Host-generated
  - **Write Counter**: Current value
  - **Data**: RPMB Device Configuration Block structure (refer to Figure 699)
- All other fields cleared to `0h`.

## Key Requirements
- **Write Counter Expired**: If expired, result = `0005h` (write failure), no write occurs.
- **MAC Mismatch**: If calculated MAC ≠ received MAC, result = `0002h` (authentication failure), no write.
- **Boot Partition Protection Disabled**: If data attempts to disable, result = `0008h` (Invalid RPMB Device Configuration Block), no write.
- **Authentication Success**: Data written to RPMB Device Configuration Block.
- **Other Errors**: Result = `0001h` (general failure).

## Architecture & Behavior
- **Result Return**: Controller returns successful completion for **Security Send** regardless of write success.
- **Host Action**: On successful Security Send, host sends **Security Receive** to retrieve response.
  - Returns RPMB Data Frame with:
    - **Response Message Type**: `0600h`
    - **Write Counter**: Incremented value
    - **MAC**: Controller-generated
    - **Result**: Result code
    - All other fields cleared to `0h`.
- **Write Counter Independence**: Device Configuration Block counter is independent of RPMB target 0. Writes do not affect RPMB target 0 counter.
- **Read Access**: Current Write Counter value can be read via **Authenticated Device Configuration Block Read** (Section 8.1.23.4).

sections.title: Authenticated_Device_Configuration_Block_Read
sections.summary:
# 8.1.23.4 Authenticated Device Configuration Block Read

### Overview
- **Section ID**: 8.1.23.4 | **Page**: 643-644
- Initiated by a **Security Send** command.
- Host sends an RPMB data frame with:
  - **Request Message Type**: `0007h`
  - **Sector Count**: `01h`
  - **Nonce**: Generated by host
  - All other fields = `00h`
- On successful completion, host sends **Security Receive** to retrieve data.

### Response
Controller returns an RPMB data frame with:
- **Response Message Type**: `0700h`
- **Sector Count**: `01h`
- **Nonce**: Copy of host-generated nonce
- **Data**: RPMB Device Configuration Block Data Structure (Figure 690)
- **MAC**: Calculated from Response Type, Nonce, Address, Data, Result
- **Write Counter**: Current write counter value for the Device Configuration Block
- **Result**: 
  - `0002h`: Authentication failure (MAC calculation failed)
  - `0001h`: General failure (other errors)
- All other fields = `00h`

### Key Notes
- The **Write Counter** for the Device Configuration Block is independent of RPMB target 0.
- The **Write Counter value** returned is shown in Figure 700.
- MAC validation is required for data integrity and authentication.

sections.title: Reservations
sections.summary:
# 8.1.24 Reservations

## Overview
- **Section ID**: 8.1.24 | **Page**: 644–646
- Provides coordination for two or more hosts accessing a shared namespace.
- Incorrect use may cause data corruption or system impairment.
- Reservation conflict handling after division events is defined in section 3.2.5.2.

## Reservation Conflict Handling
- A command is checked for reservation conflict at the start of processing.
- If conflict is detected, the controller aborts the command with **Reservation Conflict** status.
- Once allowed, a command cannot be later aborted due to a new reservation.

## Host-Controller Association
- Each controller in a multi-path I/O environment is associated with exactly one host.
- Hosts may be associated with multiple controllers (e.g., Host A in Figure 701).
- Hosts must register a **non-zero Host Identifier** (via Set Features) with each controller before using reservations.
- The Host Identifier ensures consistent reservation rights across all controllers for a host.

## Host Identifier Requirements
- If the **RHII** bit in the `CTRATT` field of Identify Controller (Figure 328) is set to '1', reservations require a non-zero Host Identifier.
- If controller does **not** support reservations with Host Identifier `0h`:
  - A reservation command from a host with Host Identifier `0h` is aborted with **Host Identifier Not Initialized**.
- If controller **does** support reservations with Host Identifier `0h`:
  - Registrations/reservations remain associated with the host using `0h`, not with a host using a non-zero identifier.
- Commands from a host with Host Identifier `0h` that conflict with existing reservations (e.g., as in Figure 702 and 703) are aborted with **Reservation Conflict**.

## Support Requirements
- **Optional** per namespace and controller.
- **Namespace support** indicated by non-zero **Reservation Capabilities (RESCAP)** in Identify Namespace data structure.
- **Controller support** indicated by **Reservations Support (RESERVS)** bit set to '1' in **Optional NVM Command Support (ONCS)** field of Identify Controller (Figure 328).

## Invalid Command Handling
- Commands (Reservation Report, Register, Acquire, Release) are aborted with **Invalid Command Opcode** if:
  - Target controller does not support reservations.
  - Target namespace does not support reservations.

## Controller Requirements (if supporting reservations):
- Set RESERVS bit in ONCS to '1'.
- Support:
  - Reservation Report (Section 7.8)
  - Reservation Register (Section 7.6)
  - Reservation Acquire (Section 7.5)
  - Reservation Release (Section 7.7)
  - Reservation Notification log page
  - Reservation Log Page Available asynchronous events
  - Reservation Notification Mask Feature
  - Host Identifier Feature
  - Reservation Persistence Feature

## Dispersed Namespace Support
- If controller supports dispersed namespaces and reservations:
  - Support **Dispersed Namespace Reservation Support (DISNSRS)** bit set to '1' in relevant commands (Reservation Report, Register, Acquire, Release) per Section 8.1.10.6.

## Namespace Requirements (if supporting reservations):
- Non-zero value in RESCAP field.
- Support **Persist Through Power Loss (PTPL)** state.
- Support sufficient resources to register a reservation key on **every controller** in the NVM subsystem with access to the shared namespace (Reservation Register must not fail due to resource exhaustion).

## Note
- **Ignore Existing Key** behavior has been updated for better compatibility with SCSI implementations.
- Conformance to updated behavior is indicated in the RESCAP field. Refer to NVM Express Base Specification, Revision 1.2.1, for previous definition.

sections.title: Reservation_Types
sections.summary:
# 8.1.24.1 Reservation_Types

The NVM Express interface supports six reservation types:
- Write Exclusive
- Exclusive Access
- Write Exclusive - Registrants Only
- Exclusive Access - Registrants Only
- Write Exclusive - All Registrants
- Exclusive Access - All Registrants

Differences among types relate to:
- Excluded access type (writes or all accesses)
- Access rights of registrants vs. reservation holder
- Whether registrants are also reservation holders

Reservations and registrations persist across Controller Level Resets and NVM Subsystem Resets, except those due to power loss. Reservations may optionally persist through power loss using the **Persist Through Power Loss State (PTPLS)**, which is associated with each namespace supporting reservations and can be modified via:
- Reservation Register command (Section 7.6)
- Set Features command (Section 5.2.26)

---

sections.title: Reservation_Notifications
sections.summary:
# 8.1.24.2 Reservation Notifications

- **Types**: Three types of reservation notifications:  
  1. Registration preempted  
  2. Reservation released  
  3. Reservation preempted  

- **Trigger**: Notifications occur when specific conditions are met (detailed in related sections).  
- **Log Page**: A *Reservation Notification* log page is created when an unmasked notification occurs on a namespace associated with the controller.  
- **Masking**: Notifications can be masked per reservation type and per namespace ID using the **Reservation Notification Mask** feature (see section 5.2.26.1.33).  
- **Event Notification**: A host may use the **Asynchronous Event Request** command (see section 5.2.2) to be notified of available Reservation Notification log pages (see section 5.2.12.1.34).

sections.title: Registering
sections.summary:
# 8.1.24.3 Registering

### Overview
A host must register a **reservation key** with a namespace before reserving it. This key identifies the host, enables authentication, and allows preemption of failed/uncooperative registrants. The key value and selection method are outside the scope of this specification.

### Key Requirements
- **Registration** creates a host–namespace association.
- A host only needs to register on **one controller** (with the same Host Identifier) to become a registrant on **all controllers** associated with the host and having access to the namespace.
- For **dispersed namespaces**, registration on one controller in any participating NVM subsystem suffices for registration across **all participating subsystems** and associated controllers.

### Reservation Register Command (Section 7.6)
Execute the **Reservation Register** command with:
- **RREGA field = 000b** (Register Reservation Key)
- **NRKEY field** contains the reservation key value.

#### Behavior for RREGA = 000b:
- **IEKEY field is ignored.**
- If a registrant attempts to register with a **different reservation key**, the command **aborts** with **Reservation Conflict** status.
- Multiple registrations of the **same key** are permitted.

#### Key Values
- No restrictions on reservation key values across hosts with **different Host Identifiers** (i.e., multiple hosts may use the same key).

### Replacing Reservation Key
To replace an existing key, use the Reservation Register command with:
- **RREGA field = 010b** (Replace Reservation Key)
- **CRKEY field** = current reservation key
- **NRKEY field** = new reservation key

#### Rules:
- Replacement applies to **all controllers** with the same Host Identifier as the processing controller.
- For **dispersed namespaces**, applies to **all participating NVM subsystems**.
- If **CRKEY does not match** the current key, command **aborts** with **Reservation Conflict**.
- **IEKEY bit = 1** allows replacement **without regard** to current registration status or key value.
- Replacement **does not affect any reservation** held on the namespace.

sections.title: Unregistering
sections.summary:
# 8.1.24.4 Unregistering

A host unregistering from a namespace must execute a **Reservation Register** command (Section 7.6) with:
- **RREGA field set to `001b`** (Unregister Reservation Key)
- **CRKEY field** containing its current reservation key

**Conditions for failure**:
- If **CRKEY does not match** the current key → **Reservation Conflict** status
- If the host is **not a registrant** → **Reservation Conflict** status

**Success**:
- Host is no longer a registrant of the namespace.

**Alternative unregister method**:
- Set **IEKEY bit to '1'** in the Reservation Register command to unregister **without regard to current reservation key**.

**Reservation release**:
- Unregistering may release a reservation held by the host.
- Reservation is released if:
  - The host is the **last remaining reservation holder** (reservation type: *Write Exclusive - All Registrants* or *Exclusive Access - All Registrants*)
  - The host is the **only reservation holder**

**Reservation released notification**:
- If the released reservation was of type:
  - *Write Exclusive - Registrants Only*
  - *Exclusive Access - Registrants Only*
- A **reservation released notification** is sent to **all controllers** associated with **registered hosts other than the unregistrant**.

sections.title: Acquiring_a_Reservation
sections.summary:
### 8.1.24.5 Acquiring a Reservation

- **Section ID**: 8.1.24.5 | **Page**: 650-650

#### Key Requirements:
- Host must be a **registrant** of the namespace to acquire a reservation.
- Reservation is obtained via the **Reservation Acquire command** (Section 7.5).
- **RACQA field** must be set to `000b` (Acquire).
- **CRKEY field** must contain the current reservation key associated with the host; must match the key used during registration.
- If **CRKEY does not match**, command aborts with **Reservation Conflict** status.
- If host is not a registrant, command aborts with **Reservation Conflict** status.

#### Reservation Rules:
- Only **one reservation** is allowed per namespace at a time.
- If a registrant attempts to acquire a reservation on a namespace already reserved:
  - Command aborts with **Reservation Conflict**.
- If a reservation holder attempts to acquire a reservation of a **different type** on the same namespace:
  - Command aborts with **Reservation Conflict**.
- If a reservation holder attempts to acquire a reservation of the **same type**:
  - Not a **Reservation Conflict**; command is processed.
- A reservation holder may **preempt** a reservation to **change the reservation type**.

sections.title: Releasing_a_Reservation
sections.summary:
# 8.1.24.6 Releasing a Reservation

- **Only the reservation holder** can release a reservation on a namespace.
- **Sequence for releasing a reservation**:
  1. Execute the **Reservation Release command** (Section 7.7).
  2. Set **RRELA** field to `000b` (Release).
  3. Set **RTYPE** field to the reservation type being released.
  4. Provide the **current reservation key (CRKEY)** matching the host's registration key.

- **Error conditions**:
  - If **CRKEY does not match**, command aborts with **Reservation Conflict** status.
  - If **RTYPE does not match** the current reservation type, command completes with **Invalid Field in Command** status.

- **Behavior when no reservation exists or host is not holder**:
  - Command completes **successfully** but has **no effect**.

- **Reservation released notification**:
  - Triggered when reservation is released and **RTYPE is not Write Exclusive or Exclusive Access**.
  - Sent to **all controllers** in the NVM subsystem associated with **registrants**, **excluding** the controller of the host issuing the command.

sections.title: Preempting_a_Reservation_or_Registration
sections.summary:
# 8.1.24.7 Preempting a Reservation or Registration

## Overview
A host that is a **registrant** may preempt a reservation or registration by executing a **Reservation Acquire** command (Section 7.5) with:
- **RACQA** field set to:
  - `001b` (Preempt)
  - `010b` (Preempt and Abort)
- **CRKEY** (Current Reservation Key) matching the host’s current reservation key.

If **CRKEY does not match**, the command is aborted with **Reservation Conflict**. If the host is **not a registrant**, the command is aborted with **Reservation Conflict**.

## Preemption Actions Based on Reservation Type
### Case 1: Reservation Type ≠ Write Exclusive - All Registrants & ≠ Exclusive Access - All Registrants
- **PRKEY matches current reservation holder**:
  - All registrants with matching reservation key (except issuing host) are unregistered.
  - Reservation is released.
  - New reservation of type specified in **RTYPE** is created for the issuing host.

- **PRKEY ≠ current reservation holder and PRKEY ≠ 0h**:
  - Registrants with PRKEY matching are unregistered.

- **PRKEY = 0h**:
  - Command aborted with **Invalid Field in Command**.

### Case 2: Reservation Type = Write Exclusive - All Registrants or Exclusive Access - All Registrants
- **PRKEY = 0h**:
  - All registrants (except issuing host) are unregistered.
  - Reservation is released.
  - New reservation of type specified in **RTYPE** is created for the issuing host.

- **PRKEY ≠ 0h**:
  - Registrants with matching reservation key are unregistered.
  - If no such registrants exist, command is aborted with **Reservation Conflict**.

### Case 3: No Reservation Held
- Registrants whose reservation key matches **PRKEY** are unregistered.

## Self-Preemption
A reservation holder may preempt itself:
- Registration is maintained.
- Reservation is released.
- New reservation of type **RTYPE** is created.

## Preempt and Abort (RACQA = 010b)
Same behavior as Preempt (`001b`) **except**:
- All controllers associated with hosts whose reservation/registration is preempted are requested to **abort all commands** addressed to the specified namespace (NSID).
- Completion of the **Reservation Acquire** command **waits** for all requested command aborts to complete (even if some cannot be aborted).
- Command abort is **best effort** (may be incomplete or already completed).
- Prompt execution of aborts is recommended to reduce delay.

## Notifications
- When a registrant is unregistered, a **registration preempted notification** occurs on all controllers **except** the issuing host.
- When reservation type changes, a **reservation released notification** occurs on all controllers associated with **remaining registrants** except the issuing host.

sections.title: Clearing_a_Reservation
sections.summary:
### 8.1.24.8 Clearing a Reservation

**Purpose**: A host that is a registrant may clear a reservation (release the reservation and unregister all registrants) on a namespace.

**Requirements**:
- Execute a **Reservation Release command** (Section 7.7).
- Set the **Reservation Release Action (RRELA)** field to `001b` (i.e., **Clear**).
- Supply the **Current Reservation Key (CRKEY)** associated with the host.

**Conditions**:
- If the **CRKEY** does not match the host's registered key → **Abort** with status code **Reservation Conflict**.
- If the host is not a registrant → **Abort** with status code **Reservation Conflict**.

**Atomic Operation**:
- The reservation held on the namespace (if any) is released.
- All registrants are unregistered from the namespace.

**Notification**:
- A **reservation preempted notification** is sent to all controllers in the NVM subsystem associated with hosts whose registrations are removed—**except** those associated with the host that issued the command.

sections.title: Reporting_Reservation_Status
sections.summary:
# 8.1.24.9 Reporting Reservation Status

- **Section ID**: 8.1.24.9 | **Page**: 652-652  
- A host determines the current reservation status of a namespace by executing the **Reservation Report command** (refer to Section 7.8).  
- No additional detailed requirements, definitions, or architectural specifics are provided in the given excerpt.

sections.title: Rotational_Media
sections.summary:
# 8.1.25 Rotational_Media

### Overview
Rotational media (e.g., HDDs, CD-ROMs) uses electromechanical methods for data access, differing from non-rotational media (e.g., NAND). It includes spinning platters and actuators.

### Controller Requirements
A controller supporting namespaces on rotational media must:
- **a)** Set `Rotational Media` bit to `'1'` in the `NSFEAT` field of the I/O Command Set Independent Identify Namespace data structure (NVM Express NVM Command Set Specification).
- **b)** Support the **Rotational Media Information** log page (Section 5.2.12.1.22).
- **c)** Support the **Spinup Control** feature (Section 5.2.26.1.18).
- **d)** Support **Endurance Groups** (Section 3.2.3).
- **e)** Set `EG Rotational Media` bit to `'1'` in the `EGFEAT` field of the Endurance Group Information log page for each rotational media endurance group.

### Power State Behavior
- If a namespace on rotational media is attached but its spindle is not spinning, the controller must enter **non-operational power state** (NOPS = `'1'`, Figure 329).

### NVM Subsystem Reset Behavior
For a domain with an endurance group on rotational media:
- If **Spinup Control** is:
  - **Disabled**: Initial spinup for all such endurance groups in the domain is initiated.
  - **Enabled**: Initial spinup is **inhibited** during NVM Subsystem Reset until a controller in the domain issues a **Set Features (Power Management)** command with an operational power state.

### Transport Consideration
- If using **PCIe transport**, the **PCIe Slot Power Control** feature may affect supported power states (refer to PCI Express Base Specification).

sections.title: Sanitize_Operations
sections.summary:
# 8.1.26 Sanitize Operations

A **sanitize operation** alters all user data in the sanitization target such that recovery is prohibitively difficult (per IEEE Std 2883). The scope differs between:
- **NVM subsystem sanitize operation** (Section 1.5.70): Affects all media allocated for user data, volatile caches, and non-volatile caches containing user data. Sub-controllers' Submission/Completion Queues may be altered (implementation-specific), while all other Controller Memory Buffer data is altered.
- **Namespace sanitize operation** (Section 1.5.65): Affects only the namespace's media, including all media allocated for use by the sanitization target, and any volatile or non-volatile caches associated with that namespace.

### Key Requirements and Behavior:
- **Global Data Erased Bit**: If a namespace sanitize operation is performed on every namespace and no user data has been written since, the **Global Data Erased bit** in the Sanitize Status log page shall **not be set to '1'**.
- **Media Protection**: If user data was not successfully purged during an NVM subsystem sanitize operation, the media must be made permanently inaccessible via all interfaces (including management).
- **Composition Changes**: If the NVM subsystem composition changes (e.g., new domain, division) and prevents successful sanitization, the operation fails. Changes that do not impede sanitization do not cause failure. If media verification is prevented due to composition changes, the **MVCNCLD bit** is set to '1'.
- **Excluded Areas**: Sanitize operations **do not affect**:
  - Replay Protected Memory Block
  - Boot partitions
  - Media and caches not containing user data
- **Log Pages and Features**: May be modified to prevent user data derivation (refer to Section 8.1.26.3).
- **Controller Level Reset**: Once started, sanitize operations in **Restricted Processing**, **Unrestricted Processing**, **Media Verification**, or **Post-Verification Deallocation** states cannot be aborted and continue across resets and power cycles.
- **PMR**: Required to be disabled before an NVM subsystem sanitize operation may start.

### Table 8.1.26: Sanitize Operations

| NVM Subsystem Data | NVM Subsystem Sanitize Operation | Namespace Sanitize Operation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Media allocated for user data | Purge all user data (per IEEE Std 2883) from all media | Purge all data in the namespace from all media allocated for use by the sanitization target |
| Media that is deallocated | Purge all data | Purge all data from all media allocated for use by the sanitization target |
| Volatile caches that contain user data | Purge all data | Purge all data in the volatile cache used by the sanitization target |
| Non-Volatile caches that contain user data ¹ | Purge all data | Purge all data written in the sanitization target |
| Media not able to be written (e.g., write-protected) | Make not retrievable | Make not retrievable |
| NVM subsystem information (e.g., serial number) | No effect | No effect |
| Firmware | No effect | No effect |
| Feature values (current/saved) | Feature-specific; may be modified to prevent data derivation | Purge Namespace Metadata and Namespace Admin Label; others may be modified to prevent data derivation |
| Log pages | May be modified to prevent data derivation | May be modified to prevent data derivation |
| Security credentials (e.g., in-band authentication) | No effect | No effect |
| Boot partition | No effect | No effect |
| CMB (Controller Memory Buffer) | Implementation specific | No effect |
| HMB | No effect | No effect |
| PMR | Required to be disabled before operation | No effect |

> ¹ *Non-Volatile caches may be updated via firmware and are not necessarily cleared during operation.*

sections.title: Common_Requirements_For_Commands_Requesting_Saniti
sections.summary:
# 8.1.26.1 Common Requirements For Commands Requesting Sanitize Operations

**Section ID:** 8.1.26.1 | **Page:** 655-656

### Overview
This section defines common requirements for commands requesting sanitize operations:  
- **Sanitize command** (Section 5.2.22)  
- **Sanitize Namespace command** (Section 5.2.23)  

These commands initiate, recover from, or exit a sanitize operation (e.g., Block Erase, Crypto Erase, Overwrite), which runs **in the background**. Completion is indicated via **asynchronous events** and the **Sanitize Status log page**.

### Key Requirements
- **Completion Indication**:  
  - **Sanitize Operation Completed**:  
    - Event Specific Parameter = 0h if target is NVM subsystem  
    - Event Specific Parameter = NSID if target is namespace  
  - **Sanitize Operation Completed With Unexpected Deallocation**: NSID field = 0h  
  - **Sanitize Operation Entered Media Verification State**:  
    - Event Specific Parameter = 0h if target is NVM subsystem  
    - Event Specific Parameter = NSID if target is namespace  

- **Asynchronous Event Reporting**:
  - If command submitted to **Admin Submission Queue** → Event reported by **that controller**  
  - If command submitted via **Management Endpoint** → **No event reported** by any controller  

- **Command Completion**:
  - If command starts sanitize → Return **Successful Completion**  
  - If command fails to start sanitize (status ≠ Successful Completion):  
    - Do **not** start sanitize  
    - Do **not** update Sanitize Status log page  
    - Do **not** alter user data  

- **Error Conditions**:
  - **Unsupported SANACT value** (Figures 388, 391) → Abort with **Invalid Field in Command**  
  - **NVM subsystem divided** (multi-domain) → Abort with **Asymmetric Access Inaccessible** or **Asymmetric Access Persistent Loss**  
  - **Pending firmware activation with reset**:  
    - If Firmware Commit returned:  
      a) Firmware Activation Requires Controller Level Reset  
      b) Firmware Activation Requires Conventional Reset  
      c) Firmware Activation Requires NVM Subsystem Reset  
      → Abort with same status code  
    - Otherwise → Abort with **Firmware Activation Requires Controller Level Reset**  
  - **Pending personality settings change** → Abort Sanitize command with **Access Denied**  

- **Firmware Activation**:
  - **Prohibited during sanitize operation** (refer to Section 8.1.26.5)  

- **Post-Validation**:
  - After successful parameter validation:  
    - Start sanitize in background  
    - Update Sanitize Status log page for target  
    - Complete the command with **Successful Completion**  

- **Critical Warnings**:
  - Ignore Critical Warning(s) (e.g., read-only mode) in SMART / Health Information log page  
  - Attempt to complete sanitize despite warnings

sections.title: Elements_of_Sanitize_Operations
sections.summary:
# 8.1.26.2 Elements of Sanitize Operations

A sanitize operation includes:
- **Sanitize processing**, which may involve:
  - Deallocation of all user-data-allocated media (if permitted).
  - Additional media modification.
- **Optional verification** of user-data-allocated media.
- **Post-verification deallocation** of all user-data-allocated media (if verification occurs).

Sanitize processing occurs in either:
- **Restricted Processing state** (if AUSE = 0).
- **Unrestricted Processing state** (if AUSE = 1).

**Additional media modification** is required for NVM subsystem sanitization targets if:
- NODMMAS = `10b` (from Figure 328),
- EMVS = 0 (Enter Media Verification State bit),
- NDAS = 1 (No-Deallocate After Sanitize bit).

**Media verification** is enabled only when:
- EMVS = 1,
- Sanitize processing completes successfully,
- The Sanitize Operation State Machine enters the Media Verification state.

Media verification enables host audit (refer to Section 1.5.11) by allowing successful reads even if error correction codes are invalidated (e.g., during Block Erase or Crypto Erase).

**Deallocation of user-data-allocated media** occurs in exactly one of:
1. **Restricted Processing state** – if:
   - EMVS = 0,
   - AUSE = 0,
   - NDAS = 0, or
   - NDAS = 1 and unexpected deallocation occurs.
   - **Failure**: Sanitize processing fails.

2. **Unrestricted Processing state** – if:
   - EMVS = 0,
   - AUSE = 1,
   - NDAS = 0, or
   - NDAS = 1 and unexpected deallocation occurs.
   - **Failure**: Sanitize processing fails.

3. **Post-Verification Deallocation state** – after successful media verification:
   - Controller deallocates all user-data-allocated media.
   - Success → Sanitization target enters **Idle state**.
   - Failure → Enters **Restricted Failure** or **Unrestricted Failure** state (per Section 8.1.26.4.7).

**Controller Level Reset** may skip the Media Verification and Post-Verification Deallocation states (per Section 8.1.26.4).

sections.title: Sanitize_Operation_Types_and_Support
sections.summary:
# 8.1.26.3 Sanitize Operation Types and Support

## Overview
The **Sanitize Capabilities (SANICAP)** field in the Identify Controller data structure (Figure 328) indicates supported sanitize operation types and controller attributes. Supported operation types:
- **Block Erase**: Low-level block erase for all media locations in the sanitization target.
- **Crypto Erase**: Changes media encryption keys for all media locations in the sanitization target.
- **Overwrite**: Writes fixed data patterns (defined in Figure 705) one or more times to all media locations.

Controller attributes:
- **No-Deallocate Modifies Media After Sanitize (NODMMAS)**: If `10b`, media is modified if NDAS = `1` in the sanitize command.
- **No-Deallocate Inhibited (NDI)**: Indicates support for the NDAS bit in the Sanitize command.
- **Verification Support (VERS)**: Supports Media Verification and Post-Verification Deallocation for block erase/cryo erase NVM subsystem sanitize operations.
- **Namespace Verification Support (NVERS)**: Supports Media Verification and Post-Verification Deallocation for namespace sanitize operations.

**Overwrite** is media-specific (e.g., may harm NAND endurance). If **Key Per I/O** is supported, sanitize operations must make recovery of original user data (via KEYTAG) infeasible.

## Command Submission
To start a sanitize operation:
- **Sanitize command** (`SANACT`):
  - `010b`: Block Erase NVM subsystem
  - `011b`: Overwrite NVM subsystem
  - `100b`: Crypto Erase NVM subsystem
- **Sanitize Namespace command** (`SANACT` = `100b`: Crypto Erase namespace)

After successful sanitize, user data values are defined by the NVM Express I/O Command Set specifications.

## Sanitize Status Log Page (Section 5.2.12.1.36)
- Indicates estimated time, parameters, and status of the most recent sanitize operation.
- Reports in progress if:
  - Sanitize processing is ongoing
  - In **Media Verification** state
  - In **Post-Verification Deallocation** state
- **GDE bit**: Indicates if NVM subsystem has user data (when no NVM subsystem operation is in progress).
- **NDE bit**: Indicates if namespace has user data (when no namespace operation is in progress).
- **Initialized** before controller readiness (sections 3.5.3, 3.5.4).
- **Updated** on namespace creation and state transitions (Section 8.1.26.4).
- **Progress monitoring**: Host should limit polling to ≤ once every several minutes.
- **SPROG field**: Indicates progress in long-running states (Restricted Processing, Unrestricted Processing, Post-Verification Deallocation). Initialized to `0h` on entry; updated per Figure 302. Not modified except as specified.

## Completion & Event Handling
- Sanitize operation completes when target enters:
  - **Idle**
  - **Restricted Failure**
  - **Unrestricted Failure**
- After completion or entry to **Media Verification**, host should read Sanitize Status log page with NSID and Retain Asynchronous Event = `0` to clear pending asynchronous events.
- If **Sanitize** command is supported:
  - All controllers must:
    - Support **Sanitize Status log page**
    - Support **Sanitize Operation Completed** asynchronous event
    - Support **Sanitize Operation Completed With Unexpected Deallocation** if Sanitize Config feature is enabled
    - Support **Exit Failure Mode** action
    - Support ≥1 sanitize operation type (Block Erase, Overwrite, Crypto Erase)
    - Support same set of operation types across all controllers
    - Indicate supported types in **Sanitize Capabilities**
    - If **VERS** or **NVERS** = `1`, support:
      - **FAILS** field
      - **SANS** field
      - **Media Verification** and **Post-Verification Deallocation** states
      - **Sanitize Operation Entered Media Verification State** event

## Sanitize Config Feature (Section 5.2.26.1.15)
- **No-Deallocate Response Mode (NODRM)**:
  - **Error Response Mode**: Aborts Sanitize command with **Invalid Field in Command** if NDAS = `1` and NDI = `1`.
  - **Warning Response Mode**: Processes command; if successful, sets **SOS** = `100b` (**Sanitized Unexpected Deallocate**) in Sanitize Status log page.

---

### Table 8.1.26.3: Overwrite Pattern Behavior (Figure 705)
| OIPBP¹ | Overwrite Pass Count¹ | Overwrite Pass Number | User Data except PI Metadata | Protection Information² |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0` | All | All | Overwrite Pattern¹ | Each byte set to `FFh` |
| `1` | Even | First | Inversion of Overwrite Pattern¹ | Each byte cleared to `00h` |
| | | Subsequent | Inversion of Overwrite Pattern¹ from previous pass (bit XOR with `1`) | |
| `1` | Odd | First | Overwrite Pattern¹ | Each byte set to `FFh` |
| | | Subsequent | Inversion of Overwrite Pattern¹ from previous pass (bit XOR with `1`) | |

**Notes:**
1. Parameters in Command Dword 10 (`OIPBP`, `Overwrite Pass Count`) and Dword 11 (`Overwrite Pattern`). See Section 5.2.22.
2. If Protection Information is present in metadata.

---

## 8.1.26.3.1 Sanitize NVM Subsystem Failure Handling
- If NVM subsystem sanitize fails (enters **Restricted Failure** or **Unrestricted Failure**):
  - Abort non-allowed commands with **Sanitize Failed** until:
    - A new successful NVM subsystem sanitize operation starts
    - Or **Exit Failure Mode** action is executed (Section 5.2.22).

## 8.1.26.3.2 Sanitize Namespace Failure Handling
- If namespace sanitize fails:
  - Abort all **I/O commands** on the failed NSID with **Sanitize Namespace Failed**.
  - Process **Admin commands** (excluding Sanitize Namespace-specific restrictions) with **Sanitize Namespace Failed** status.

sections.title: Sanitize_Operation_State_Machine
sections.summary:
# 8.1.26.4 Sanitize Operation State Machine

## Overview
- **Purpose**: Defines the state of sanitization for each supported sanitization target (NVM subsystem or allocated namespace).
- **Instance**: One state machine per supported sanitization target.
- **Transitions**: Described in Figure 706; labeled with a letter (condition) and optional number (differentiates transitions with same condition).
- **Asynchronous Events**: Reported in Completion Queue entry for Asynchronous Event Request command:
  - **Dword 0 (Figure 150)**:
    - Log Page Identifier = `81h` (Sanitize Status log page).
    - Asynchronous Event Information:
      - `01h` (Sanitize Operation Completed).
      - `02h` (Sanitize Operation Completed With Unexpected Deallocation).
      - `03h` (Sanitize Operation Entered Media Verification State).
    - Asynchronous Event Type = `110b` (I/O Command specific status).
  - **Dword 1 (Figure 151)**:
    - Event Specific Parameter = NSID for sanitization target. For NVM subsystem, NSID = `0h`.

- **Sanitize Status Log Page**:
  - **Sanitize State (SANS)**: Updated to the value of the new state on each transition.
  - **Sanitize Progress (SPROG)**: Cleared to `0h` in Idle state.
  - **Media Verification Canceled (MVCNCLD)**: Cleared to `0` in Idle state.

---

## 8.1.26.4.1 Idle State
- **Description**: No sanitize operation is in progress.
- **Conditions**:
  - No prior sanitize operation or last one was successful.
  - After an unrestricted failure, transitioned from Unrestricted Failure to Idle via **Exit Failure Mode**.
- **Operations**:
  - Sanitize and Sanitize Namespace commands processed without restrictions.
  - All power management resumes.
  - Clear SPROG to `0h` and MVCNCLD to `0` in Sanitize Status log page.

- **State Transitions (Table 8_1_26_4_1_Idle_State)**:
  | Starting | Ending | Label | Transition Condition |
  | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
  | Idle | Restricted Processing | A1 | Start sanitize in restricted mode (AUSE = `0`) |
  | Idle | Unrestricted Processing | B1 | Start sanitize in unrestricted mode (AUSE = `1`) |

---

## 8.1.26.4.2 Restricted Processing State
- **Description**: Sanitize processing is in progress.
- **Failure**: Transitions to Restricted Failure state.
- **Operations**:
  - Set SPROG as per Figure 302.
  - Perform additional media modification (Section 8.1.26.2).
  - Deallocate all user data media (if permitted).
  - Set MVCNCLD to `1` if:
    - NVM subsystem composition changes.
    - Controller Level Reset occurs (transport-specific or subsystem reset).
  - All controllers/Mgmt Endpoints process commands per Section 8.1.26.5.
  - **Abort**:
    - NVM subsystem target: Sanitize/Sanitize Namespace → Sanitize In Progress.
    - Namespace target: Sanitize/Sanitize Namespace → Sanitize Namespace In Progress.
  - **Upon Completion**:
    - Set SANS to `0h` (Idle) and:
      - NVM subsystem target:
        - If Sanitize Namespace not supported: set GDE = `1`.
        - If supported: set GDE = `1` and NDE = `1` for each namespace.
      - Namespace target: set NDE = `1`.
    - Set FAILS = `1h` (Restricted Processing state).
    - Report asynchronous event:
      - Sanitize Operation Completed or
      - Sanitize Operation Completed With Unexpected Deallocation (as per Section 8.1.26.1).
    - If EMVS = `1` and no MVCNCLD, transition to Media Verification state (via F1).

- **State Transitions (Table 8_1_26_4_2_Restricted_Processing_State)**:
  | Starting | Ending | Label | Transition Condition |
  | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
  | Restricted Processing | Idle | C1 | Sanitize completes, EMVS = `0` or (EMVS = `1`, MVCNCLD = `1`, deallocation succeeds) |
  | Restricted Processing | Restricted Failure | D1 | Sanitize fails |
  | Restricted Processing | Media Verification | F1 | Sanitize completes, EMVS = `1`, MVCNCLD = `0` |

---

## 8.1.26.4.3 Restricted Failure State
- **Description**: Entered when sanitize processing fails or deallocation fails in Post-Verification Deallocation.
- **Operations**:
  - All controllers/Mgmt Endpoints process commands per Section 8.1.26.5.
  - Recovery requires a **Sanitize command with AUSE = `0`** (restricted mode).
  - **Abort**:
    - NVM subsystem target:
      - SANACT = `001b` (Exit Failure Mode) → Sanitize Failed.
      - SANACT = `101b` (Exit Media Verification State) → Invalid Field in Command.
      - AUSE = `1` → Sanitize Failed.
    - Namespace target:
      - SANACT = `001b` → Sanitize Namespace Failed.
      - SANACT = `101b` → Invalid Field in Command.
      - AUSE = `1` → Sanitize Namespace Failed.
  - Persistent Memory Region: Behave as per Section 8.1.26.5.
  - **Recovery**: Restart sanitize operation in Restricted Processing state.
  - Clear SPROG to `0h` and MVCNCLD to `0` in Sanitize Status log page.

- **State Transitions (Table 8_1_26_4_3_Restricted_Failure_State)**:
  | Starting | Ending | Label | Transition Condition |
  | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
  | Restricted Failure | Restricted Processing | A2 | Start sanitize in restricted mode (AUSE = `0`) |

---

## 8.1.26.4.4 Unrestricted Processing State
- **Description**: Sanitize processing in unrestricted mode; failure leads to Unrestricted Failure.
- **Operations**:
  - Set SPROG as per Figure 302.
  - Perform additional media modification (Section 8.1.26.2).
  - Deallocate user data media (if permitted).
  - Set MVCNCLD to `1` if:
    - NVM subsystem composition changes.
    - Controller Level Reset occurs (transport-specific or subsystem reset).
  - All controllers/Mgmt Endpoints process commands per Section 8.1.26.5.
  - **Abort**:
    - NVM subsystem target: Sanitize/Sanitize Namespace → Sanitize In Progress.
    - Namespace target: Sanitize/Sanitize Namespace → Sanitize Namespace In Progress.
  - **Upon Completion**:
    - Set SANS to `0h` (Idle) and:
      - NVM subsystem target:
        - If Sanitize Namespace not supported: GDE = `1`.
        - If supported: GDE = `1`, NDE = `1` for each namespace.
      - Namespace target: NDE = `1`.
    - Set FAILS = `1h` (Unrestricted Processing state).
    - Report asynchronous event:
      - Sanitize Operation Completed or
      - Sanitize Operation Completed With Unexpected Deallocation (as per Section 8.1.26.1).
    - If EMVS = `1`, transition to Media Verification state.

sections.title: Sanitize_Operation_Restrictions
sections.summary:
# 8.1.26.5 Sanitize Operation Restrictions

## Summary

When a sanitize operation starts (transition into **Restricted Processing** or **Unrestricted Processing**), all controllers in the NVM subsystem must:

- Update the **Sanitize Status log page** (see Section 5.2.12.1.36).
- Suspend autonomous power state management (Section 8.1.18.2).
- Clear all outstanding asynchronous events for **NVM subsystem sanitize**:
  - Sanitize Operation Completed
  - Sanitize Operation Completed With Unexpected Deallocation
  - Sanitize Operation Entered Media Verification State
- Abort non-allowed commands (via **Sanitize In Progress** status), except:
  - Media verification Read commands
- Abort in-progress device self-test operations.
- Release stream identifiers for any open streams.

For **namespace sanitize operations**:
- Abort I/O commands specifying the target namespace NSID (except media verification Read).
- Process Admin commands per Section 5.1.2.
- Abort in-progress device self-tests for the target namespace or NSID `FFFFFFFFh`.
- Release stream identifiers allocated exclusively for the namespace.

---

## While Sanitize Operation in Progress (Restricted Processing, Unrestricted Processing, Media Verification, Post-Verification Deallocation):

### General:
- Flush commands: Process as defined in Section 7.2.
- Firmware activation: Prohibited.
- Persistent Memory Region: Cannot be enabled (setting `PMRCTL.EN` to `1` does not clear `PMRSTS.NRDY`).
- Set Features (CDP): Aborted with **Sanitize In Progress**.

### If Sanitization Target is NVM Subsystem:
- All I/O commands **except Flush** → aborted with **Sanitize In Progress** (unless allowed by Figure 143).
- Any command not permitted in Figure 143 → aborted with **Sanitize In Progress**.

### If Sanitization Target is Namespace:
- In **Media Verification** state: Sanitize Namespace command allowed with access restrictions (Section 8.1.26.3).
- All I/O commands (except Flush) specifying the namespace NSID → aborted with **Sanitize Namespace In Progress** (unless allowed).
- All Admin commands: Process as per Section 5.1.2.

---

## While Sanitize Operation in Failure State (Restricted Failure, Unrestricted Failure):

### General:
- Sanitize command: Allowed with action restrictions (Section 5.2.2).
- For **NVM Subsystem target**:
  - Unauthorized commands → aborted with **Sanitize In Progress**.
  - All I/O commands (except Flush) → aborted with **Sanitize Failed**.
  - Persistent Memory Region: Cannot be enabled (same as above).
- For **Namespace target**:
  - Sanitize and Sanitize Namespace commands: Allowed with access restrictions (Section 8.1.26.3).
  - Other Admin commands: Process as per Section 5.1.2.
  - I/O commands (except Flush) specifying the namespace NSID → aborted with **Sanitize Namespace Failed**.

---

## Management Endpoints
When a sanitize operation starts, all **Management Endpoints** in the NVM subsystem must perform the operation as defined in the **NVM Express Management Interface Specification**.

sections.title: Sanitize_Operation_Effects_on_Exported_NVM_Subsyst
sections.summary:
# 8.1.26.6 Sanitize Operation Effects on Exported NVM Subsystems

### Overview
- **Section ID**: 8.1.26.6 | **Page**: 674-674
- A **sanitize operation** on an **Underlying NVM Subsystem** sanitizes user data in all **Underlying Namespaces** it contains, including those associated with **Exported Namespaces** in any **Exported NVM Subsystem**.
- A **sanitize operation** on an **Exported Namespace** sanitizes all user data in its associated **Underlying Namespace**.

### Conditions Triggering Sanitize Restrictions
If an **Exported NVM Subsystem** or **Exported Namespace** is associated with an **Underlying Namespace** in an **Underlying NVM Subsystem** that is experiencing either:
- A sanitize operation in progress, or  
- A failed sanitize operation with no successful recovery,  

then the **Exported NVM Subsystem** must enforce **sanitize operation restrictions** (as defined in section 8.1.26.5) on I/O commands specifying that Exported Namespace, and may enforce additional restrictions from that section.

sections.title: Submission_Queue_(SQ)_Associations
sections.summary:
# 8.1.27 Submission Queue (SQ) Associations

### Overview
- **Section ID**: 8.1.27 | **Page**: 674-675  
- When **Predictable Latency Mode** is enabled, all I/O commands for namespaces in a given NVM Set have consistent quality of service and predictable latencies (see §8.1.19.1).  
- **SQ Associations** provides hints to the controller about which I/O queues are associated with a given NVM Set, enhancing performance under Predictable Latency Mode.  
- This capability is **optional** and **not required** for Predictable Latency Mode.

### Controller Requirements
If the controller supports SQ Associations, it must indicate support in the **Controller Attributes (CTRATT)** field of the **Identify Controller** data structure for:
- SQ Associations capability
- NVM Sets
- Predictable Latency Mode  
(Refer to Figure 328 for field definitions.)

### Host Operation
The host enables SQ Associations by creating an association between an **NVM Set** and a **Submission Queue** during queue creation (via *Create I/O Submission Queue* command, §5.3.2, or *Connect* command, §6.3).

### Host Requirements for Benefits
To realize SQ Associations benefits, the host must:
- **(a)** Create an association between each Submission Queue and an NVM Set.
- **(b)** Only issue I/O commands to Submission Queues associated with the NVM Set containing the namespace specified in the command.

### Important Note
Failure to follow these rules while SQ Associations is enabled may **impact Predictable Latency** (see §8.1.19.1).

sections.summary:
### 8.1.28 Standard Vendor Specific Command Format

- **Section ID**: 8.1.28 | **Page**: 675-675  
- **Purpose**: Defines a standard format for Vendor Specific commands supported by controllers.  
- **Usage**: Host storage drivers use the **Number of Dwords** fields to prevent physical memory corruption (e.g., buffer overflows).  
- **Support Indication**: Controller supports this format if indicated in the **Identify Controller** data structure (Figure 328), specifically via:  
  - **Admin Vendor Specific Command Configuration** field  
  - **I/O Command Set Vendor Specific Command Configuration** field  
- **Reference**: Figure 82 (command format) and Figure 328 (Identify Controller data structure) provide structural details.

sections.title: Telemetry
sections.summary:
# 8.1.29 Telemetry

### Overview
Telemetry enables manufacturers to collect internal data logs to improve product functionality and reliability. Data is returned via **Telemetry Host-Initiated** or **Telemetry Controller-Initiated** log pages (see sections 5.2.12.1.8 and 5.2.12.1.9). Data is vendor-specific; the feature defines the mechanism for collection. Support is indicated in the **Log Page Attributes (LPA)** field of the Identify Controller data structure.

### Key Design Principles
- A one-to-one mapping of issues to data collections is essential to avoid ambiguity in root cause analysis.
- A **three-phase process** (with optional fourth phase) supports flexible data collection:
  1. **Phase 1 (Small):** Minimal data to identify distinct issues.
  2. **Phase 2 (Medium):** Targeted, more detailed data.
  3. **Phase 3 (Large):** Additional details if prior data is insufficient.
  4. **Phase 4 (Extra-Large):** Only if **DA4S = 1** and **ETDAS = 1h** (Host Behavior Support, section 5.2.26.1.14).

### Telemetry Data Structure
- Each telemetry log consists of **Telemetry Data Blocks**, each **512 bytes**.
- Logs are segmented into:
  - **Three Telemetry Data Areas (small, medium, large)** if **DA4S = 0**.
  - **Four Telemetry Data Areas (small, medium, large, extra-large)** if **DA4S = 1** and **ETDAS = 1h**.
- All areas start at **Telemetry Data Block 1**.
- Each area represents the controller’s internal state at capture time.
- **Data Area 3** (large) must be non-zero length if **Data Area 4** exists.

### Operational Model
1. Host detects telemetry support via **Identify Controller** data structure.
2. Host enables **Extended Telemetry Data Area 4 Supported (ETDAS)** by setting it to `1h` in Host Behavior Support (5.2.26.1.14).
3. Host prepares storage for telemetry data.
4. To receive controller-initiated data, host enables **Telemetry Log Notices** via Asynchronous Event Configuration (5.2.26.1.5).
5. To collect data:
   - Read appropriate Telemetry Data Blocks from the log page in **512-byte units**.
   - Read all supported Telemetry Data Areas (1–4) if available.
   - Set **Retain Asynchronous Event** bit to `1`.
   - Re-read header to ensure **Data Generation Number** matches original (avoid inconsistent data).
   - For controller-initiated log: verify **Telemetry Controller-Initiated Data Available** remains `1h`.
   - After read, clear **Retain Asynchronous Event** to `0` to signal completion.
   - Forward collected data to the controller manufacturer.

### Data Collection Triggers
- **Host-initiated:**
  - Triggered by events like system crash or normal operation.
  - Host submits **Get Log Page** command with **Create Telemetry Host-Initiated Data** bit set to `1`.
  - Controller must complete within **< 1 second**.
  - **NVM subsystem** may use per-controller or shared log pages.
  - Shared logs use **Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Generation Number** to detect changes by other controllers or management endpoints.

- **Controller-initiated:**
  - Triggered by **Asynchronous Event Request** with **Telemetry Log Changed** event.
  - Host can also check **Telemetry Controller-Initiated Data Available** field.
  - Host reads log via **Get Log Page** command.
  - Controller must not modify data during host read.
  - **Only one set of controller-initiated data** exists; controller prioritizes versions.
  - Controller increments **Telemetry Controller-Initiated Data Generation Number** when replacing data.
  - Host must ensure the generation number does not change during read to maintain data consistency.

sections.title: Telemetry_Data_Collection_Examples_(Informative)
sections.summary:
# 8.1.29.1 Telemetry Data Collection Examples (Informative)

This section provides examples of Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Areas. The same concepts apply to Controller-Initiated Data Areas.

- If a Telemetry Host-Initiated log page has no data, the following fields are cleared to `0h`:
  - `Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Area 1 Last Block = 0`
  - `Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Area 2 Last Block = 0`
  - `Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Area 3 Last Block = 0`

- When all three data areas are populated (Figure 714), the values are:
  - `Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Area 1 Last Block = 65`
  - `Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Area 2 Last Block = 1,000`
  - `Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Area 3 Last Block = 30,000`

- Telemetry data is stored in a single set of Telemetry Data Blocks starting at Telemetry Data Block 1:
  - Data in blocks 1–65 of all areas (1, 2, 3) is identical.
  - Data in blocks 66–1,000 of areas 2 and 3 is identical.

- When only the second data area is populated (Figure 715), values are:
  - `Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Area 1 Last Block = 0`
  - `Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Area 2 Last Block = 1,000`
  - `Telemetry Host-Initiated Data Area 3 Last Block = 1,000`

- Telemetry data in blocks 1–1,000 of areas 2 and 3 is identical.

> **Figures**:
> - **Figure 714**: All data areas populated
> - **Figure 715**: Only data area 2 populated

sections.title: Universally_Unique_Identifiers_(UUIDs)_for_Vendor
sections.summary:
# 8.1.30 Universally Unique Identifiers (UUIDs) for Vendor Specific Information

- **Purpose**: Define UUIDs for vendor-specific information in specifications.
- **UUID Format**: 128-bit identifier, typically represented as 32 hexadecimal digits in 5 groups separated by hyphens (e.g., `123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000`).
- **Structure**: UUIDs are structured as:
  - 16 bytes (128 bits) in binary format.
  - Composed of:
    - 1st field: 4 bytes (16 bits) – version and variant.
    - 2nd field: 2 bytes (16 bits) – variant and clock sequence.
    - 3rd field: 2 bytes (16 bits) – clock sequence.
    - 4th field: 2 bytes (16 bits) – node identifier.
    - 5th field: 6 bytes (48 bits) – node identifier.
- **Usage**: Must be used to uniquely identify vendor-specific data elements.
- **Requirements**:
  - UUIDs must be globally unique.
  - Must conform to RFC 4122 standards.
  - Must not be reused across different vendor or specification contexts.
- **Vendor Allocation**:
  - Vendors must use standard UUID generation methods (e.g., UUIDv4 for random generation).
  - Reserved UUID prefixes may be allocated by central authorities (e.g., ISO/IEC 11578).
- **Implementation Guidance**:
  - UUIDs should be generated at the time of data creation.
  - UUIDs must be stored and transmitted in standard hex format (e.g., `urn:uuid:123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000`).
- **Compliance**:
  - Implementation must validate UUID format and uniqueness.
  - Invalid UUIDs (e.g., missing components, incorrect length) are not allowed.

sections.title: UUIDs_for_Vendor_Specific_Information_Introduction
sections.summary:
# 8.1.30.1 UUIDs for Vendor Specific Information Introduction

- **Purpose**: Enables commands to specify vendor-specific information by referencing a UUID that defines the format of the data.
- **Context**: Used in commands (e.g., Set Features, Identify) where fields are vendor-specific or contain data structures with vendor-defined content.
- **Key Mechanism**: 
  - A command specifies a definition via an index into the **UUID List** supported by the controller (refer to §5.2.13.2.14).
  - Each definition of vendor-specific information is associated with a **UUID** defined by the entity (e.g., NVM subsystem vendor or customer).
- **UUID List Management**:
  - The **NVMe Invalid UUID** (refer to §8.1.30.2) replaces a previously valid UUID in the list.
  - Purpose: Maintains static indices in the UUID List, as host access depends on fixed index positions.
- **Interoperability**: NVM subsystem vendors and customers agree on UUID assignments via out-of-band communication (outside this specification).
- **Note**: UUIDs are used to disambiguate vendor-specific data structures when different entities define the same type of information differently.

sections.title: UUIDs_for_Vendor_Specific_Information_Requirements
sections.summary:
# 8.1.30.2 UUIDs for Vendor Specific Information Requirements

- A **UUID list** is a list of non-zero UUID values, terminated by a `0h` UUID. Valid UUIDs are non-zero values excluding the **NVMe Invalid UUID**: `FFFFFFFF_FFFFFFFF_7FFFFFFF_FFFFFFFFh`.
